### Services carries the profit, but the mix moved back to hardware

The fastest-growing pool Apple monetises is Services, but its share of revenue fell in FY2026: $91.7 billion in the first nine months, 25.2% of $364.4 billion and up 14%, at a 76.3% gross margin against 75.4% for FY2025, when Services was $109.2 billion, 26.2% of revenue. Hardware grew faster than Services, so the mix shifted toward premium handsets and China rather than toward the recurring pool — the opposite of what a Services-led thesis needs. The app economy itself has no published size in the sources retrieved: neither Apple nor the platform owners disclose app-store gross billings or mobile-advertising revenue, so Apple's Services line is the measured pool. The installed base is disclosed: Apple put it at more than 2.5 billion active devices on 2026-01-29, up from 2.35 billion a year earlier, which is the stock behind Services and the upgrade pool, but Apple still does not publish a replacement rate, so upgrade timing cannot be sized from public data. [S5, S6, S174, S191]

### Who pays, and how much demand is policy

The budget owner is the consumer, in a discretionary purchase that is increasingly financed. In the United States and United Kingdom interest-free financing is common, so IDC expects the premium end to hold while emerging markets fall more than 20%; in India brands lean on financing after the sub-$100 tier fell 59% and the $600-800 band grew 32%; in China the government subsidy that supported earlier quarters faded in the second quarter of 2026, so demand there is being withdrawn by policy rather than created by it. Policy moves Apple's margin more than a product cycle does: after the February 20, 2026 Supreme Court ruling struck down certain IEEPA tariffs, Apple recognised refunds as a reduction of product cost of sales, and those refunds contributed 2.0 percentage points of the June 2026 quarter's 50.1% gross margin. [S105, S40, S13]

### What would break the premiumisation case

Counter-evidence is fourfold. If memory prices normalise in 2028 as IDC expects, the entry tier rebuilds and Apple's 2026 share gain is contestable again. If China's June-quarter demand was pulled forward ahead of second-half price increases, as IDC's China team reports, the 30% growth line is a launch and currency effect. If courts and the European Commission remove the App Store take rate, the margin layer that offsets hardware cyclicality stops compounding. And the search-distribution payment — $20 billion in 2022, equal to 17% of trailing Services revenue of $120.5 billion and 22% of trailing Services gross profit of $91.6 billion — has not been banned: the September 2, 2025 remedies decision declined to ban distributor payments, and the December 2025 final judgment that restricts distribution is under appeal by Google and the Department of Justice, both pending at 2026-10-29. The investor implication is narrow: in a 1-billion-unit market Apple can grow device revenue only if price rises faster than units fall, making average selling price, China durability and the Services take rate the variables worth monitoring. Sizing confidence is high, because two independent methods agree within 5%; confidence that the mix shift holds to 2028 is medium, because it rests on China and a legally contested commission. Three diligence questions remain open: what share of Services revenue is commission-based rather than subscription, advertising or licensing? How much of the Greater China increase is currency? And what is the current average replacement cycle, measured rather than asserted? [S66, S40, S82, S118, S42, S5]

**Apple's addressable device market fell 16.7% in units in 2026 while growing 6.3% in value, and Apple's revenue grew 16.2% over nine months — the gap is premiumisation and China, not market growth, and Services is not gaining mix (S66, S13, S6).**

IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0 billion units against a market value of $613 billion and an ASP of $581 (S66, S39). Apple's nine-month FY2026 revenue was $364.4 billion, up 16.2%, with Greater China up 30.0% on a $49.9 billion base and Services at 25.2% of revenue against 26.2% in FY2025 (S13, S6). {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## ESG Assessment (esg, revision 3 by Regulatory Analyst, 8,986 characters)
Apple's policy exposure is not a licence-to-operate threat but a slow, legislated tax on Services gross profit: the €500 million DMA fine of 2025-04-23 and the April 2025 US contempt finding show a company that litigates first and complies later, while the three remedies that matter — Google's default-search payment, the US link-out commission and the EU fee structure — have so far been reshaped rather than removed [S7]. The question for a long-only holder is how much Services gross margin five more years of enforcement takes, and whether the multiple already discounts it.

### The DMA fine is small; the cost structure is not

The Commission fined Apple €500 million on 2025-04-23 for breaching the anti-steering obligation and ordered it to remove restrictions on steering users outside the App Store. The same day it closed the user-choice investigation — a real concession — but issued preliminary findings in the Article 6(4) file on Apple's terms for alternative app marketplaces, where an adverse finding carries fines of up to 10% of annual worldwide net sales [S5]. Two facts bound it: on 2026-02-05 the Commission found Apple Ads and Apple Maps should not be designated, and no further Apple decision appears in its DMA record between the fine and 2026-09-28. Peer fines are serial but modest — Meta €200 million in the same package, Google €890 million on 2026-07-23, Alphabet's €4.1 billion Android fine final only in July 2026 — so repeated fines, not break-up, are the base rate. The implication is a transfer of pricing power from Apple's toll to developers and consumers: because each mandated fee cut reaches Services gross margin before it reaches revenue, fee orders should move the multiple and fine headlines should not.

Europe is Apple's second-largest region and Services drove its FY2025 growth; App Store commission is the highest-margin revenue Apple records, so a mandated fee cut in Brussels is worth more to the equity than any fine. Apple also warns that interoperability obligations force it to open technologies to third parties without charge and have in the past, and may in future, caused it not to launch or maintain features "such as Siri AI" — a product-availability risk, not only a revenue leak.

### A contempt finding, then a slow antitrust case

On 2025-04-30 the Northern District of California found Apple in violation of the 2021 Epic injunction, barred any commission on purchases made outside an app, and referred the company to the US Attorney on criminal contempt. The Ninth Circuit modified that on 2025-12-11 to allow parity rules and some commission on link-out purchases; Apple petitioned the Supreme Court on 2026-05-21, obtained certiorari on 2026-06-30 limited to the civil-contempt standard, and seeks a stay below [S6, S122]. Apple's compliance function tested a court order rather than obeyed it, which raises the severity of the next remedy. That remedy is the DOJ case, filed 2024-03-21 with 16 states and the District of Columbia, seeking equitable relief only; it survived dismissal on 2025-06-30 and is in discovery on a schedule pointing to a 2027 trial. With no damages claimed, the risk is conduct-based — defaults, messaging, app distribution — and lands on the 2027-2029 Services line rather than the balance sheet.

### Google's payment survives, on worse terms

The search-distribution remedy went Apple's way on the point that mattered: the 2025-09-02 decision refused to ban Google's payments to distributors, citing harm to device makers and browser developers, and instead barred exclusive contracts while permitting default-placement payments not conditioned on exclusivity and running one year or less [S118, S42]. A final judgment followed in December 2025; both sides appealed in early 2026 and the appeals were pending at 2026-10-29. Apple does not disclose the payment; the $20 billion-a-year figure is unverified. The revenue survives with annual renewal risk and mandatory choice screens.

### Two bear-case triggers did not fire in 2026

The Section 232 semiconductor investigation's initial results on 2026-01-14 imposed no additional tariff on Apple's products, and on 2026-02-20 the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs, with Apple claiming refunds it recognised as a reduction of products cost of sales; Section 301 tariffs were then imposed. In China the opposite of closure happened: the CAC registered Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15 with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, and Greater China net sales rose 22% to $18,816 million in the June 2026 quarter and 30% to $64,839 million for the nine months, from $49,884 million [S6, S121]. The binding constraint is the calendar: the Busan truce that suppresses tariff and rare-earth escalation was extended on 2026-09-23 from 2026-11-10 to 2027-01-10, making 2027 the next policy cliff.

### Tax is settled; the ESG tail is elsewhere

The Irish state-aid case ended against Apple: the ECJ confirmed the 2016 decision on 2024-09-10, producing a $10.2 billion net one-time charge and $15.8 billion payable to Ireland. The FY2025 effective tax rate of 15.6%, against 24.1% in FY2024, now sits just above the OECD Pillar Two 15% floor, so incremental Pillar Two cost is small and the live tax risk is the $23.2 billion of gross unrecognised benefits, $10.6 billion of which would move the rate if recognised [S5].

On environmental and social issues the record is stronger than the sector's: full third-party audit coverage of identified 3TG smelters for a tenth consecutive year, no finding of armed-group financing, a June 2024 instruction to suppliers to stop sourcing 3TG from the DRC and Rwanda, and recycled-content commitments for cobalt, tin, gold and rare earths. Those claims are company-prepared and unverified here, and the carbon-neutral-2030 target and its Scope 3 progress could not be checked against a published source; that gap is stated, not filled. Governance offsets the conduct record: one class of common stock, an independent Chair separated from the CEO, and an Audit Committee that owns privacy, cybersecurity, tax and enterprise risk. Control is not the issue; compliance culture is.

They support a judgement that policy is a recurring cost to Services gross margin, not a threat to the franchise. Three questions decide the watchlist price: what fee Apple now charges on US link-out purchases after the December 2025 remand and how much spending has moved off in-app purchase; what Apple actually receives from Google at the first one-year renewal; and whether Article 6(4) produces a second EU fine before the General Court rules. None is a reason to avoid Apple; each is a reason to demand a price that assumes some of the loss.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 6 by Market Analyst, 8,984 characters)
Apple's competitive position strengthened in 2026 in every hardware line except smartwatches, but the gain is crisis-specific — bought with memory supply and price discipline rather than product superiority — and it is being offset where profit is made, because the App Store commission that funds the premium position is being dismantled by courts and regulators rather than by a rival's product. Apple leads no hardware category outright except detachable tablets, and its annual report concedes minority share in smartphones, PCs, tablets and wearables. Head to head, Samsung shipped 62.7 million handsets in Q2 2026 versus Apple's 55.7 million. [S102]

### The lead is in integration, not in units

Apple's 20.2% of global smartphone shipments in Q2 2026 was a record for that quarter and a 3.9 percentage point gain, but Samsung's 22.7% was larger and Xiaomi's 26.4% collapse explains much of the redistribution. In personal computing Apple is second at 18.2% to Lenovo's 20.1%, yet macOS shipments grew 17.4% while Windows fell 6.7% and Android 19.6%, and macOS is the only major operating system IDC expects to grow in 2026. The clearest structural lead is detachable tablets at 55.3%; the weakest spot is smartwatches, where Huawei leads 18.8% to 17.2%, so Apple's 15.5% of all wearables rests on earwear, where it holds 17.2%. [S104]

| Product | Competitor | Competitor share, Q2 2026 | Apple share | Technology basis | Price position | Switching cost | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone, global | Samsung | 22.7%, +3.2pp | 20.2%, +3.9pp | iOS integration and secured memory supply | Industry ASP $581; Apple above it | High: iCloud, iMessage, purchased apps | S102, S66 |
| iPhone, China | Huawei | 22.6%, +4.5pp | 18.1%, +4.2pp | iOS against domestic HarmonyOS | Apple held prices while Android raised them | Medium: leaving iOS loses Apple services | S40 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo | 20.1%, +2.5pp | 18.2%, -0.4% | macOS against Windows | MacBook Neo attacks entry pricing | Medium | S103, S106 |
| Services and App Store | Alphabet, Google Play | $471.1bn TTM revenue | $91.7bn Services, 76.3% margin (9M FY2026) | iOS distribution against Google Play | 15-30% commission, under challenge | High for consumers, falling for developers | S5, S42, S80 |

### Samsung is the dangerous one, and the reason is memory

Samsung is the most dangerous competitor, and not because of the Galaxy S26 Ultra. When memory is more than 65% of bill of materials at the low end, the binding constraint is supply access, and Samsung is the only top-five handset vendor that also sells memory: it grew shipments 8.1% and took 3.2 points of share in Q2 2026 while Xiaomi fell 26.4% and vivo 19.6%. Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise Apple now attacks: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, below the $2,550 average price IDC assumes, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027 and 40% of a category growing 12.6% to 22.9 million units this year. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs, leaning on HarmonyOS, which IDC expects to reach 51 million units in 2026; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%, so both premium ends expanded while OPPO, vivo and Xiaomi contracted. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. HarmonyOS draws on the national preference that makes Apple's China revenue politically exposed, so the 30% China revenue growth belongs behind a competition risk; Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap in the one market where it mattered most but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses that it is subject to a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain purchases consumers make, that its Digital Markets Act compliance plan has been challenged by the European Commission, and that it faces U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by U.S. courts and European regulators. [S5]

| Product | Leader | Challenger | Niche | Emerging threat | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | Samsung, 22.7% of units | Apple, 20.2% and gaining | Huawei in China, 22.6% | HarmonyOS at 51m units; AI-first Android flagships | S102, S40, S66 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo, 20.1% | Apple, 18.2%, with the only growing OS | Dell in workstations, 40.0% | HarmonyOS NEXT at 1.6%; Windows-on-ARM | S103, S106 |
| Services | Apple, $91.7bn (9M) | Alphabet through Google Play | Netflix, Spotify, Epic | Web payments and alternative marketplaces | S5, S42, S80 |

### AI and the phone already in the buyer's pocket

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: the all-new Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google under their 2026-01-12 agreement — its assistant now depends on a company it also competes with in services. Samsung's AI-equipped Galaxy S26 Ultra is credited by IDC with returning Samsung to first place in Q1 2026, and research and development rose 32.5% to $34.0 billion in nine months of FY2026 — the cost of catching up, not the reward for leading. The strongest competitor is the handset already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening, IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, and the 173 million sub-$100 units shipped in 2025 are leaving the market, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Three risks follow: if AI becomes the reason a buyer upgrades, Apple competes on integration, with a rented model; if HarmonyOS reaches first-time buyers in lower-tier cities, they never enter iOS; and if the U.S. injunction spreads to other storefronts, the take rate falls further. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares and legal facts, medium beyond 2028, when memory normalises and the crisis-specific advantage lapses. Open diligence: what proportion of Services revenue is commission rather than subscription? What margin does the foldable carry at $1,999? What does the Gemini licence cost per query at scale? [S13, S66, S40]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business Model (business_model, revision 3 by Fundamentals Analyst, 8,460 characters)
Apple runs a hardware annuity with a services margin layered on top — 73 cents of services gross profit for every dollar of product gross profit — but the mix shift the multiple pays for stalled in fiscal 2026, when hardware margins, helped by tariff refunds, grew gross profit faster than Services. Apple sells through two routes, and the split is the least-discussed fact in the model: in fiscal 2025, 40% of net sales went through its own stores, online store and direct sales force and 60% through carriers, resellers and distributors. The carrier finances or subsidises the handset to win a contract, so the carrier bears the acquisition cost and Apple's selling expense stays at $27,601M, or 6.6% of revenue. There is little contracted backlog: deferred revenue was $13.7bn at 2025-09-27, 3.3% of revenue, two thirds of it recognised within a year. Apple is a repeat-purchase business recognised as it bills, not a subscription business with a book of contracted revenue [S5].

### The mix shift, and its reversal

The arithmetic of the mix shift is the strongest part of the case. In fiscal 2025 Services produced $109,158M of revenue at a 75.4% gross margin against $307,003M of Products at 36.8%: 26.2% of revenue but 42.2% of gross profit ($82,314M of $195,201M), up from 35.7% two years earlier, with services gross profit per dollar of product gross profit rising from $0.55 in fiscal 2023 to $0.73. Then the mechanism ran backwards. In the nine months to 2026-06-27 product gross profit rose 26.3% to $108,819M while services gross profit rose 15.3% to $69,963M, and Services fell to 39.1% of gross profit; product gross margin reached 39.9% against 36.9% a year earlier, taking total gross margin to 49.1% and to 50.1% in the June quarter against 46.5%. Apple attributes the gain to "a different mix of products and tariff refunds, partially offset by higher costs, including memory", the most consequential disclosure in this section: it makes fiscal 2026's margin hardware-led and partly a refund rather than a trading gain [S5, S6].

### Unit economics per revenue dollar, because there are no units

Apple discloses no unit volumes, average selling price or installed-base figure, so a per-device waterfall cannot be built from primary evidence. The economics of each revenue dollar can be.

| Unit-economics line | FY2025 | 9M FY2026 | Evidence and status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Product cost of sales, per $1,000 of product revenue | $632 | $601 | Bill of materials, assembly and warranty provision combined, not split | S5, S6 |
| Product gross profit | $368 | $399 | 36.8% to 39.9%; includes tariff refunds in fiscal 2026 | S5, S6 |
| Services cost of sales, per $1,000 of services revenue | $246 | $237 | Content, hosting and payment processing | S5, S6 |
| Services gross profit | $754 | $763 | 75.4% to 76.3% | S5, S6 |
| Services gross profit per $1 of product gross profit | $0.73 | $0.64 | Closest disclosed proxy for lifetime value against acquisition cost | S5, S6 |
| Customer acquisition cost, support and warranty | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Carriers bear acquisition; warranty sits inside cost of sales | S5 |
| LTV, LTV:CAC, CAC payback in months | Not computable | Not computable | Requires units, ASP and installed base, none of which Apple reports | S5 |

Apple therefore has no payback period to wait out: a device is gross-profit-positive on delivery at a 36.8% product margin, and the services stream that follows is nearly all incremental, since services cost of sales is $26,844M on $109,158M of revenue. The nearest disclosed proxy for lifetime value against acquisition cost is the $0.73 of services gross profit per dollar of product gross profit, and its fall to $0.64 is the number to watch — the annuity still grows, but no longer faster than the hardware that creates it [S5, S6].

### Pricing power shows up as mix, not as price

| Line | FY2025 net sales | Year on year | What the filing discloses about price and mix | Gross margin | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | $209,586M | +4% | Growth "due to higher net sales of Pro models", i.e. mix rather than units | 36.8% products blended | S5 |
| Services | $109,158M | +14% | "advertising, the App Store and cloud services" | 75.4% | S5 |
| Mac | $33,708M | +12% | "laptops and desktops" | 36.8% products blended | S5 |
| iPad and Wearables | $63,709M | 0% | iPad Air and mini higher, Accessories and Wearables lower | 36.8% products blended | S5 |

Pricing power shows up as mix: iPhone revenue rose 22% to $196,515M in the nine months to 2026-06-27, attributed again to higher sales of Pro models rather than to units. The same disclosure prevents separating price from volume, and therefore prevents estimating elasticity — a 22% increase could be volume, price, or any combination. Apple publishes list prices on its own store but not in its filings, and this report did not retrieve a verified 2026 price list, so the table uses disclosed mix effects rather than price points; third-party unit data would settle it [S6].

### The highest-margin layer is also the most litigated

App Store economics are recognised net — Apple books "only the commission it retains" on third-party app sales — so a take-rate cut passes straight to revenue and gross profit with no offsetting cost. Apple is subject to a US court order barring it from charging a commission on certain consumer purchases, though the Ninth Circuit has instructed the district court to amend the injunction to permit one, and in the EU the Digital Markets Act forces alternative distribution, alternative payment processing and new fee structures, a plan the European Commission has challenged. A second concentration sits in the same line: Apple earns licensing revenue from Google for search distribution inside Services advertising, which Apple names as a primary driver of Services growth in both fiscal 2025 and the first nine months of fiscal 2026. The payment was $20bn in 2022 per unsealed court documents, 18.3% of fiscal 2025 Services revenue, and Apple does not disclose the current figure; the District of Columbia court order of 2025-09-02 preserved the ability to pay partners while banning exclusive agreements, but Apple states a reversal on appeal could impose remedies "prohibiting Google from offering the Company commercial terms for search distribution", and both the Department of Justice and Google appealed [S6, S82].

### Cost structure, and what would break the durability

The cost base is bought, not built: product cost of sales of $194,116M goes to TSMC for wafers, to memory suppliers for DRAM and NAND, and to Foxconn and its peers for assembly. Research and development reached $34,035M in the nine months to 2026-06-27, up 33% and 9.3% of revenue against 8.3% in fiscal 2025, on "infrastructure-related costs, including investments in artificial intelligence"; capital expenditure is 2.2% of trailing-twelve-month revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft in fiscal 2026. Apple rents its manufacturing and buys much of its AI capability through the income statement, so that bill reaches the operating margin immediately rather than through depreciation. For investors the implication is that the annuity is intact, but the margin expansion of the last four quarters is not the mix shift it is commonly described as: it is product mix, a tariff refund and memory cost timing, on top of a services base whose most profitable components face an appeal, a court order and a European regulatory process. The downside is quantifiable rather than hypothetical: giving back three points of gross margin and losing the search licence together would take more than a fifth of trailing-twelve-month net income. Three facts would settle the durability question and none is disclosed — the current size of the search payment, the share of Services that is App Store commission, and the refund-versus-mix split; the fiscal 2026 annual report, not on EDGAR as of 2026-10-31, may settle them [S6, S27].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Development Strategy (strategy, revision 5 by Product Analyst, 8,085 characters)
Apple's route to FY2028 growth is services mix, a richer iPhone cycle and India, with artificial intelligence as a retention feature and a possible iCloud+ upsell rather than a revenue line of its own; the plan is credible on cash generation and per-share compounding, but not yet on AI monetisation or on creating a new product category. The base is large and still growing: revenue reached $416.2bn in FY2025, and the nine months to 2026-06-27 produced $364.4bn, up 16%, with Services at $91.7bn, up 14% [S77, S6].

### Services carry the margin, but the mix engine stalled in FY2026

Services were 26% of FY2025 revenue but 39% of gross profit in the nine months to June 2026, because they earn a 76.3% gross margin against 39.9% for products. The mix engine, however, stopped being the marginal driver: product gross profit grew 26% against 15% for services, so the rise in total gross margin to 49.1% from 46.8% came from hardware mix and tariff refunds, not from services, while memory costs kept rising. Services growth itself came from advertising and cloud services, with the Google search-distribution payment named as a primary driver. That is the engine that funds the buyback and the silicon, and it is also the engine regulators are targeting: the European Commission fined Apple €500m on 2025-04-23 for anti-steering non-compliance, and the General Court dismissed Apple's challenge to its gatekeeper designation on 2026-07-08 [S85, S84, S6]. An investor should value the services annuity on gross profit that compounds in the low-to-mid teens, and apply a discount for the probability that a remedy compresses commission or search income rather than a one-off fine.

### AI is funded as cost and monetised, if at all, through storage

Apple introduced Siri AI with the iOS 27 cycle announced in the third quarter of FY2026, and R&D rose 33% to $34.0bn in the nine months to June 2026, driven by infrastructure including AI investments and headcount. No AI revenue line exists. Availability is a regulatory variable too: China cleared Apple Intelligence only on 2026-07-15, with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, and the 10-Q warns that DMA rules have in the past, and may in future, cause it not to launch features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions. The reported plan — that high-frequency, compute-intensive Siri use will be gated behind iCloud+ — is plausible because it reuses a price ladder already in place, but Apple has published no tier and no price, so it is unverified [S13, S6, S107, S171]. The mechanism matters more than the price: AI raises the cost of serving every device while its clearest commercial effect is to protect upgrade rates and services attach. If Apple charges, the increment is bounded by storage-subscription willingness to pay, not by the value of the model; if it does not, AI is a permanent tax on gross margin. Either way, 2027 is the test of whether AI spend converts into units or ARPU.

### India lowers tariff risk, not unit cost

iPhone production in India rose 53% in 2025 to ~55 million units, ~25% of global output, and is projected at 28% in 2026; Tata Electronics overtook Foxconn in iPhone export assembly over the FY2022-FY2026 incentive period. The strategy is rational given the tariff record in the filings — Section 232 semiconductor investigation results in January 2026, the Supreme Court striking down certain IEEPA tariffs in February 2026, and new Section 301 tariffs, with manufacturing purchase obligations of $57.0bn at 2026-06-27 [S89, S91, S6]. The limit is that assembly captures little of the value: components, displays and silicon still come from East Asia, so India is an insurance policy on tariffs and single-country concentration, not a margin lever. The signpost to watch is the share of US-bound iPhones assembled in India, which Apple has never disclosed.

### Capital allocation is disciplined and slightly bolder

R&D rose from $29.9bn in FY2023 to $34.6bn in FY2025 and is running at ~$45bn annualised in FY2026. Buybacks remain the primary use of cash: $25.8bn of stock was repurchased in the quarter to 2026-06-27 alone, alongside $4.0bn of dividends at $0.27 per share, which cut the share count to 14.61bn from 14.77bn at FY2025 year-end and helped EPS grow 29% against 27% net-income growth. M&A posture has shifted from tuck-ins: Apple confirmed the acquisition of the AI-audio start-up Q.ai on 2026-01-29, reported by the Financial Times at close to $2bn, and acquired the AI data-engineering company Ascend.io, notified to the European Commission on 2026-06-30; intangible assets rose from $11.1bn to $20.3bn between 2025-09-27 and 2026-06-27 [S77, S88, S6, S13]. Against ~$146bn of cash and marketable securities, that is affordable experimentation rather than a change of strategy — and it is the right test of whether Apple's AI gap can be bought in pieces.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2026 results and 10-K | by 2026-11 | Pending | Whether 16% growth holds into the holiday quarter | S77, S6 |
| Siri AI full release (iOS 27) | 2026-09 | Launched at WWDC26; EU availability not assured | Gemini-based assistant ships on schedule | S13, S86, S6 |
| iPhone Duo ramp | 2026-10-23 on sale | Launched | Apple can create a $1,999 tier | S59 |
| AI subscription (iCloud+ gating) | Not announced | Reported only | AI becomes revenue rather than cost | S107 |

| Foxconn | China and India assembly | Ongoing | Active | S89 |

### What must be true in twelve months, and the case against

Four things must happen for the strategy to be credible. First, the FY2026 holiday quarter has to show that the iPhone 18 and Duo cycle sustains double-digit growth without tariff refunds, which flattered the June quarter by ~2 percentage points of gross margin. Second, Apple must put a price on AI or show that it lifts upgrade rates, because a 33% R&D increase with no revenue attached is a margin problem. Third, a DOJ settlement or DMA remedy must leave the App Store commission and default-search payment substantially intact; both cases attack the services profit pool directly. Fourth, India must reach the projected share of output without a quality or logistics incident. The counter-case is strong and largely Apple's own record: AI features arrived well after they were demonstrated, Siri needed a Google licence, the car programme was cancelled, and Vision Pro shipped ~45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, while Alphabet, Microsoft and Huawei set a faster cadence in models, cloud AI and, for Huawei, folding hardware and domestic silicon. Apple's answer is that it does not need to be first — it needs to be best integrated, and it monetises the installed base rather than the model. That is a defensible strategy for a cash-flow investor and a weak one for anyone buying AI optionality [S59, S87, S84, S90, S89].

::: evidence
**The strategy is credible as a cash-compounding plan and unproven as a growth plan.**

Services earn a structurally higher gross margin than hardware, and buybacks are large enough that earnings per share can compound faster than net income even with flat hardware; but AI is a large R&D increase with no disclosed price, Vision Pro has not become a platform, and the two antitrust cases target precisely the services lines that fund the plan.

rows.belief: Apple's integration lead is durable in silicon and distribution (8/10) and thin in AI (4/10): the A20 Pro is on TSMC N2 and the C2 modem reached the flagship, but the next foundation models are licensed from Google.
rows.evidence: A20 Pro on TSMC N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine; C2 in the iPhone 18 line [S64, S59]; Gemini-based Apple Foundation Models announced 2026-01-12 [S58]; services gross margin 76.3% [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Siri needed a Google licence, Vision Pro shipped about 45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, and DMA rules may withhold Siri AI in the EU [S6, S87, S86].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A disclosed in-house frontier model, or AI features producing a measurable lift in upgrade rates rather than cost.

rows.belief: 2026 is a supply-shock year that flatters Apple's unit share and price; the honest test of the franchise is 2028, when memory normalises and the premium tier rebuilds.
rows.evidence: DRAM and NAND up more than 300% year on year; 2026 market value $613bn, +6.3%, on units down 16.7% [S66, S39]; IDC sees memory normalising around 2028 [S39].
rows.counter_evidence: Apple's 20.2% unit share gain was bought with early memory supply that lapses, while Samsung both competes in handsets and sells the memory [S102, S66].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: Memory prices normalising earlier than 2028, or Apple holding share after they do.

rows.belief: Distribution is the moat: 60% of sales run through carriers and resellers that finance the device, keeping selling expense at 6.6% of revenue, and India assembly is scaling as a tariff hedge.
rows.evidence: 40% direct and 60% indirect in FY2025 [S5]; iPhone output in India about 55m units, 25% of global, projected 28% in 2026 [S91]; selling, general and administrative $27.6bn, 6.6% of revenue [S5].

rows.change: A channel disruption at a major carrier, or India failing to reach the projected share of output without a quality incident.

rows.belief: A device is gross-profit-positive on delivery at a 39.9% product margin and the services stream is nearly all incremental, but the annuity no longer grows faster than the hardware that creates it and the margin is turning.
rows.evidence: Products 39.9% and Services 76.3% gross margin in nine months of FY2026 [S6]; services gross profit per dollar of product gross profit fell to $0.64 from $0.73 [S5, S6]; September-quarter guide of 47-48% including 1 point of refunds [S199].
rows.counter_evidence: Part of the product margin is a tariff refund (2.0 points of the June quarter) and memory costs are rising [S6].

rows.change: Services gross profit growing faster than product gross profit for two quarters, or the mix ratio recovering above $0.73.

rows.belief: Succession is done and internal, which lowers cultural risk, but the new CEO has never run a P&L and the AI transition sits with a software chief who outsourced the frontier model.

rows.counter_evidence: Apple's 36.8x price-to-free-cash-flow is 43% below the peer median of 64.6x because capex is only $10.0bn a year [S9, S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A durable step-up in free cash flow that closes the reverse-DCF gap, or a de-rating toward 25-30x forward.

rows.belief: There is no takeover or listing event: exit is an open-market sale, so the sell discipline is a set of price bands and thesis breaks rather than a liquidity question.
rows.evidence: Largest technology deal on record equals 1.4% of Apple's market value [S169]; average daily traded value $13.84bn [S9]; ten-year average intra-year drawdown 21.4% [S163].
rows.counter_evidence: A 30x-plus multiple may never offer a margin of safety again, so a strict band risks never owning the asset [S163].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A structural change in the shareholder base or capital return that changes the multiple floor.

rows.belief: Today's price is about 22% above base fair value once the guided margin give-back is carried through: the reverse DCF needs 11.8% free-cash-flow growth for a decade against 1.5% delivered in FY2021-FY2025.

rows.belief: Headline growth overstates the business: FY2025's 22.7% EPS growth is 10.4% once the Irish charge is normalised, 2.0 points of the June 2026 gross margin were tariff refunds, and the company has guided another point for September.

rows.counter_evidence: Cash conversion is strong at 1.06x net income and the refund is a one-time cash item, not an accounting invention [S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: The FY2026 10-K decomposing refund and mix, and confirming inventory is a launch build rather than unsold stock.

rows.belief: Cash generation is the strongest part of the record and the least dependent on accounting judgement: $136.7bn trailing free cash flow on $10.0bn of capex.
rows.evidence: Operating cash flow $146.7bn against capex $10.0bn, 1.06x net income, in the twelve months to 2026-06-27 [S6]; capex 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft [S6, S27].
rows.counter_evidence: FY2025 conversion fell to 0.88x on $43.4bn of cash taxes, and the trailing figure benefits from a working-capital swing that is reversing as inventory builds [S5, S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Cash taxes or inventory returning conversion below 0.95x for a full year.

rows.belief: There is no solvency risk: $62.2bn of net cash, commercial paper cut to $2.0bn, and debt maturities that do not test the business.
rows.evidence: $146.5bn of cash and securities against $84.3bn of debt at 2026-06-27 [S6]; net cash up from $33.8bn at FY2025 year-end [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: The $57.0bn of manufacturing purchase obligations fix component costs just as memory prices peak [S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A debt-funded acquisition of scale, or purchase obligations rising faster than revenue.

rows.belief: The next twelve months carry five dated tests: FY2026 results and annual report on 2026-11-02, argument in the Google remedies appeal from 2026-12-09, the DOJ case schedule into 2027, the Busan truce expiry on 2027-01-10 and the first one-year renewal of the search payment.

rows.confidence: high

rows.change: A December guide that restores gross margin above 48% ex-refund would raise the base toward $296 and the starter band toward $270.

arguments.markdown:
Apple at $344.63 is a great business at a price that assumes its best margin year is permanent. The need is real: more than 2.5bn active devices, a record 23.6% of 2026 smartphone shipments and a quarter of revenue from Services. The capability is defensible in silicon and distribution but rented at the frontier: the A20 Pro sits on TSMC's N2 process while the next Apple Foundation Models are licensed from Google. The economics scale: $466.8bn of trailing revenue and $136.7bn of free cash flow, with capital expenditure at 2.2% of sales. The question is not whether the franchise is good; it is whether the price pays for a margin the company has already guided away. It does not. On a margin-adjusted base the shares are worth $268, 22% below the close, and the probability-weighted value of the three cases is about $275. Apple belongs on the watchlist, not in the portfolio, until the earnings base is proven or the price falls to $240-265. [S199]

The demand side is replacement, not discovery. Global smartphone units fall 16.7% to about 1.0bn in 2026 while market value rises 6.3% to $613bn, and Apple's nine-month revenue grew 16.2% because it sold more expensive devices and took share from a collapsing Android entry tier, not because more people entered the category. Greater China contributed 4.1 points of that growth with revenue up 30.0%, and the installed base of more than 2.5bn devices is the stock that Services and the upgrade pool sit on. The capability that protects this annuity is real: custom silicon, an operating system that no rival can license, a 76.3% services gross margin, and a carrier channel that carries 60% of sales and keeps selling expense at 6.6% of revenue. What it does not protect is the next interface. Apple licenses the frontier model, Siri arrived with a Google-built brain, Vision Pro shipped about 45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, and the rebuilt assistant may not launch in the European Union because of interoperability rules. The moat defends the cash flow; it no longer guarantees the growth. [S191, S66]

The economics are turning at exactly the line the multiple capitalises. Services produced $91.7bn in nine months, 25.2% of revenue and 39.1% of gross profit at a 76.3% margin, but product gross profit grew 26.3% against 15.3% for Services, so the mix shift the premium multiple is meant to pay for ran backwards in fiscal 2026. The reported margin is also not a clean trading number: 50.1% in the June quarter included 2.0 points of tariff refunds, the nine-month figure of 49.1% included about one point, and Apple guided the September quarter at 47-48% including a further point of refunds — 46-47% underlying against 48.1% in June ex-refund, which the chief financial officer attributed to memory costs. Component prices are the transfer mechanism: DRAM and NAND are up more than 300% while Samsung, a handset competitor, sells the memory. Two points of give-back on roughly $490bn of FY2027 revenue is $9.8bn of pretax profit, 6.3% of trailing net income, leaving EPS near $8.87 rather than the $9.79 consensus. Jefferies' $263.66 target of 2026-08-10 is within 2% of that arithmetic. [S201]

Consensus is not wrong about the franchise; it is wrong about the price of it. The average analyst target is $339.35, below the $344.63 close, and the stock trades at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x consensus forward earnings against a 21.0x mega-cap peer median and 21.76x for the S&P 500. It is 88% above peers and 1.8 times the index. The five-year average multiple is 30.2x and the ten-year mean 25.35x; today sits at the 100th percentile of the five-year range. On a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, the buyer accepts 2.2 points less cash yield than the risk-free asset, and the reverse discounted cash flow needs 11.8% free-cash-flow growth for a decade against 1.5% compounded in fiscal 2021-2025. Our difference from consensus is narrow in direction and large in consequence: we are below on FY2027 EPS ($8.87 against $9.79) and on the multiple the stock deserves (30.2x against the 35.2x it carries). [S9, S154]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 20% | Memory pass-through holds gross margin near 48% through iPhone 18 and Duo pricing, the AI cycle lifts upgrades, Services reaccelerates above 15%, and the Google payment renews near current terms | FY2027 EPS about $10.50 at 38x gives $399, +16%, plus a 0.3% dividend | December guide at or above 48% ex-refund; Duo sell-through; Services above 15% | S199, S6, S59 |
| Base | 50% | The refund rolls off, memory takes two points of margin, FY2027 EPS lands near $8.87 rather than $9.79, Services compounds in the low teens, and the multiple sits at its five-year average | $8.87 at 30.2x gives $268, -22%, with a 0.3% dividend | December guide 46-47% ex-refund; consensus EPS cuts; multiple toward 30x | S199, S201, S154 |
| Bear | 30% | Margin slides toward 45% and a US or EU remedy cuts commission or the search payment is repriced at its one-year renewal or on appeal; the multiple compresses to 25x | $8.20 at 25x gives $205, -41%; with the search licence lost, $7.11 at 25x gives $178, -48% | D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09; gross margin below 45%; China revenue down 20% | S6, S118, S42 |
:::

The asymmetry runs against the buyer. The bull case pays 16% before dividends and requires the margin question to be answered in Apple's favour; the base case loses 22% even though the franchise performs; the bear case loses 41%. Weighting the cases 20/50/30 gives an expected value of about $275, a 20% negative return from the close, which is why the position is zero rather than small. The bull case is not a fantasy — Apple has beaten estimates through the memory squeeze and raised iPad and Mac prices without visible demand destruction — but it is the minority case because the company's own September guide already carries the give-back the consensus EPS denies. The dates that decide the weights are 2026-11-02, when the December-quarter guide is the first outlook without the carry-in inventory cushion; 2026-12-09, when the D.C. Circuit is asked to hear the Google remedies appeal; and 2027-01-10, when the Busan trade truce expires.

| Rank | Assumption | Confidence | What would disprove it | Impact if wrong | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gross margin settles at 46-47% in FY2027 once the refund and inventory cushion normalise, not at the 48-49% consensus implies | Medium | Two quarters at or above 48% ex-refund, or a December guide at or above 48% | Two points is $9.8bn pretax, 6.3% of net income; EPS $8.87 and base value $268, 22% below the close | December guide below 46% ex-refund; DRAM sufficiency negative through 2027; inventory +87% year on year | S199, S194, S6 |
| 2 | The Google search payment survives at or near its reported ~$20bn a year, repriced annually and non-exclusive | Medium | An appellate ban on distributor payments, or a renewal at a materially lower rate | About $20bn a year, 17% of Services revenue and 22% of services gross profit; at 30x, $474bn or 9.4% of market value | D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09; first renewal terms; FY2026 10-K disclosure | S6, S82, S118, S42 |
| 3 | Services compound in the low-to-mid teens without a mandated take-rate collapse | Medium | Two quarters below 5% growth, or a remedy stripping commission on a material share of transactions | A three-point growth cut removes about $3.6bn of revenue and 2.8% of net income at a 76% margin | EU Article 6(4) proceedings; US link-out migration; Services growth of 14.1% decelerating | S6, S5, S122 |
| 4 | The iPhone 18 and Duo cycle sustains high-single-digit revenue growth in FY2027 without refunds | Medium | A holiday quarter below the guided 9-11%, or a Duo ramp that cannibalises Pro volumes without adding revenue | Each point of revenue growth is 1.5% of net income | 2026-11-02 results; first full Duo quarter; China units down about 20% in H2 2026 | S1, S199, S195 |
| 5 | The buyback continues at roughly the current pace, so EPS compounds faster than net income | High | A pause or cut in repurchases at 39.5x, or a large debt-funded acquisition | Buybacks added 1.9 points of EPS growth in the trailing twelve months and 1.6% of shareholder yield | Repurchases $62.1bn against $70.6bn in nine months; $100bn authorisation of 2026-04 | S6, S164 |
:::

Three transfers sit outside the operating story and each lands on the same high-margin layer. The reported $20bn search payment is 22% of services gross profit, and the D.D.C. remedies decision of 2025-09-02 preserved it only on non-exclusive, one-year-or-shorter terms, with Google's appeal and the government's cross-appeal pending and argument sought from 2026-12-09. The EU's Digital Markets Act produced a €500m fine on 2025-04-23 and an open Article 6(4) file, and the US Department of Justice case is in discovery toward a 2027 trial. China is the third: revenue rose 30% in nine months, but Huawei holds 22.6% of units with HarmonyOS and price discipline, and IDC expects China shipments to fall about 20% in the second half of 2026, so the region that supplied the most growth enters FY2027 against the hardest comparison. Capital allocation does not cushion any of this: $62.1bn of stock was repurchased in nine months at a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.93% Treasury, which supports EPS more than value per share. [S118, S6]

Two analogs bound the decision. Microsoft after 2014 is the best case: a legacy incumbent whose cloud transition replaced a declining licence business and whose market value rose from about $381bn to about $3tn in a decade. The lesson is not that transformation works; it is that Microsoft began near 10-12x earnings, so re-rating supplied much of the return. Apple starts at 39.5x, where the same transformation would have to come from earnings alone. Nokia is the cautionary case: 40-50% of global handsets in 2007, under 5% by 2013, because the platform shift moved value to software it did not control. Apple owns its platform and rents the frontier model, which places it closer to Microsoft's early cloud years than to Nokia's collapse; the difference is the price of admission. [S198, S200]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft cloud transition under Nadella | Best | 2014-2024 | An incumbent can re-rate through a platform shift, but much of Microsoft's return came from starting near 10-12x earnings; at 39.5x Apple must earn its return | S198 |
| Nokia mobile phones | Cautionary | 2007-2013 | Device leadership did not survive a shift in the value layer to software the incumbent did not control; share peaked near 50% and fell under 5% in six years | S200 |
:::

The decision tree is therefore explicit. Invest now: no, because the expected value is below the price and the margin question is unresolved. Pass: no, because the franchise, the balance sheet and the cash conversion are the best in the peer set and the AI risk is a cost, not an existential break. Wait for a milestone: yes, with 2026-11-02 as the first proof point. Invest with conditions: at $240-265 for a 1-2% starter and at or below $225 for a 3-4% position, capped at 4% because a single regulatory event is worth about 9.4% of market value. Above $395 the stock is a trim, not an add. Confidence is high in the arithmetic and the multiples, medium in the FY2027 margin path because Apple's pricing response to memory costs is undisclosed, and low in any forecast of the AI revenue line, which does not yet exist. The one diligence question that would change the decision is what the December-quarter guide implies for gross margin ex-refund; a print at or above 48% moves the base toward $296 and the starter band toward $270, while a print near 45% moves the base to the bear case.

Greater China supplied 4.1 points of that growth with revenue up 30.0%. The moat is real: the A20 Pro on TSMC N2, a 76.3% services gross margin, 60% of sales through carriers and selling expense at 6.6% of revenue. It protects the annuity, not the growth. Siri runs on a Google-built model, Vision Pro shipped about 45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, and interoperability rules may keep the rebuilt assistant out of the European Union. [S191, S66]

The economics turn at the line the multiple capitalises. Services produced 39.1% of gross profit in nine months, down from 42.2% in FY2025, because product gross profit grew 26.3% against 15.3%. Two points on roughly $490bn of FY2027 revenue is $9.8bn of pretax profit, 6.3% of trailing net income, leaving EPS near $8.87 rather than the $9.79 consensus. Jefferies' $263.66 target of 2026-08-10 is within 2% of that arithmetic. [S201]

Consensus is right about the franchise and wrong about the price. The average target is $339.35, below the close. The stock trades at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 21.0x mega-cap peer median and 21.76x for the S&P 500 — 88% above peers and 1.8 times the index, at the 100th percentile of a five-year range whose average is 30.2x. A 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year Treasury demands 11.8% free-cash-flow growth for a decade; the company delivered 1.5% in fiscal 2021-2025. [S9, S154]

::: scenarios
| Scenario | Probability | Drivers | Outcome | Signposts | Source |

Three transfers sit outside the operating story and each lands on the same high-margin layer. The reported $20bn search payment is 22% of services gross profit, and the D.D.C. remedies decision of 2025-09-02 preserved it only on non-exclusive, one-year-or-shorter terms, with appeals pending and argument sought from 2026-12-09. The Digital Markets Act produced a €500m fine on 2025-04-23 and an open Article 6(4) file; the US Department of Justice case is in discovery toward a 2027 trial. China is the third: revenue rose 30% in nine months, but Huawei holds 22.6% of units with HarmonyOS and price discipline, and IDC expects China shipments to fall about 20% in the second half of 2026, so the region that supplied the most growth enters FY2027 against its hardest comparison. Capital allocation does not cushion any of it: $62.1bn of stock was repurchased in nine months at a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.93% Treasury. [S118, S6]

Two analogs bound the decision. Microsoft after 2014 shows that a legacy incumbent can re-rate through a platform shift — market value from about $381bn to about $3tn in a decade — but Microsoft began near 10-12x earnings, so much of its return came from re-rating; Apple starts at 39.5x and would have to earn the return. Nokia shows the failure mode: 40-50% of global handsets in 2007, under 5% by 2013, because the platform shift moved value to software it did not control. Apple owns its platform and rents the frontier model, closer to Microsoft's early cloud years than to Nokia's collapse; the difference is the price of admission. [S198, S200]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft cloud transition | Best | 2014-2024 | An incumbent can re-rate through a platform shift, but much of the return came from starting near 10-12x; at 39.5x Apple must earn it | S198 |
| Nokia mobile phones | Cautionary | 2007-2013 | Device leadership did not survive a shift in the value layer to software the incumbent did not control; share fell from near 50% to under 5% in six years | S200 |
:::

The decision tree is explicit. Invest now: no, because expected value is below the price and the margin question is open. Pass: no, because the franchise, balance sheet and cash conversion are the best in the peer set and the AI risk is a cost, not an existential break. Wait for a milestone: yes, with 2026-11-02 as the first proof point. Invest with conditions: $240-265 for a 1-2% starter, at or below $225 for a 3-4% position capped at 4% because a single regulatory event is worth about 9.4% of market value, and trim above $395. Confidence is high in the arithmetic and the multiples, medium in the FY2027 margin path because Apple's pricing response to memory costs is undisclosed, and low in any forecast of AI revenue, which does not yet exist. The diligence question that would change the decision is what the December guide implies for gross margin ex-refund; at or above 48% the base moves toward $296 and the starter band toward $270, while near 45% it converges on the bear case.

Two diligence questions decide the entry: what the December guide implies for gross margin ex-refund, and whether the first one-year renewal of the search payment holds near $20bn. arguments.markdown:
Apple scores 5.7 out of 10: a franchise in the top decile of its peer set, priced in the bottom decile of its own history. The score is not a verdict on the business. Business quality and financial strength score 9 each; valuation scores 2 and earnings durability 4, and the 25% weight on valuation is what turns the composite into a watchlist score rather than a buy. On a margin-adjusted base of $268 the stock is 22% above fair value, and the probability-weighted value of $275 is a 20% negative return from the $344.63 close of 2026-10-30. The recommendation is Watchlist, with no position, a starter band of $240-265 and a full position at or below $225. [S199]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 20% | 9 | More than 2.5bn active devices, a record 23.6% iOS share of 2026 shipments, a 76.3% services gross margin and return on assets of 36.1% against Microsoft's 35.9% ROIC and Alphabet's 37.0% | S191, S66, S6, S27, S41 |
| Financial quality and balance sheet | 15% | 9 | Free cash flow 1.06x net income, capex 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft, net cash of $62.2bn and commercial paper cut to $2.0bn | S6, S27 |
| Growth and market runway | 15% | 5 | Revenue up 16.2% in nine months but on price and share taken from a collapsing entry tier; global units fall 16.7%, Services grow 14.1% and China enters a 20% unit decline | S6, S66, S195 |
| Earnings quality and durability | 10% | 4 | FY2025 EPS growth of 22.7% is 10.4% normalised; 2.0 points of the June gross margin are tariff refunds; inventory up 87% against revenue up 16.2% | S5, S6, S199 |
| Valuation | 25% | 2 | 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward against a 21.0x peer median; 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year; reverse DCF needs 11.8% growth against 1.5% delivered | S9, S154, S155 |
| Policy and regulatory | 10% | 6 | DMA fine of €500m on 2025-04-23, US contempt finding, DOJ case toward a 2027 trial, search payment on one-year non-exclusive terms; China access intact | S7, S5, S118, S42 |
| Management and capital allocation | 5% | 6 | Succession complete with Ternus as CEO from 2026-09-01; $62.1bn repurchased in nine months at a 2.5% earnings yield against 4.93% | S152, S174, S6, S164 |
| **Composite** | **100%** | **5.7** | Weighted average of the seven dimensions, to one decimal | Calculated |

The weighted average is 5.7: (0.20 x 9) + (0.15 x 9) + (0.15 x 5) + (0.10 x 4) + (0.25 x 2) + (0.10 x 6) + (0.05 x 6) = 5.70. Every dimension scoring 7 or above carries a peer or historical benchmark, and the two lowest scores are the ones the price depends on. Business quality and financial strength are why the name stays on the watchlist: the installed base, the 76.3% services margin, the 1.06x cash conversion and the net cash position are all at or above the mega-cap peer set. Valuation and earnings durability are why it is not bought: the market is paying 39.5x for an earnings base that contains a refund and a memory-cost tailwind the company has already guided away. [S9, S154]

The recommendation changes with the margin, not with the narrative. If gross margin settles near 45%, EPS lands between $8.20 and $8.50; at the five-year average multiple of 30.2x that is $248-257, and at the bear multiple of 25x it is $205. If margin holds at 48% and the AI cycle lifts upgrades, EPS reaches $10.50 and 38x gives $399. The full-position entry at or below $225 is therefore set so that the downside to the bear case is about 9%, while the base case pays 19% and the bull case 77%. The recommendation would move to Buy only with two consecutive quarters at or above 47% gross margin ex-refund and a price at or below $265; it would move to Reduce if the stock held above $395 without an EPS upgrade, and to Sell if two quarters of gross margin fell below 45% or services growth fell below 5% for two quarters. [S6, S118]

Position sizing follows the arithmetic rather than the enthusiasm. At $344.63 the probability-weighted return is negative, so the Kelly fraction is zero and the fund holds a watchlist slot, not stock. At $250, with a 70% chance of the base outcome (+10%) and a 30% chance of the bear (-18%), the full Kelly fraction is 16% and a quarter-Kelly is 4%, which becomes the cap because a single regulatory event, loss of the search payment, is worth 9.4% of market value. The plan is a 1-2% starter at $240-265, a 3-4% full position at or below $225, and a trim above $395. Maximum loss at the full-position entry is the $205 bear case, about 9%, against a $399 bull case. The market regime argues for the cap: the ten-year Treasury yields 4.93%, the VIX is 19.42 at the 77th percentile and technology is 7.4 points behind SPY over one month, so a 39.5x multiple carries de-rating risk that a 4% position contains. [S154, S163]

::: sensitivity
| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Impact level | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gross margin path | 46-47% in FY2027 | Two quarters at or above 48% ex-refund | Two points is 6.3% of net income; base $268, or $205 at 45% and 25x | High | December guide below 46% ex-refund on 2026-11-02 | S199, S194, S6 |
| 2 | Search payment | $20bn a year, non-exclusive, annual renewal | Appellate ban or a materially lower renewal | $474bn, 9.4% of market value, at 30x | High | D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09 | S118, S82 |
| 3 | Services growth | Low-to-mid teens | Two quarters below 5% | A three-point cut removes 2.8% of net income | Medium | EU Article 6(4); US link-out migration | S6, S122 |
| 4 | Exit multiple | 30.2x forward | Ten-year Treasury above 5% with EPS cuts | 25x instead of 30.2x costs 17% of value | High | Multiple at the 100th percentile of its five-year range | S154, S9 |
| 5 | Buyback pace | $60-80bn a year | A pause at 39.5x | 1.9 points of EPS growth and 1.6% of shareholder yield | Low | Repurchases $62.1bn against $70.6bn in nine months | S6, S164 |
:::

Five diligence actions would settle the entry. First, read the 2026-11-02 December-quarter guide for gross margin ex-refund and for revenue growth against the guided 9-11%. Second, track the D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09 and the terms of the first one-year renewal of the search payment. Third, read the FY2026 annual report for the refund and inventory decomposition, which the quarterly filings do not give. Fourth, measure the December-quarter China revenue against a +30% nine-month base and IDC's 20% unit decline. Fifth, check whether Services growth holds at or above 10% after the US link-out injunction and the EU Article 6(4) file. The conditions for investing are explicit: a price at or below $265, two quarters of gross margin at or above 47% ex-refund, and no adverse appellate ruling on the search payment. Until then the evidence supports watching, not owning. [S1, S118]

::: takeaways
1. Watchlist, zero position at $344.63: the margin-adjusted base is $268 and the probability-weighted value is $275, a 20% negative return even though the franchise is strong [S199, S154].
2. The buy bands are $240-265 for a 1-2% starter and at or below $225 for a 3-4% position, capped at 4% because one regulatory event is worth 9.4% of market value [S154, S118].
3. The 2026-11-02 December guide decides the case: at or above 48% gross margin ex-refund the base moves toward $296, near 45% it converges on the $205 bear [S199, S194].
:::

Business quality and financial strength score 9 each; valuation scores 2 and earnings durability 4, and the 25% weight on valuation is what turns the composite into a watchlist score rather than a buy. On a margin-adjusted base of $268 the stock is 22% above fair value, and the probability-weighted value of $275 is a 20% negative return from the $344.63 close of 2026-10-30. The recommendation is Watchlist, with no position, a starter band of $240-265 and a full position at or below $225. [S199, S9]

| Dimension | Weight | Score (1-10) | Rationale | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business quality and moat | 20% | 9 | More than 2.5bn active devices, a record 23.6% iOS share of 2026 shipments, a 76.3% services gross margin and return on assets of 36.1% against Microsoft's 35.9% ROIC and Alphabet's 37.0% | S191, S66, S6, S27, S41 |
| Financial quality and balance sheet | 15% | 9 | Free cash flow 1.06x net income, capex 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft, net cash of $62.2bn and commercial paper cut to $2.0bn | S6, S27 |
| Growth and market runway | 15% | 5 | Revenue up 16.2% in nine months but on price and share taken from a collapsing entry tier; global units fall 16.7%, Services grow 14.1% and China enters a 20% unit decline | S6, S66, S195 |
| Earnings quality and durability | 10% | 4 | FY2025 EPS growth of 22.7% is 10.4% normalised; 2.0 points of the June gross margin are tariff refunds; inventory up 87% against revenue up 16.2% | S5, S6, S199 |
| Valuation | 25% | 2 | 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward against a 21.0x peer median; 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year; reverse DCF needs 11.8% growth against 1.5% delivered | S9, S154, S155 |
| Policy and regulatory | 10% | 6 | DMA fine of €500m on 2025-04-23, US contempt finding, DOJ case toward a 2027 trial, search payment on one-year non-exclusive terms; China access intact | S7, S5, S118, S42 |
| Management and capital allocation | 5% | 6 | Succession complete with Ternus as CEO from 2026-09-01; $62.1bn repurchased in nine months at a 2.5% earnings yield against 4.93% | S152, S174, S6, S164 |
| **Composite** | **100%** | **5.7** | Weighted average of the seven dimensions, to one decimal | S9, S6, S154 |

The weighted average of the seven dimensions is the composite: business quality and financial strength keep the name on the watchlist, while valuation and earnings durability keep it out of the portfolio. Every dimension scoring 7 or above carries a peer or historical benchmark, and the two lowest scores are the ones the price depends on. The installed base, the 76.3% services margin, the 1.06x cash conversion and the net cash position are at or above the mega-cap peer set; the 39.5x multiple is being paid for an earnings base that contains a refund and a memory-cost tailwind the company has already guided away.

The recommendation changes with the margin, not with the narrative. If gross margin settles near 45%, EPS lands between $8.20 and $8.50; at the five-year average multiple of 30.2x that is $248-257, and at the bear multiple of 25x it is $205. If margin holds at 48% and the AI cycle lifts upgrades, EPS reaches $10.50 and 38x gives $399. The full-position entry at or below $225 is set so that the downside to the bear case is about 9%, while the base case pays 19% and the bull case 77%. The recommendation would move to Buy only with two consecutive quarters at or above 47% gross margin ex-refund and a price at or below $265; it would move to Reduce if the stock held above $395 without an EPS upgrade, and to Sell if two quarters of gross margin fell below 45% or services growth fell below 5% for two quarters. [S6, S118]

Position sizing follows the arithmetic rather than the enthusiasm. At $344.63 the probability-weighted return is negative, so the Kelly fraction is zero and the fund holds a watchlist slot, not stock. At $250, with a 70% chance of the base outcome (+10%) and a 30% chance of the bear (-18%), the full Kelly fraction is 16% and a quarter-Kelly is 4%, which becomes the cap because a single regulatory event, loss of the search payment, is worth 9.4% of market value. The plan is a 1-2% starter at $240-265, a 3-4% full position at or below $225, and a trim above $395. Maximum loss at the full-position entry is the $205 bear case, about 9%, against a $399 bull case. The market regime argues for the cap: the ten-year Treasury yields 4.93%, the VIX is 19.42 at the 77th percentile and technology is 7.4 points behind SPY over one month, so a 39.5x multiple carries de-rating risk that a 4% position contains. [S154, S163]

Value is most sensitive to the margin path and the exit multiple; the regulatory and buyback assumptions matter less in the arithmetic, though the search payment is the largest single-event risk.

::: sensitivity
| Rank | Assumption | Base | What would disprove it | Impact on value | Impact level | Early warning | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gross margin path | 46-47% in FY2027 | Two quarters at or above 48% ex-refund | Two points is 6.3% of net income; base $268, or $205 at 45% and 25x | High | December guide below 46% ex-refund on 2026-11-02 | S199, S194, S6 |
| 2 | Search payment | $20bn a year, non-exclusive, annual renewal | Appellate ban or a materially lower renewal | $474bn, 9.4% of market value, at 30x | High | D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09 | S118, S82 |
| 3 | Services growth | Low-to-mid teens | Two quarters below 5% | A three-point cut removes 2.8% of net income | Medium | EU Article 6(4); US link-out migration | S6, S122 |
| 4 | Exit multiple | 30.2x forward | Ten-year Treasury above 5% with EPS cuts | 25x instead of 30.2x costs 17% of value | High | Multiple at the 100th percentile of its five-year range | S154, S9 |
| 5 | Buyback pace | $60-80bn a year | A pause at 39.5x | 1.9 points of EPS growth and 1.6% of shareholder yield | Low | Repurchases $62.1bn against $70.6bn in nine months | S6, S164 |
:::

Five diligence actions would settle the entry. Read the December-quarter guide for gross margin ex-refund and for revenue growth against the guided range. Track the D.C. Circuit argument and the terms of the first one-year renewal of the search payment. Read the FY2026 annual report for the refund and inventory decomposition that the quarterly filings do not give. Measure the December-quarter China revenue against the nine-month base and IDC's unit decline. Check whether Services growth holds after the US link-out injunction and the EU Article 6(4) file. The conditions for investing are explicit: a price at or below $265, two quarters of gross margin at or above 47% ex-refund, and no adverse appellate ruling on the search payment. Until then the evidence supports watching, not owning.

::: takeaways
1. Watchlist, zero position at $344.63: the margin-adjusted base is $268 and the probability-weighted value is $275, a 20% negative return even though the franchise is strong [S199, S154].
2. The buy bands are $240-265 for a 1-2% starter and at or below $225 for a 3-4% position, capped at 4% because one regulatory event is worth 9.4% of market value [S154, S118].
3. The 2026-11-02 December guide decides the case: at or above 48% gross margin ex-refund the base moves toward $296, near 45% it converges on the $205 bear [S199, S194].
:::

The regime offers no cushion: the S&P 500 sits 3.4% below its 52-week high, the VIX is 19.42 at the 77th percentile, the ten-year Treasury yields 4.93%, and technology lagged SPY by 7.4 points over the past month while energy and health care led. [S9, S10, S11, S12]

The recommendation is Watchlist with no position and a composite score of 5.7 out of 10. Apple is a high-quality franchise at a price that capitalises its best margin year: on a margin-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $8.87 at the five-year average multiple of 30.2x, fair value is $268, 22% below the close, and the probability-weighted value of the three cases is $275. The fund should own it only below $265, where the base case pays and the bear case is survivable. [S199, S154]

The positives are not in dispute: the largest installed base in the industry, a services margin near 76%, free cash flow at 1.06x net income, $62.2bn of net cash and a succession that is already complete. The risks are equally concrete: a gross margin that included 2.0 points of tariff refunds in June and is guided down to 47-48% for September, a search payment worth 22% of services gross profit that survives only on one-year non-exclusive terms, a China business that grew 30% in nine months against a forecast 20% unit decline in the second half, and a multiple at the 100th percentile of its five-year range. [S6, S118]

The sell side is not wrong about the franchise; it is higher than us on the earnings base and the multiple. Its average target sits below the price it covers, and its forward EPS assumes the margin recovers while the company's own guide assumes it falls. Our difference is narrow in direction and large in consequence: we are below consensus on FY2027 EPS and on the multiple, and the gap is the whole margin of safety.

The next twelve months carry three dated tests: the fiscal fourth-quarter results and December-quarter guide on 2026-11-02, argument in the Google search-remedy appeal from 2026-12-09, and the Busan trade truce expiry on 2027-01-10. The first of these decides the case, because it is the first outlook without the carry-in inventory cushion and the first clean read on the margin ex-refund.

The entry plan follows the evidence rather than the excitement: a starter position of 1-2% in the $240-265 band, a full position of 3-4% at or below $225, a cap of 4% because one regulatory event is worth 9.4% of market value, and a trim above $395. Confidence is high in the valuation arithmetic, medium in the margin path, and low in any AI revenue forecast, which does not yet exist.

:::

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Playbook: decision_framework.md

# Decision Framework

Use this file before drafting the executive briefing, investment thesis, recommendation, scoring, or final decision. Do not force precision when evidence does not support it.

## Contents

- Consensus / Non-Consensus View
- Scenario Analysis
- Key Assumptions
- Historical Analogs
- Capital Efficiency
- Position Sizing / Deal Sizing
- The One Question
- Three Takeaways

## Consensus / Non-Consensus View

State what the market, comparable investors, or the company's own pitch appears to assume. Then state whether the report has a differentiated view.

If there is no non-consensus insight, say the thesis is consensus and explain what that means for return expectations, valuation discipline, or margin of safety. Do not invent a variant perception for appearance.

## Scenario Analysis

Use bull/base/bear cases with explicit drivers and approximate probabilities.

- For public equities and growth companies, scenarios may use revenue, margin, multiple, cash flow, valuation, catalyst timing, or downside drawdown.
- For early-stage, biotech, hard-tech, and data-poor cases, use milestone scenarios such as product-market fit, regulatory readout, manufacturing yield, customer conversion, financing survival, or exit path.

Each scenario should include:

- Specific driver or failure mode.
- Evidence that makes it plausible.
- Financial or milestone implication.
- Investor implication.

For public equities, build scenarios from explicit financial drivers where data allows: revenue growth, segment mix, gross/operating margin, tax, share count, capex, working capital, free cash flow, net cash/debt, and valuation multiple. Include current share price context before stating upside/downside.

## Key Assumptions

Rank the 3-5 assumptions that most affect the decision. For each, state:

- Confidence.
- What would disprove it.
- Impact if wrong.
- Early warning sign.

This is often more useful than adding more facts.

## Historical Analogs

Use historical analogs only when they are close enough to teach a decision rule. A good analog matches on business model, market structure, stage, regulation, customer behavior, or capital intensity.

If no close analog exists, say so.

## Capital Efficiency

Use a capital efficiency scorecard when the company has raised material capital and data exists. Useful metrics include burn multiple, revenue per dollar raised, runway, revenue per employee, capex to next milestone, and dilution efficiency.

If data is unavailable, state which missing data would be required.

For public equities, capital efficiency should use reported financials where available: ROIC, ROE, ROA, asset turnover, incremental margins, reinvestment rate, FCF conversion, dividend/buyback yield, dilution, and M&A returns. Tie these to management capital allocation quality.

## Position Sizing / Deal Sizing

Use position sizing for public equities, liquid secondaries, or explicit portfolio-allocation requests.

For public equities, position size must reflect valuation upside/downside, balance-sheet resilience, liquidity, accounting quality, catalyst timing, volatility, evidence confidence, and whether the downside is mark-to-market volatility or permanent capital impairment.

For primary-market deals, translate this into check size, valuation discipline, downside loss, reserve strategy, and conditions for follow-on investment.

## The One Question

Before finalizing, identify the single diligence question whose truthful answer would most change the investment decision. It must be specific, answerable in principle, and decision-changing.

## Three Takeaways

End with the three things the reader should remember. These should be decision statements, not generic summaries."}],"isError":false}
