### The growth is half tax base effect, and a quarter buyback

Fiscal 2025's net income rose 19.5%, but pretax income rose 7.5% ($132,729M against $123,485M) and the tax provision fell 30.3% to $20,719M because fiscal 2024 carried the one-time $10.2bn Irish charge — $15.8bn payable to Ireland, offset by a $4.8bn US foreign tax credit and $823M of released unrecognised benefits. Normalising fiscal 2024 at fiscal 2025's 15.6% rate gives $104,222M and underlying growth of 7.5%, not 19.5%. The EPS gap above that is the buyback: from fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2025 net income grew 15.5% while diluted EPS grew 21.7% and diluted shares fell 5.1%, so 5.4 percentage points of EPS growth was a smaller denominator — and that contribution is fading, at 1.9 percentage points in the trailing twelve months (EPS +16.9% against net income +15.1%), because repurchases slowed to $62,094M in the nine months to 2026-06-27 from $70,579M while operating cash flow rose 43%. Capital return has stopped outrunning cash: buybacks and dividends were $97,866M against free cash flow of $136,683M, or 72%, against 107% in fiscal 2025, and net cash rose by $28,410M in nine months. At the $344.63 close on 2026-10-30 and the 14,594.2M shares issued and outstanding reported on the 10-Q cover at 2026-07-17, equity is worth $5.03trn; on trailing diluted EPS of $8.72 that is 39.5x earnings and a 2.72% free cash flow yield, while the ten-year Treasury yielded 4.93%. Diluted shares of 14,715M are the EPS denominator and sit 0.8% above the outstanding count, so the two bases are consistent. Repurchasing at that spread is accretive to EPS and not obviously accretive to value per share [S5, S6, S9].

### Cash is real; the working-capital cushion is not

Cash generation is the strongest part of the record and the hardest to fake: operating cash flow of $146,724M against capital expenditure of $10,041M, with free cash flow at 1.06x net income. The anomaly is fiscal 2025, when free cash flow fell to 0.88x of net income despite $111,482M of operating cash flow; cash paid for income taxes that year was $43,369M, 32.7% of pretax income against a 15.6% book rate and 21.1% in fiscal 2024 — a gap consistent with settlement payments on the Irish case and the TCJA repatriation tax, the final $8.8bn of which was paid in the nine months to 2026-06-27. That supports reading the gap as timing, and the recovery to 1.06x is consistent with it. The working-capital change runs the other way: inventory reached $11,092M at 2026-06-27 from $5,925M a year earlier, an 87% increase against 16.2% revenue growth, lifting days inventory to 16.9 from 9.4 and pulling the cash conversion cycle to −56.8 days from −71.1 at the fiscal 2025 year-end [S5, S6].

The balance sheet carries no leverage risk: at 2026-06-27 Apple held $146,517M of cash and marketable securities against $84,344M of debt, for net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M, with commercial paper cut to $1,997M from $7,979M, and other income and expense netted to −$321M in fiscal 2025 because interest earned on the securities book offsets interest paid. The commitments that matter are forward purchases — $57.0bn of manufacturing purchase obligations, $56.2bn due within twelve months, and $29.3bn of other purchase obligations — which fix component supply and, with it, the cost base when memory prices move. Two accounting details deserve attention: gross intangible assets rose $13,270M to $38,220M in nine months with no goodwill recognised, which indicates purchased intellectual property, content or asset acquisitions rather than share purchases, and is not explained in the quarterly filing; and gross unrecognised tax benefits were $23.2bn at 2025-09-27, of which $10.6bn would affect the effective rate and up to $6bn may move within twelve months [S6].

### Returns are distorted by the buyback, not flattered by the business

Reported returns are not usable as quality scores: return on equity was 148.8% and return on invested capital 320.6% on invested capital of $45,347M — $107,520M of equity plus $84,344M of debt less $146,517M of securities — because $258,212M of cumulative buybacks shrank the equity base. The honest comparison is return on assets of 36.1% against Microsoft's 35.9% return on invested capital in fiscal 2026 and Alphabet's 37.0% in fiscal 2025 [S6, S27, S41].

### What moves the outcome, and by how much

The geographic picture also cuts against the standard bear case: Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64,839M in the nine months to 2026-06-27 and 22% in the June quarter, so nine months already exceed the whole of fiscal 2025's $64,377M after two years of decline. What moves the outcome most is gross margin. On trailing-twelve-month revenue of $466,823M one point of gross margin is $4,668M of pretax profit, or 3.0% of net income, while one point of revenue growth at the current margin is $1,878M, or 1.5%. Three cases, all on the trailing twelve months and none a forecast: a two-point margin gain takes EPS to $9.24, a two-point give-back to $8.20, and a two-point give-back with the loss of the search licence to $7.11, 18.8% below the base — and the licence should be modelled as intact but repriced annually, because the September 2025 order permitted non-exclusive placement payments of one year or less rather than ending them, while the $20bn figure is a 2022 court-record number Apple has never confirmed. The cash is real and the balance sheet is net cash; the growth is weaker than reported; and the margin sits at a cyclical high with a tariff-refund component inside it. An investor paying 39.5x trailing earnings is paying for the first and third to persist while the second is already reversing. The diligence question that matters most is what the fiscal 2026 annual report says about inventory composition and the split between refund and product mix, neither of which the quarterly filings settle [S6, S82, S118].

::: info warning
**The fiscal 2026 gross margin is not yet a clean number.** Strip out the tariff refund Apple attributes to the June quarter and the margin is still above any full year in this record, but a smaller step-change than the reported figure implies; against an inventory build growing faster than revenue, the annual report carries the burden of proof.
:::

Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack is still the widest integrated consumer technology stack, but in 2026 the company rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — so what remains defensible is distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved the iPhone to TSMC N2, the C2 modem reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google announced the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to TSMC N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS, about double the prior generation's AI throughput. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm, so each step costs more. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9% a year earlier, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q warns that advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints are expected to intensify [S6, S64].

| Node, A19 Pro / A20 Pro | TSMC N3P (2025) / N2 (2026) | Teardown and trade reporting | S63, S64 |
| Neural Engine, A20 Pro | 32 cores, ~52 TOPS, ~2x A19 Pro | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| N2 wafer price | ~$30,000 vs $18,000-20,000 at 3nm | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| Product gross margin | 39.9% vs 36.9% (9M FY2025) | Reported financials | S6 |
| On-device model / PCC context | ~3B parameters / 32K tokens | Apple research and developer docs | S61, S62 |

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device, Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model optimised through KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; on its servers, a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model runs inside Private Cloud Compute, which enforces stateless processing, no privileged access even for Apple staff, and attested software images. The binding constraint is memory bandwidth and power: phone-class memory caps on-device inference at single-digit billions of parameters, so harder queries are offloaded. The ceiling is disclosed: a 32K-token context is small against frontier assistants, and Apple's own models were not frontier-quality. The unresolved question for the privacy story is where Gemini-derived inference physically runs: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on Apple devices and Private Cloud Compute, while trade reporting says Google's cloud performs the Gemini computation, puts the licence at ~$1bn a year and the default-search payment at ~$20bn. Neither figure is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, nearly two years after its 2024 debut, with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu supplying a separate model stack. Apple's differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; an investor should underwrite the cash flow and installed base, not the AI layer [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched on 2026-09-09 at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 went on sale on 2026-10-23. iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27, with Greater China up 30%. The C2 modem supports US mmWave and uses 15% less energy than the C1X, but the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max appears to keep a Qualcomm modem, so Qualcomm retains leverage over the highest-ASP SKU. Vision Pro is the counter-example: ~390,000 units in 2024, ~45,000 in the December 2025 quarter despite the M5 refresh, ~600,000 lifetime, and an IDC forecast of ~290,000 units in 2026 [S59, S13, S87].

### What is enforceable is regulatory, not patent

Apple publishes no patent count; the FY2025 10-K says only that it is "pursuing thousands of applications around the world" and that no single right protects its products [S5]. Patent families and technology-specific grants therefore remain unverified: USPTO Patent Center and EPO Espacenet could not be searched in this research, and the export of 2024-2026 Apple-assigned families in on-device AI, wearable health, foldable hinge and AR optics has been requested. The only cross-company measure retrieved is grant counts: Apple took 2,722 US patents in 2025, down 11.6% from 3,082 and sixth overall, against Samsung's 7,054 in first place for a fourth year and Huawei's 3,052 in fourth [S211]. In AI filings Apple does not appear in the top three worldwide, where Samsung filed 2,162, Huawei 1,822 and Google 1,672 in 2025 [S208]. Those bound the portfolio without measuring it. What is documented in detail is a regulatory estate — hypertension and sleep-apnoea notifications, a hearing-aid De Novo grant and imaging calibration — each cleared on its own clinical file, a slower but more durable barrier than a patent family.

### The moat is wide at the bottom of the stack and thin at the top

| Installed base and developers | 8 | A decade of switching costs and services attach, but not exclusive | Every platform owner holds a multi-billion-device base; the barrier is monetisation depth, not access | 10+ years | S5 |
| **Composite** | **8/10 hardware, 4/10 AI** | Hard to copy, easy to rent; IP adds no credit | 8+ years for a new entrant; Samsung still buys flagship silicon | — | S58, S64, S207 |

The replication test is now a base rate rather than an assertion. Intel bought Infineon's wireless unit for about $1.4bn in a deal that closed in Q1 2011, then sold its smartphone modem business to Apple for $1bn, completed on 2019-12-02 — roughly nine years without a durable phone-modem position [S206, S210]. Apple began from that purchase, 2,200 engineers and more than 17,000 wireless patents, and shipped its first in-house modem, the C1 in the iPhone 16e, in February 2025, just over five years later; in 2026 the largest iPhone still appears to carry Qualcomm [S209, S59]. Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack is still the widest integrated consumer technology stack, but in 2026 the company rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — so what remains defensible is distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved the iPhone to TSMC N2, the C2 modem reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google announced the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to TSMC N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS, about double the prior generation's AI throughput. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm, so each step costs more. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9% a year earlier, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q warns that advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints are expected to intensify [S6, S64].

| N2 wafer price | ~$30,000 vs $18,000-20,000 at 3nm | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| Product gross margin | 39.9% vs 36.9% (9M FY2025) | Reported financials | S6 |
| On-device model / PCC context | ~3B parameters / 32K tokens | Apple research and developer docs | S61, S62 |

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device, Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model optimised through KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; on its servers, a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model runs inside Private Cloud Compute, which enforces stateless processing, no privileged access even for Apple staff, and attested software images. The binding constraint is memory bandwidth and power: phone-class memory caps on-device inference at single-digit billions of parameters, so harder queries are offloaded. The ceiling is disclosed: a 32K-token context is small against frontier assistants, and Apple's own models were not frontier-quality. The unresolved question for the privacy story is where Gemini-derived inference physically runs: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on Apple devices and Private Cloud Compute, while trade reporting places the Gemini computation in Google's cloud, the licence at ~$1bn a year and the default-search payment at ~$20bn. Neither figure is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, nearly two years after its 2024 debut, with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu supplying a separate model stack. Apple's differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; an investor should underwrite the cash flow and installed base, not the AI layer [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched on 2026-09-09 at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 went on sale on 2026-10-23. iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27, with Greater China up 30%. The policy tests are narrow for a US holder: no foreign-buyer limit on a share sale, no lock-up, and no venue constraint at NasdaqGS, the S&P 500 or the Nasdaq-100. The binding policy risk sits in the asset, not the exit. The Google search payment, reported at $20B in 2022 and never disclosed by Apple, is on today's base about 17% of trailing Services revenue of $120.5B and 22% of services gross profit of $91.6B, and it survived the D.D.C.'s remedies decision of 2025-09-02, which refused the DOJ's near-total ban on distribution payments and permitted non-exclusive default-placement deals of one year or less. Final judgment followed in December 2025, Google appealed in January 2026 and the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026; the appeals were pending at 2026-10-29. The payment continues on non-exclusive, annually renegotiated terms; the event that would force a sale is its loss or material cut at a renewal or on appeal, not a ban in force. $20B of near-pure-margin revenue taxed at 21% is $15.8B of earnings, and at 30x that is $474B, 9.4% of the $5,029.6B market value. The slower policy risks are DMA and DOJ commission rules, and China, where revenue was $64.8B in nine months of fiscal 2026 and can turn on policy rather than Apple's execution. At 38.9x margin-adjusted earnings there is no cushion for a services margin shock. [S118, S42, S82, S13]

The strongest case against this discipline is that a 30x-plus multiple never offers a margin of safety again. The answer is a time rule rather than a permanent price target: if Apple trades above $268 for four consecutive quarters while Services growth stays above 10%, reassess the band against the then-current multiple instead of waiting for a level the business has outgrown. Until then, watchlist above $268, a 1-2% starter at $240-265, a full 3-4% position at or below $225 and a trim to half at or above $395. Confidence is high in the drawdown record and the return arithmetic, medium in the exit multiple, which depends on the ten-year yield of 4.93% on 2026-10-30. The diligence questions are the first one-year renewal of the Google payment, the June margin without the 2 points of tariff refund, and whether the 2026-11-02 release confirms the 47-48% September guide. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 4 by Lead Analyst, 8,839 characters)
Apple at $344.63 is a great business at a price that assumes its best margin year is permanent. More than 2.5bn active devices, a record 23.6% of smartphone shipments and a quarter of revenue from Services make the need real; custom silicon, iOS and carrier distribution make the capability defensible, though the frontier model is licensed from Google. The economics scale: $466.8bn of trailing revenue, $136.7bn of free cash flow and capital expenditure at 2.2% of sales. The question is price. If a ~50% gross margin is a floor, the stock is fairly valued at 35x forward earnings; if it is a refund-and-memory peak, our calculation on the verified June margin and the September guide puts fair value at $268, 22% below the close. [S13, S6]

Demand is replacement, not discovery. Global units fall 16.7% to 1.0bn in 2026 while market value rises 6.3% to $613bn, and Apple's nine-month revenue grew 16.2% on price and on share taken from a collapsing entry tier. Greater China supplied 4.1 points of that growth with revenue up 30.0%. The moat is real: the A20 Pro on TSMC N2, a 76.3% services gross margin, 60% of sales through carriers and selling expense at 6.6% of revenue. It protects the annuity, not the growth. Siri runs on a Google-built model, Vision Pro shipped 45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, and interoperability rules may keep the rebuilt assistant out of the European Union. [S191, S66]

The economics turn at the line the multiple capitalises. Services produced 39.1% of gross profit in nine months, down from 42.2% in FY2025, because product gross profit grew 26.3% against 15.3%. The margin is not clean: the June quarter's 50.1% included 2.0 points of tariff refunds, verified in Apple's 2026-07-30 release, and the 47-48% September guide — company guidance on the earnings call, trade-reported and unverified in the release, with another point of refunds — leaves 46-47% underlying against 48.1% in June ex-refund, which management attributed to memory. Two points on $490bn of FY2027 revenue is $9.8bn of pretax profit, 6.3% of trailing net income, leaving EPS near $8.87 rather than the $9.79 consensus: the team's calculation on S6 and S13. [S13, S6, S202]

Consensus is right about the franchise and wrong about the price. The average target is $339.35, below the close. The stock trades at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 21.0x mega-cap peer median and 21.76x for the S&P 500 — 88% above peers and 1.8 times the index, at the 100th percentile of a five-year range whose average is 30.2x. A 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year Treasury demands 11.8% free-cash-flow growth for a decade; the company delivered 1.5% in fiscal 2021-2025. The asymmetry runs against the buyer: the bull case pays 16% before dividends and needs the margin question answered in Apple's favour, the base case loses 22% even though the franchise performs, and the bear loses 41%. Weighting the cases 15/50/35 gives an expected value of $266, a 23% negative return, which is why the position is zero rather than small. The bull case is not a fantasy — Apple has beaten estimates through the squeeze and raised iPad and Mac prices without visible demand destruction — but it is the minority case because the company's own September guide already carries the give-back the consensus EPS denies. [S9, S154]

| Base | 50% | Refund rolls off, memory takes two points, EPS near $8.87, multiple at its five-year average | $8.87 at 30.2x = $268, -22% | Guide 46-47% ex-refund; EPS cuts; multiple toward 30x | S13, S6, S154 |

| 1 | Gross margin settles at 46-47% in FY2027, not the 48-49% consensus implies | Medium | Two quarters at or above 48% ex-refund; a December guide at or above 48% | Two points is $9.8bn pretax, 6.3% of net income; base $268, 22% below the close | December guide below 46% ex-refund; DRAM tight through 2027; inventory +87% year on year | S13, S6, S194 |
| 2 | The search payment survives near $20bn a year, repriced annually and non-exclusive | Medium | An appellate ban, or a renewal at a materially lower rate | 17% of Services revenue, 22% of services gross profit; at 30x, $474bn or 9.4% of market value | D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09; first renewal terms | S6, S82, S118 |
| 3 | Services compound in the low-to-mid teens without a mandated take-rate collapse | Medium | Two quarters below 5% growth; a remedy stripping commission on a material share | A three-point growth cut removes $3.6bn of revenue and 2.8% of net income | EU Article 6(4); US link-out migration; services growth decelerating | S6, S5, S122 |
| 4 | The iPhone 18 and Duo cycle sustains high-single-digit revenue growth without refunds | Medium | A holiday quarter below the guided 9-11%; a Duo ramp that cannibalises Pro volumes | Each point of revenue growth is 1.5% of net income | 2026-11-02 results; China units down 20% in H2 2026 | S1, S13, S195 |
:::

Three transfers sit outside the operating story and each lands on the same high-margin layer. The reported $20bn search payment is 22% of services gross profit, and the D.D.C. remedies decision of 2025-09-02 preserved it only on non-exclusive, one-year-or-shorter terms, with appeals pending and argument sought from 2026-12-09. The Digital Markets Act produced a €500m fine on 2025-04-23 and an open Article 6(4) file; the US Department of Justice case is in discovery toward a 2027 trial. China is the third: revenue rose 30% in nine months, but Huawei holds 22.6% of units with HarmonyOS and price discipline, and IDC expects China shipments to fall 20% in the second half of 2026, so the region that supplied the most growth enters FY2027 against its hardest comparison. Capital allocation does not cushion any of it: $62.1bn of stock was repurchased in nine months at a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.93% Treasury. The decision tree follows: invest now no, because expected value is below the price and the margin question is open; pass no, because the franchise, balance sheet and cash conversion are the best in the peer set and the AI risk is a cost rather than an existential break; wait for the 2026-11-02 guide; then invest with conditions at $240-265 for a 1-2% starter and at or below $225 for a 3-4% position capped at 4%, trimming above $395. [S118, S6, S154]

Two analogs bound the decision. Microsoft after 2014 shows that a legacy incumbent can re-rate through a platform shift — market value from $381bn to $3.0tn in a decade — but Microsoft began near 10-12x earnings, so much of its return came from re-rating; Apple starts at 39.5x and would have to earn the return. Nokia shows the failure mode: 40-50% of global handsets in 2007, under 5% by 2013, because the platform shift moved value to software it did not control. Apple owns its platform and rents the frontier model, closer to Microsoft's early cloud years than to Nokia's collapse; the difference is the price of admission. Two diligence questions decide the entry: what the December guide implies for gross margin ex-refund, and whether the first one-year renewal of the search payment holds near $20bn. Confidence is high in the arithmetic and the multiples, medium in the FY2027 margin path because the September range is transcript-based and Apple's pricing response to memory costs is undisclosed, and low in any forecast of AI revenue, which does not yet exist; the Watchlist call rests on the verified June margin and the multiple, not on the guide alone. At or above 48% ex-refund on 2026-11-02 the base moves toward $296 and the starter band toward $270; near 45% it converges on the bear case. [S198, S200, S13]

::: analogs
| Analog | Kind | Period | Lesson | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft cloud transition | Best | 2014-2024 | An incumbent can re-rate through a platform shift, but much of the return came from starting near 10-12x; at 39.5x Apple must earn it | S198 |
| Nokia mobile phones | Cautionary | 2007-2013 | Device leadership did not survive a shift in the value layer to software the incumbent did not control; share fell from near 50% to under 5% in six years | S200 |
:::"}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Comprehensive Scoring & Recommendation (scoring, revision 5 by Lead Analyst, 7,633 characters)
Apple scores 5.7 out of 10: a franchise in the top decile of its peer set, priced in the bottom decile of its own history. The score is not a verdict on the business. Business quality and financial strength score 9 each; valuation scores 2 and earnings durability 4, and the 25% weight on valuation is what turns the composite into a watchlist score rather than a buy. On a margin-adjusted base of $268, fair value is 22% below the $344.63 close of 2026-10-30, and the probability-weighted value of $266 is a 23% negative return. The recommendation is Watchlist, with no position, a starter band of $240-265 and a full position at or below $225. [S13, S9]

Maximum loss at the full-position entry is 17-24% to the 21x de-rating case of $172-186, against a $399 bull case; a starter at $265 carries 30-35%. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Executive Briefing (executive_summary, revision 4 by Lead Analyst, 6,693 characters)
Apple closed at $344.63 on 2026-10-30, a $5,029.6bn market capitalisation, 1.2% below its all-time closing high of $348.91 on 2026-10-29 and 27.5% higher over twelve months against 10.8% for the S&P 500, with an 11.6% gain since the 2026-07-30 results against 1.2% for the index. [S9, S10, S11, S12]

The recommendation is Watchlist with no position and a composite score of 5.7 out of 10. Apple is a high-quality franchise at a price that capitalises its best margin year: on a margin-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $8.87 at the five-year average multiple of 30.2x, fair value is $268, 22% below the close, and the probability-weighted value of the three cases is $266, a 23% negative return. The fund should own it only below $265, where the base case pays and the bear case is survivable. [S13, S154]

The positives are not in dispute: the largest single-vendor installed base in the industry, a services margin near 76%, free cash flow at 1.06x net income, $62.2bn of net cash and a succession that is already complete. The risks are equally concrete: a gross margin that included 2.0 points of tariff refunds in June and a September guide of 47-48% stated on the earnings call rather than in the release, a search payment worth 22% of services gross profit that survives only on one-year non-exclusive terms, a China business that grew 30% in nine months against a forecast 20% unit decline in the second half, and a multiple at the 100th percentile of its five-year range. [S6, S118, S191, S202]

The sell side is not wrong about the franchise; it is higher than us on the earnings base and the multiple. Its average target sits below the price it covers, and its forward EPS assumes the margin recovers while the company's own call-stated September guide assumes it falls. Our difference is narrow in direction and large in consequence: we are below consensus on FY2027 EPS and on the multiple, and the gap is the whole margin of safety.

The next twelve months carry three dated tests: the fiscal fourth-quarter results and December-quarter guide on 2026-11-02, argument in the Google search-remedy appeal from 2026-12-09, and the Busan trade truce expiry on 2027-01-10. The first of these decides the case, because it is the first outlook without the carry-in inventory cushion and the first clean read on the margin ex-refund.

The entry plan follows the evidence rather than the excitement: a starter position only in the lower band, a full position only at the bear-case level, a cap because one regulatory event is worth a tenth of market value, and a trim at the top of the range. The follow-up diligence is the December guide for margin ex-refund, the terms of the first renewal of the search payment, the annual report's refund and inventory split, China revenue against its nine-month base, and Services growth after the US link-out injunction. Confidence is high in the valuation arithmetic, medium in the margin path, and low in any AI revenue forecast, which does not yet exist; the rating does not rest on the precise September range.

Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack is still the widest integrated consumer technology stack, but in 2026 the company rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — so what remains defensible is distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved the iPhone to TSMC N2, the C2 modem reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google announced the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS, about double the prior generation. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9%, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q expects advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints to intensify [S6, S64].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node, A19 Pro / A20 Pro | TSMC N3P (2025) / N2 (2026) | Teardown and trade reporting | S63, S64 |
| Neural Engine, A20 Pro | 32 cores, ~52 TOPS, ~2x A19 Pro | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| N2 wafer price | ~$30,000 vs $18,000-20,000 at 3nm | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| Product gross margin | 39.9% vs 36.9% (9M FY2025) | Reported financials | S6 |
| On-device model / PCC context | ~3B parameters / 32K tokens | Apple research and developer docs | S61, S62 |

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device, Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model with KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; on its servers, a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model runs inside Private Cloud Compute, with stateless processing, no privileged access even for Apple staff, and attested software images. Memory bandwidth and power cap on-device inference at single-digit billions of parameters, so harder queries are offloaded. The disclosed ceiling is a 32K-token context, small against frontier assistants. Where Gemini-derived inference physically runs is unresolved: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on Apple devices and Private Cloud Compute, while trade reporting places the Gemini computation in Google's cloud at a reported ~$1bn a year, alongside a ~$20bn default-search payment. Neither figure is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, nearly two years after its 2024 debut, with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu on a separate model stack. Differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; underwrite the cash flow and installed base, not the AI layer [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

| Dimension | Apple 2024 (AFM v1) | Apple 2026 (Gemini-based AFM) | Google (supplier) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frontier model | Own ~3B on-device plus server model | Gemini-derived | Owns Gemini | S58, S61 |
| Cost structure | Fixed R&D and data-centre capex | Fixed R&D plus per-query licence | Licence revenue | S58, S86 |
| What Apple keeps | Silicon, OS, orchestration | Silicon, OS, interface, orchestration | Model, training, inference | S58, S60 |

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched on 2026-09-09 at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 went on sale on 2026-10-23. iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27, with Greater China up 30%. The C2 modem supports US mmWave and uses 15% less energy than the C1X, but the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max appears to keep a Qualcomm modem, so Qualcomm retains leverage over the highest-ASP SKU. Vision Pro is the counter-example: ~390,000 units in 2024, ~45,000 in the December 2025 quarter despite the M5 refresh, ~600,000 lifetime, and an IDC forecast of ~290,000 in 2026 [S59, S13, S87].

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Commercial | 2026-09 | $196.5bn, 54% of 9M | Products 39.9% | C2 in Pro Max, 2027 | S59, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Commercial | 2026-10-23 | Inside iPhone; undisclosed | Not disclosed | First-quarter volume | S59 |
| Watch Series 11 / Ultra 3 | Commercial | 2025-09 | Wearables $27.3bn, +2% | Not disclosed | Hypertension roll-out | S5, S6 |
| Vision Pro (M5) | Commercial | 2025-10 | ~45k units Q4 2025 | Not disclosed | Lower-cost model, late 2026 | S87 |
| Services | Commercial | — | $91.7bn, +14% | 76.3% | AI tier / iCloud+ gating | S6, S107 |

### What is enforceable is regulatory, not patent

Apple publishes no patent count; the FY2025 10-K says only that it is "pursuing thousands of applications around the world" and that no single right protects its products [S5]. Families and technology-specific grants remain unverified: USPTO Patent Center and EPO Espacenet could not be searched, and an export of 2024-2026 Apple-assigned families in on-device AI, wearable health, foldable hinge and AR optics has been requested. The only cross-company measure retrieved is grants: Apple took 2,722 US patents in 2025, down 11.6% from 3,082 and sixth, against Samsung's 7,054 in first place for a fourth year and Huawei's 3,052 [S211]. In AI filings Apple is absent from the top three worldwide, where Samsung filed 2,162, Huawei 1,822 and Google 1,672 in 2025 [S208] — bounds, not a measurement. What is documented is a regulatory estate — hypertension and sleep-apnoea notifications, a hearing-aid De Novo grant and imaging calibration — each cleared on its own clinical file, a slower but more durable barrier than a patent family.

| Hypertension Notification | K250507 | US FDA | 2025-09-11 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S30 |
| Sleep Apnea Notification | K240929 | US FDA | 2024-09-13 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S33 |
| Hearing Aid Feature | DEN230081 | US FDA | 2024-09-12 | De Novo granted | AirPods | S34 |
| Medical Imaging Calibration | K253582 | US FDA | 2026-04-01 | Cleared 510(k) | Display calibration | S29 |

### The moat is wide at the bottom of the stack and thin at the top

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Benchmark or base rate | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Custom SoC and modem | 8 | Design team plus priority N2 access; no IP credit while family grants are unverified | Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 | 8+ years to parity | S59, S64, S207 |
| Hardware-OS integration | 8 | Six operating systems co-designed with custom silicon | No peer ships a leading-edge phone SoC and its OS at scale | 5-7 years | S5 |
| On-device model efficiency | 5 | Quantisation and KV-cache methods are published | ~3B parameters and 32K context disclosed | 1-2 years | S61 |
| Frontier model | 3 | Available to licence, as Apple has shown | Gemini licence reported at ~$1bn a year | 1-2 years, by cheque | S58 |
| FDA-cleared health features | 7 | Each feature needs its own trial and clearance | Four Apple clearances since 2024; rivals must file separately | 3-4 years | S30, S33, S34 |
| Installed base and developers | 8 | Switching costs and services attach, but not exclusive | Every platform owner holds a multi-billion-device base; monetisation depth, not access, is the barrier | 10+ years | S5 |
| **Composite** | **8/10 hardware, 4/10 AI** | Hard to copy, easy to rent; IP adds no credit | 8+ years for a new entrant; Samsung still buys flagship silicon | — | S58, S64, S207 |

The replication test is now a base rate. Intel bought Infineon's wireless unit for about $1.4bn, closing in Q1 2011, and sold its smartphone modem business to Apple for $1bn, completed 2019-12-02 — roughly nine years without a durable phone-modem position [S206, S210]. Apple started from that purchase, 2,200 engineers and over 17,000 wireless patents, and shipped its first in-house modem, the C1 in the iPhone 16e, in February 2025, just over five years later; in 2026 the largest iPhone still appears to carry Qualcomm [S209, S59]. Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 [S207]. A funded team reaches a first competitive component in about five years; parity in a phone-class SoC plus OS is an eight-to-ten-year proposition, which is why the hardware composite is capped at 8/10 and IP adds nothing. A granted-family count against Samsung and Alphabet would move that number: parity in on-device AI, health, hinge and AR optics would restore the withheld point and take the composite to 9/10; fewer than half Samsung's families in foldables and AR optics would cut those sub-scores and add freedom-to-operate cost, holding it at 8/10 or below. Counter-evidence is Apple's own record: Siri needed a Google licence, the car was cancelled, Vision Pro has not reached platform volumes [S58, S87]. The Q3 FY2026 10-Q adds a regulatory one: DMA interoperability obligations have in the past, and may in future, cause Apple not to launch or maintain features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions [S6]. Two diligence questions remain: whether the Google agreement allows on-device fine-tuning, and whether the 2027 Pro Max moves fully to the C2.

::: evidence
**Apple's integration advantage is durable in silicon and distribution, but it no longer extends to the model layer.**

The A20 Pro's 2nm node and 32-core Neural Engine keep Apple at the leading edge of phone silicon, and its FDA clearances give it a regulated feature estate rivals must replicate filing by filing. But basing the next Apple Foundation Models on Gemini concedes that the frontier layer is bought: the reported ~$1bn licence turns a fixed R&D advantage into a variable cost paid to a competitor, and availability varies by jurisdiction, with China on a Qwen/Baidu stack and DMA rules possibly withholding Siri AI in the EU [S6, S58, S64, S86, S120, S171].
:::

arguments.markdown:
Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack remains the widest integrated consumer stack, but in 2026 Apple rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — leaving distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing as the defensible assets, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved to TSMC N2, the C2 reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google said the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9%, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q expects memory and advanced-node constraints to intensify [S6, S64].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node, A19 Pro / A20 Pro | TSMC N3P (2025) / N2 (2026) | Teardown and trade reporting | S63, S64 |
| Neural Engine, A20 Pro | 32 cores, ~52 TOPS, ~2x A19 Pro | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| N2 wafer price | ~$30,000 vs $18,000-20,000 at 3nm | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| Product gross margin | 39.9% vs 36.9% (9M FY2025) | Reported financials | S6 |
| On-device model / PCC context | ~3B parameters / 32K tokens | Apple research and developer docs | S61, S62 |

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model with KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; server queries go to a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model inside Private Cloud Compute, which enforces stateless processing, no privileged access even for Apple staff, and attested software images. Memory bandwidth and power cap on-device inference at single-digit billions of parameters. The disclosed ceiling is a 32K-token context, small against frontier assistants. Where Gemini-derived inference runs is unresolved: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on its devices and PCC, while trade reporting puts the Gemini computation in Google's cloud at a reported ~$1bn a year, alongside a ~$20bn default-search payment; neither is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, nearly two years after its 2024 debut, with Qwen and Baidu on a separate stack. Differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; underwrite the cash flow and installed base, not the AI layer [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

| Dimension | 2024 (AFM v1) | 2026 (Gemini-based) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model ownership | Own ~3B on-device plus server model | Gemini-derived | S58, S61 |
| Cost | Fixed R&D and data-centre capex | Fixed R&D plus per-query licence | S58, S86 |
| What Apple keeps | Silicon, OS, orchestration | Silicon, OS, interface, orchestration | S58, S60 |

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched on 2026-09-09 at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 went on sale on 2026-10-23. iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27, with Greater China up 30%. The C2 modem supports US mmWave and uses 15% less energy than the C1X, but the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max appears to keep a Qualcomm modem, so Qualcomm retains leverage over the highest-ASP SKU. Vision Pro is the counter-example: ~45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, ~600,000 lifetime, and an IDC forecast of ~290,000 in 2026 [S59, S13, S87].

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Commercial | 2026-09 | $196.5bn, 54% of 9M | Products 39.9% | C2 in Pro Max, 2027 | S59, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Commercial | 2026-10-23 | Inside iPhone; undisclosed | Not disclosed | First-quarter volume | S59 |
| Watch Series 11 / Ultra 3 | Commercial | 2025-09 | Wearables $27.3bn, +2% | Not disclosed | Hypertension roll-out | S5, S6 |
| Vision Pro (M5) | Commercial | 2025-10 | ~45k units Q4 2025 | Not disclosed | Lower-cost model, late 2026 | S87 |
| Services | Commercial | — | $91.7bn, +14% | 76.3% | AI tier / iCloud+ gating | S6, S107 |

### What is enforceable is regulatory, not patent

Apple publishes no patent count; the FY2025 10-K says only that it is "pursuing thousands of applications around the world" and that no single right protects its products [S5]. Families and technology-specific grants remain unverified — USPTO Patent Center and EPO Espacenet could not be searched, and an export of 2024-2026 Apple-assigned families in on-device AI, wearable health, foldable hinge and AR optics has been requested. The only cross-company measure retrieved is grants: Apple took 2,722 US patents in 2025, down 11.6% and sixth, against Samsung's 7,054 in first place for a fourth year [S211]; in AI filings Apple is absent from the top three, where Samsung filed 2,162, Huawei 1,822 and Google 1,672 in 2025 [S208]. That bounds the portfolio without measuring it. What is documented is a regulatory estate — hypertension and sleep-apnoea notifications, a hearing-aid De Novo grant and imaging calibration — each cleared on its own clinical file, a slower but more durable barrier than a patent family.

| Asset | Identifier | Jurisdiction | Date | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent portfolio | Count not disclosed | US and foreign | Ongoing | "Thousands of applications"; families and grants unverified | US grants 2,722 in 2025 vs Samsung 7,054; family count missing | S5, S208, S211 |
| Hypertension Notification | K250507 | US FDA | 2025-09-11 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S30 |
| Sleep Apnea Notification | K240929 | US FDA | 2024-09-13 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S33 |
| Hearing Aid Feature | DEN230081 | US FDA | 2024-09-12 | De Novo granted | AirPods | S34 |
| Medical Imaging Calibration | K253582 | US FDA | 2026-04-01 | Cleared 510(k) | Display calibration | S29 |

### The moat is wide at the bottom of the stack and thin at the top

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Benchmark or base rate | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Custom SoC and modem | 8 | Design team plus priority N2 access; no IP credit while family grants are unverified | Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 | 8+ years to parity | S59, S64, S207 |
| Hardware-OS integration | 8 | Six operating systems co-designed with custom silicon | No peer ships a leading-edge phone SoC and its OS at scale | 5-7 years | S5 |
| On-device model efficiency | 5 | Quantisation and KV-cache methods are published | ~3B parameters and 32K context disclosed | 1-2 years | S61 |
| Frontier model | 3 | Available to licence, as Apple has shown | Gemini licence reported at ~$1bn a year | 1-2 years, by cheque | S58 |
| FDA-cleared health features | 7 | Each feature needs its own trial and clearance | Four Apple clearances since 2024; rivals must file separately | 3-4 years | S30, S33, S34 |
| Installed base and developers | 8 | Switching costs and services attach, but not exclusive | Every platform owner holds a multi-billion-device base; monetisation depth, not access, is the barrier | 10+ years | S5 |
| **Composite** | **8/10 hardware, 4/10 AI** | Hard to copy, easy to rent; IP adds no credit | 8+ years for a new entrant; Samsung still buys flagship silicon | — | S58, S64, S207 |

The replication test is a base rate. Intel bought Infineon's wireless unit for about $1.4bn, closing in Q1 2011, and sold its smartphone modem business to Apple for $1bn, completed 2019-12-02 — nine years without a durable phone-modem position [S206, S210]. Apple started from that purchase, 2,200 engineers and over 17,000 wireless patents, and shipped the C1 in the iPhone 16e in February 2025, just over five years later; in 2026 the largest iPhone still appears to carry Qualcomm [S209, S59]. Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 [S207]. First competitive components take about five years; parity in a phone-class SoC plus OS takes eight to ten, which is why the hardware composite is capped at 8/10 and IP adds nothing. A granted-family count against Samsung and Alphabet would move that number: parity in on-device AI, health, hinge and AR optics would restore the withheld point, taking the composite to 9/10; fewer than half Samsung's families in foldables and AR optics would cut those sub-scores and add freedom-to-operate cost, holding it at 8/10 or below. Counter-evidence is Apple's own record: Siri needed a Google licence, the car was cancelled, Vision Pro has not reached platform volumes [S58, S87]. The 10-Q adds a regulatory one: DMA interoperability obligations have in the past, and may in future, cause Apple not to launch or maintain features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions [S6]. Two diligence questions remain: whether the Google agreement allows on-device fine-tuning, and whether the 2027 Pro Max moves fully to the C2.

::: evidence
**Apple's integration advantage is durable in silicon and distribution, but it no longer extends to the model layer.**

The A20 Pro's 2nm node and 32-core Neural Engine keep Apple at the leading edge of phone silicon, and its FDA clearances give it a regulated feature estate rivals must replicate filing by filing. But basing the next Apple Foundation Models on Gemini concedes that the frontier layer is bought: the reported ~$1bn licence turns a fixed R&D advantage into a variable cost paid to a competitor, and availability varies by jurisdiction, with China on a Qwen/Baidu stack and DMA rules possibly withholding Siri AI in the EU [S6, S58, S64, S86, S120, S171].
:::

arguments.markdown:
Apple's exit is the market, not a buyer, and at $344.63 the margin-adjusted 15/50/35 case is worth $266, 23% below the close, so the discipline is a $240-265 starter, a full position at or below $225 and a trim at $395. At a $5,029.6B market value the largest technology acquisition on record, Microsoft's $68.7B all-cash purchase of Activision Blizzard agreed on 2022-01-18, equals 1.4% of the company, and any bid would face the US and EU antitrust review that Microsoft's own deal attracted; a leveraged buyout of a $4.97T enterprise value is arithmetically impossible. The exit is a sale into the market: a 1% position in a $1B fund is $10M, 0.07% of the $13.84B average daily traded value. [S9, S169, S154]

| Exit route | Named buyer or venue | Rationale | Timing | Likelihood | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open-market sale | NasdaqGS, $13.84B average daily traded value | The only route that absorbs a position without a discount | Any trading day | The route actually used | S9 |
| Strategic acquisition | No named buyer; largest technology deal $68.7B vs $5,029.6B market value | Size, antitrust, no strategic gap Apple fills | Not foreseeable | Very low | S169 |
| Leveraged buyout | None | $4.97T enterprise value and $84.3B of debt cannot be financed | Not foreseeable | Negligible | S6 |
| Company buyback (partial exit) | Apple Inc. | $100B authorised on 2025-05-01 and a further $100B on 2026-04-30; $61.8B repurchased in the nine months to 2026-06-27, 1.6% of shares a year | Ongoing | High but discretionary | S204, S205, S6 |
| Dividend | Apple Inc. | $0.27 a quarter, 0.31% yield, declared 2026-07-30 | Quarterly | Certain while declared | S13 |
| Index and passive flows | S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 constituent | Structural bid, not an exit route | Ongoing | Structural | S163 |

Apple's own record sets the cost of ownership. Over the last ten completed years the average intra-year peak-to-trough drawdown was 21.4%, lasting 82 days, and four episodes exceeded 30%: 2018 fell 36.73%, 2020 31.43%, 2022 30.75% and 2025 30.22%. Each recovered — 2020 returned 80.75% for the calendar year and 2025 8.56% — but each recovery came with a re-rating as well as earnings growth, and a buyer at 38.9x cannot count on the re-rating half. From $344.63 the average drawdown is $271 and a 30% drawdown is $240. On 2026-10-30 Apple was 1.23% below its high while the Nasdaq-100 was 9.09% below its own and the S&P 500 3.05%, so the stock enters any correction from relative strength. [S163, S168]

| Precedent episode | Peak | Trough | Drawdown | Days | Equivalent price from $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | $58.02 (2018-10-03) | $36.71 (2018-12-24) | -36.73% | 82 | $218 | S163 |
| 2020 | $81.80 (2020-02-12) | $56.09 (2020-03-23) | -31.43% | 40 | $236 | S163 |
| 2022 | $182.01 (2022-01-03) | $126.04 (2022-12-28) | -30.75% | 359 | $239 | S163 |
| 2025 | $247.10 (2025-02-24) | $172.42 (2025-04-08) | -30.22% | 43 | $240 | S163 |
| Ten-year average | - | - | -21.39% | 82 | $271 | S163 |

The multiple, not the remembered share price, is what made past entries work. The 2022 trough of $126.04 on 2022-12-28 was 20.6x fiscal 2022 diluted EPS of $6.11; a repeat of that multiple on the margin-adjusted $8.87 would be $183, below the bear case. The base case is not a bear forecast: it takes the team's margin-adjusted EPS of $8.87 — the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin included 2 points of tariff refunds and its $2.02 EPS included $0.11, and two points of give-back on $490B of fiscal 2027 revenue is $9.8B of pretax profit — and applies 30.2x, the five-year average. That is $268. The bear applies 25x to $8.20, or $205; the bull applies 38x to $10.50, or $399. Weighted 15% bull, 50% base and 35% bear, the value is $266, 23% below the close. [S13, S6, S154]

| Scenario | Probability | EPS | Multiple | Value | Versus $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 15% | $10.50 | 38.0x | $399 | +16% | S13, S154 |
| Base | 50% | $8.87 | 30.2x | $268 | -22% | S13, S6, S154 |
| Bear | 35% | $8.20 | 25.0x | $205 | -41% | S6, S118 |
| Probability-weighted | 100% | - | - | $266 | -23% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |

The mechanism is arithmetic: the fund is paid by the exit multiple times EPS growth plus the dividend, so the entry price sets the return. A long-only fund should underwrite a three-to-five-year hold, the period over which the Services annuity and the installed base can compound enough to absorb a de-rating. On the margin-adjusted $8.87 growing 8% a year to $11.17 by fiscal 2029 and $3.37 of cumulative dividends, the annual total return depends almost entirely on the exit multiple, and the entry price decides whether the fund is paid for waiting. At $344.63 a 25x exit loses 6.4% a year and a 35x exit earns 4.6%; at $265 the same exits earn 2.2% and 14.2%; at $225 they earn 7.9% and 20.6%. An 8% return at today's price needs an exit multiple of 38.6x, above the 38x bull case; at $225 it needs 25.1x, essentially the bear multiple. [S154, S157]

| Entry price | Implied P/E on $8.87 | 3-year annual return at exit 25x | At exit 30x | At exit 35x | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $344.63 | 38.9x | -6.4% | -0.6% | +4.6% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |
| $265 | 29.9x | +2.2% | +8.5% | +14.2% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |
| $240 | 27.1x | +5.6% | +12.2% | +18.0% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |
| $225 | 25.4x | +7.9% | +14.6% | +20.6% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |

The policy tests are narrow for a US holder: no foreign-buyer limit on a share sale, no lock-up, and no venue constraint at NasdaqGS, the S&P 500 or the Nasdaq-100. The binding policy risk sits in the asset, not the exit. The Google search payment, reported at $20B in 2022 and never disclosed by Apple, is on today's base 17% of trailing Services revenue of $120.5B and 22% of services gross profit of $91.6B, and it survived the D.D.C.'s remedies decision of 2025-09-02, which refused the DOJ's near-total ban on distribution payments and permitted non-exclusive default-placement deals of one year or less. Final judgment followed in December 2025, Google appealed in January 2026 and the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026; the appeals were pending at 2026-10-29. The payment continues on non-exclusive, annually renegotiated terms; the event that would force a sale is its loss or material cut at a renewal or on appeal, not a ban in force. $20B of near-pure-margin revenue taxed at 21% is $15.8B of earnings, and at 30x that is $474B, 9.4% of the $5,029.6B market value. Slower policy risks are DMA and DOJ commission rules, and China, where revenue was $64.8B in nine months of fiscal 2026 and can turn on policy rather than execution. At 38.9x margin-adjusted earnings there is no cushion for a services margin shock. [S118, S42, S82, S13]

The strongest case against this discipline is that a 30x-plus multiple never offers a margin of safety again. The stock has averaged 30.2x over five years, and its five-year range of 22.1-40.6x shows a 25x entry is not exotic; if Services compounds at 14% on a 76% gross margin and the buyback retires 1.6% of the shares a year, a fund that waits for $225 may never own the best cash generator in the market, and the cost of the discipline is opportunity rather than loss. The answer is a time rule rather than a permanent price target: if Apple trades above $268 for four consecutive quarters while Services growth stays above 10%, reassess the band against the then-current multiple instead of waiting for a level the business has outgrown. Until then, watchlist above $268, a 1-2% starter at $240-265, a full 3-4% position at or below $225 and a trim to half at or above $395. Confidence is high in the drawdown record and the return arithmetic, medium in the exit multiple, which depends on the ten-year yield of 4.93% on 2026-10-30. The diligence questions are the first one-year renewal of the Google payment, the June margin without the 2 points of tariff refund, and whether the 2026-11-02 release confirms the 47-48% September guide. [S154, S157]

| Sell and entry trigger | Threshold | Action | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valuation: trim | At or above $395 (37.6x bull EPS; 44.5x base EPS) | Trim to half | S154, S13 |
| Valuation: add | At or below $225 (25.4x base EPS; 10% above the $205 bear) | Add to a full 3-4% position | S154, S6 |
| Valuation: starter | $240-265 (27.1-29.9x) | Open a 1-2% starter | S154, S6 |
| Thesis break: Services | Services revenue growth below 5% year on year for two quarters | Sell | S13 |
| Thesis break: margin | Gross margin below 45% ex-refund for two quarters | Sell | S13, S6 |
| Thesis break: search payment | Payment lost or materially cut at the one-year renewal, or on appeal, without an offsetting services gain | Sell or halve | S118, S42 |
| Thesis break: China | Greater China revenue down 10% year on year | Reassess, then sell | S13 |

arguments.markdown:
Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack remains the widest integrated consumer stack, but in 2026 Apple rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — leaving distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing as the defensible assets, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved to TSMC N2, the C2 reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google said the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9%, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q expects memory and advanced-node constraints to intensify [S6, S64].

| Node, A19 Pro / A20 Pro | TSMC N3P (2025) / N2 (2026) | Trade reporting | S63, S64 |
| Neural Engine, A20 Pro | 32 cores, ~52 TOPS, ~2x A19 Pro | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| N2 wafer price | ~$30,000 vs $18,000-20,000 at 3nm | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| Product gross margin | 39.9% vs 36.9% (9M FY2025) | Reported financials | S6 |
| On-device model / PCC context | ~3B parameters / 32K tokens | Apple research and docs | S61, S62 |

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model with KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; server queries go to a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model inside Private Cloud Compute, which enforces stateless processing, no privileged access even for Apple staff, and attested software images. Memory bandwidth caps on-device inference at a few billion parameters, so harder queries are offloaded. Where Gemini-derived inference runs is unresolved: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on its devices and PCC, while trade reporting puts the Gemini computation in Google's cloud at a reported ~$1bn a year, alongside a ~$20bn default-search payment; neither is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, nearly two years after its 2024 debut, with Qwen and Baidu on a separate stack. Differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; underwrite the cash flow and installed base, not the AI layer [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

| Dimension | 2024 (AFM v1) | 2026 (Gemini-based) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model ownership | Own ~3B on-device plus server model | Gemini-derived | S58, S61 |
| Cost | Fixed R&D and capex | Fixed R&D plus per-query licence | S58, S86 |

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched on 2026-09-09 at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 went on sale on 2026-10-23. iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27, with Greater China up 30%. The C2 modem supports US mmWave and uses 15% less energy than the C1X, but the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max appears to keep a Qualcomm modem, so Qualcomm retains leverage over the highest-ASP SKU. Vision Pro is the counter-example: ~45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, ~600,000 lifetime, and an IDC forecast of ~290,000 in 2026 [S59, S13, S87].

### What is enforceable is regulatory, not patent

Apple publishes no patent count; the FY2025 10-K says only that it is "pursuing thousands of applications around the world" and that no single right protects its products [S5]. Families and technology-specific grants remain unverified: USPTO Patent Center and EPO Espacenet could not be searched, and an export of 2024-2026 Apple-assigned families in on-device AI, wearable health, foldable hinge and AR optics has been requested. The only cross-company measure retrieved is grants: Apple took 2,722 US patents in 2025, down 11.6% and sixth, against Samsung's 7,054 in first place for a fourth year [S211]; in AI filings Apple is absent from the top three, where Samsung filed 2,162, Huawei 1,822 and Google 1,672 in 2025 [S208]. What is documented is a regulatory estate — hypertension and sleep-apnoea notifications, a hearing-aid De Novo grant and imaging calibration — each cleared on its own clinical file, a slower but more durable barrier than a patent family.

### The moat is wide at the bottom of the stack and thin at the top

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Benchmark or base rate | Time to replicate | Source |

| Custom SoC and modem | 8 | Design team plus priority N2 access; no IP credit while family grants are unverified | Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 | 8+ years to parity | S59, S64, S207 |
| Hardware-OS integration | 8 | Six operating systems co-designed with custom silicon | No peer ships a leading-edge phone SoC and its OS at scale | 5-7 years | S5 |
| On-device model efficiency | 5 | Quantisation and KV-cache methods are published | ~3B parameters and 32K context disclosed | 1-2 years | S61 |
| Frontier model | 3 | Available to licence, as Apple has shown | Gemini licence reported at ~$1bn a year | 1-2 years, by cheque | S58 |
| FDA-cleared health features | 7 | Each feature needs its own trial and clearance | Four Apple clearances since 2024; rivals must file separately | 3-4 years | S30, S33, S34 |
| Installed base and developers | 8 | Switching costs and services attach, but not exclusive | Every platform owner holds a multi-billion-device base; monetisation depth, not access, is the barrier | 10+ years | S5 |
| **Composite** | **8/10 hardware, 4/10 AI** | Hard to copy, easy to rent; IP adds no credit | 8+ years for a new entrant; Samsung still buys flagship silicon | — | S58, S64, S207 |

The replication test is a base rate. Intel bought Infineon's wireless unit for about $1.4bn, closing in Q1 2011, and sold its smartphone modem business to Apple for $1bn, completed 2019-12-02 — nine years without a durable phone-modem position [S206, S210]. Apple started from that purchase, 2,200 engineers and over 17,000 wireless patents, and shipped the C1 in the iPhone 16e in February 2025, just over five years later; in 2026 the largest iPhone still appears to carry Qualcomm [S209, S59]. Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 [S207]. First competitive components take about five years; parity takes eight to ten, which is why the hardware composite is capped at 8/10 and IP adds nothing. A granted-family count against Samsung and Alphabet would move that number: parity in on-device AI, health, hinge and AR optics would restore the withheld point, taking the composite to 9/10; fewer than half Samsung's families in foldables and AR optics would cut those sub-scores and add freedom-to-operate cost, holding it at 8/10 or below. Counter-evidence is Apple's own record: Siri needed a Google licence, the car was cancelled, Vision Pro has not reached platform volumes [S58, S87]. The 10-Q adds a regulatory one: DMA interoperability obligations may cause Apple not to launch features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions [S6]. Diligence: does the Google agreement allow on-device fine-tuning, and does the 2027 Pro Max move fully to the C2?

::: evidence
**Apple's integration advantage is durable in silicon and distribution, but it no longer extends to the model layer.**

The A20 Pro's 2nm node and 32-core Neural Engine keep Apple at the leading edge of phone silicon, and its FDA clearances give it a regulated feature estate rivals must replicate filing by filing. But basing the next Apple Foundation Models on Gemini concedes that the frontier layer is bought: the reported ~$1bn licence turns a fixed R&D advantage into a variable cost paid to a competitor, and availability varies by jurisdiction, with China on a Qwen/Baidu stack and DMA rules possibly withholding Siri AI in the EU [S6, S58, S64, S86, S120, S171].

arguments.markdown:
Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack remains the widest integrated consumer stack, but in 2026 Apple rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — leaving distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing as the defensible assets, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved to TSMC N2, the C2 reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google said the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9%, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q expects memory and advanced-node constraints to intensify [S6, S64].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node, A19 Pro / A20 Pro | TSMC N3P (2025) / N2 (2026) | Trade reporting | S63, S64 |
| Neural Engine, A20 Pro | 32 cores, ~52 TOPS, ~2x A19 Pro | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| N2 wafer price | ~$30,000 vs $18,000-20,000 at 3nm | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| On-device model / PCC context | ~3B parameters / 32K tokens | Apple research and docs | S61, S62 |

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model with KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; server queries go to a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model inside Private Cloud Compute, which enforces stateless processing, no privileged access and attested software images. Memory bandwidth caps on-device inference at a few billion parameters, so harder queries are offloaded. Where Gemini-derived inference runs is unresolved: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on its devices and PCC, while trade reporting puts the Gemini computation in Google's cloud at a reported ~$1bn a year, alongside a ~$20bn default-search payment; neither is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, nearly two years after its 2024 debut, with Qwen and Baidu on a separate stack. Differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; underwrite the cash flow and installed base, not the AI layer [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

| Dimension | 2024 (AFM v1) | 2026 (Gemini-based) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model ownership | Own ~3B on-device plus server model | Gemini-derived | S58, S61 |
| Cost | Fixed R&D and capex | Fixed R&D plus per-query licence | S58, S86 |

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched on 2026-09-09 at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 went on sale on 2026-10-23. iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27, with Greater China up 30%. The C2 modem supports US mmWave and uses 15% less energy than the C1X, but the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max appears to keep a Qualcomm modem, so Qualcomm retains leverage over the highest-ASP SKU. Vision Pro is the counter-example: ~45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, ~600,000 lifetime, and an IDC forecast of ~290,000 in 2026 [S59, S13, S87].

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Commercial | 2026-09 | $196.5bn, 54% of 9M | 39.9% products | C2 in Pro Max, 2027 | S59, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Commercial | 2026-10-23 | In iPhone; undisclosed | Not disclosed | First-quarter volume | S59 |
| Watch Series 11 / Ultra 3 | Commercial | 2025-09 | Wearables $27.3bn, +2% | Not disclosed | Hypertension roll-out | S5, S6 |
| Services | Commercial | — | $91.7bn, +14% | 76.3% | AI tier / iCloud+ gating | S6, S107 |

### What is enforceable is regulatory, not patent

Apple publishes no patent count; the FY2025 10-K says only that it is "pursuing thousands of applications around the world" and that no single right protects its products [S5]. Families and technology-specific grants remain unverified: USPTO Patent Center and EPO Espacenet could not be searched, and an export of 2024-2026 Apple-assigned families in on-device AI, wearable health, foldable hinge and AR optics has been requested. The only cross-company measure retrieved is grants: Apple took 2,722 US patents in 2025, down 11.6% and sixth, against Samsung's 7,054 in first place for a fourth year [S211]; in AI filings Apple is absent from the top three, where Samsung filed 2,162, Huawei 1,822 and Google 1,672 in 2025 [S208]. What is documented is a regulatory estate — hypertension and sleep-apnoea notifications, a hearing-aid De Novo grant and imaging calibration — each cleared on its own clinical file, a slower but more durable barrier than a patent family.

| Asset | Identifier | Jurisdiction | Date | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent portfolio | Count not disclosed | US and foreign | Ongoing | "Thousands of applications"; families and grants unverified | US grants 2,722 in 2025 vs Samsung 7,054; family count missing | S5, S208, S211 |
| Hypertension Notification | K250507 | US FDA | 2025-09-11 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S30 |
| Sleep Apnea Notification | K240929 | US FDA | 2024-09-13 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S33 |
| Hearing Aid Feature | DEN230081 | US FDA | 2024-09-12 | De Novo granted | AirPods | S34 |
| Medical Imaging Calibration | K253582 | US FDA | 2026-04-01 | Cleared 510(k) | Display calibration | S29 |

### The moat is wide at the bottom of the stack and thin at the top

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Benchmark or base rate | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Custom SoC and modem | 8 | Design team plus priority N2 access; no IP credit while family grants are unverified | Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 | 8+ years to parity | S59, S64, S207 |
| Hardware-OS integration | 8 | Six operating systems co-designed with custom silicon | No peer ships a leading-edge phone SoC and its OS at scale | 5-7 years | S5 |
| On-device model efficiency | 5 | Quantisation and KV-cache methods are published | ~3B parameters and 32K context disclosed | 1-2 years | S61 |
| Frontier model | 3 | Available to licence, as Apple has shown | Gemini licence reported at ~$1bn a year | 1-2 years, by cheque | S58 |
| FDA-cleared health features | 7 | Each feature needs its own trial and clearance | Four Apple clearances since 2024; rivals must file separately | 3-4 years | S30, S33, S34 |
| Installed base and developers | 8 | Switching costs and services attach, but not exclusive | Every platform owner holds a multi-billion-device base; monetisation depth, not access, is the barrier | 10+ years | S5 |
| **Composite** | **8/10 hardware, 4/10 AI** | Hard to copy, easy to rent; IP adds no credit | 8+ years for a new entrant; Samsung still buys flagship silicon | — | S58, S64, S207 |

The replication test is a base rate. Intel bought Infineon's wireless unit for about $1.4bn, closing in Q1 2011, and sold its smartphone modem business to Apple for $1bn, completed 2019-12-02 — nine years without a durable phone-modem position [S206, S210]. Apple started from that purchase, 2,200 engineers and over 17,000 wireless patents, and shipped the C1 in the iPhone 16e in February 2025, just over five years later; in 2026 the largest iPhone still appears to carry Qualcomm [S209, S59]. Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 [S207]. Parity takes eight to ten years, which is why the composite is capped at 8/10 with no IP credit. A granted-family count against Samsung and Alphabet would move it: parity in on-device AI, health, hinge and AR optics would restore the withheld point, taking the composite to 9/10; fewer than half Samsung's families in foldables and AR optics would cut those sub-scores and add freedom-to-operate cost, holding it at 8/10 or below. Counter-evidence: Siri needed a Google licence, the car was cancelled, Vision Pro never reached platform volumes [S58, S87]. The 10-Q warns DMA rules may stop Apple launching features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions [S6]. Diligence: does the Google agreement allow on-device fine-tuning, and does the 2027 Pro Max move fully to the C2?

::: evidence
**Apple's integration advantage is durable in silicon and distribution, but it no longer extends to the model layer.**

The A20 Pro's 2nm node and 32-core Neural Engine keep Apple at the leading edge of phone silicon, and its FDA clearances give it a regulated feature estate rivals must replicate filing by filing. But basing the next Apple Foundation Models on Gemini concedes that the frontier layer is bought: the reported ~$1bn licence turns a fixed R&D advantage into a variable cost paid to a competitor, and availability varies by jurisdiction, with China on a Qwen/Baidu stack and DMA rules possibly withholding Siri AI in the EU [S6, S58, S64, S86, S120, S171].
:::
