arguments.markdown:
Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack is the widest integrated consumer stack, but in 2026 Apple rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — leaving distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing as the defensible assets, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved to TSMC N2, the C2 reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google said the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9%, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q expects memory and node constraints to worsen [S6, S64].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node, A19 Pro / A20 Pro | TSMC N3P (2025) / N2 (2026) | Trade reporting | S63, S64 |
| Neural Engine, A20 Pro | 32 cores, ~52 TOPS, ~2x A19 Pro | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| N2 wafer price | ~$30,000 vs $18,000-20,000 at 3nm | Trade-press estimate | S64 |
| On-device model / PCC context | ~3B parameters / 32K tokens | Apple research and docs | S61, S62 |

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model with KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; server queries go to a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model inside Private Cloud Compute, with stateless processing, no privileged access and attested images. Memory bandwidth caps on-device inference at a few billion parameters; harder queries are offloaded. Where Gemini-derived inference runs is unresolved: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on its devices and PCC, while trade reporting puts the Gemini computation in Google's cloud at a reported ~$1bn a year; neither is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, with Qwen and Baidu on a separate stack. Differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; so a fixed-R&D moat becomes a cost that scales with usage: rented intelligence pays only if it lifts upgrades or carries a subscription [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

| Dimension | Apple 2024 (AFM v1) | Apple 2026 (Gemini-based) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model ownership | Own ~3B on-device plus server model | Gemini-derived | S58, S61 |
| Cost | Fixed R&D and capex | Fixed R&D plus per-query licence | S58, S86 |
| What Apple keeps | Silicon, OS, orchestration | Silicon, OS, interface, orchestration | S58, S60 |

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched on 2026-09-09 at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 went on sale on 2026-10-23. iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27, with Greater China up 30%. The C2 supports US mmWave and uses 15% less energy than the C1X, but the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max appears to keep a Qualcomm modem, so Qualcomm keeps the top-SKU leverage. Vision Pro is the counter-example: ~45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, ~600,000 lifetime, IDC forecasting ~290,000 in 2026 [S59, S13, S87].

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Commercial | 2026-09 | $196.5bn, 54% of 9M | 39.9% products | C2 in Pro Max, 2027 | S59, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Commercial | 2026-10-23 | In iPhone; undisclosed | Not disclosed | First-quarter volume | S59 |
| Watch Series 11 / Ultra 3 | Commercial | 2025-09 | Wearables $27.3bn, +2% | Not disclosed | Hypertension roll-out | S5, S6 |
| Services | Commercial | — | $91.7bn, +14% | 76.3% | AI tier / iCloud+ gating | S6, S107 |

### What is enforceable is regulatory, not patent

Apple publishes no patent count; the FY2025 10-K says only that it is "pursuing thousands of applications around the world" and that no single right protects its products. Families and technology-specific grants remain unverified — no patent number could be checked, because USPTO Patent Center and EPO Espacenet could not be searched — and an export of 2024-2026 Apple-assigned families in on-device AI, health, foldable hinge and AR optics has been requested. The only cross-company measure retrieved is annual US grants, in the table below, where Apple trails Samsung and Huawei and has fallen year on year. The enforceable estate is regulatory: the four FDA clearances below.

| Asset | Identifier | Jurisdiction | Date | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent portfolio | Count not disclosed | US and foreign | Ongoing | "Thousands of applications"; families and grants unverified | US grants 2,722 vs 7,054 Samsung; AI filings 2,162 Samsung, 1,822 Huawei, 1,672 Google; family count missing | S5, S208, S211 |
| Hypertension Notification | K250507 | US FDA | 2025-09-11 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S30 |
| Sleep Apnea Notification | K240929 | US FDA | 2024-09-13 | Cleared 510(k) | Watch sensing | S33 |
| Hearing Aid Feature | DEN230081 | US FDA | 2024-09-12 | De Novo granted | AirPods | S34 |
| Medical Imaging Calibration | K253582 | US FDA | 2026-04-01 | Cleared 510(k) | Display calibration | S29 |

### The moat is wide at the bottom of the stack and thin at the top

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Benchmark or base rate | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Custom SoC and modem | 8 | Design team plus N2 access; no IP credit while family grants are unverified | Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025 | 8+ years to parity | S59, S64, S207 |
| Hardware-OS integration | 8 | Six operating systems co-designed with custom silicon | No peer ships a leading-edge phone SoC and its OS at scale | 5-7 years | S5 |
| On-device model efficiency | 5 | Quantisation and KV-cache methods are published | ~3B parameters and 32K context disclosed | 1-2 years | S61 |
| Frontier model | 3 | Available to licence, as Apple has shown | Gemini licence reported at ~$1bn a year | 1-2 years, by cheque | S58 |
| FDA-cleared health features | 7 | Each feature needs its own trial and clearance | Four Apple clearances since 2024; rivals must file separately | 3-4 years | S30, S33, S34 |
| Installed base and developers | 8 | Switching costs and services attach, but not exclusive | Every platform owner holds a multi-billion-device base; monetisation depth is the barrier | 10+ years | S5 |
| **Composite** | **8/10 hardware, 4/10 AI** | Hard to copy, easy to rent; IP adds no credit | 8+ years for a new entrant; Samsung still buys flagship silicon | — | S58, S64, S207 |

The replication test is a base rate. Intel bought Infineon's wireless unit for ~$1.4bn in 2011 and sold its modem business to Apple for $1bn in 2019 — nine years without a durable phone-modem position. Apple started from that purchase, 2,200 engineers and over 17,000 wireless patents, and shipped the C1 in the iPhone 16e in February 2025, just over five years later; in 2026 the largest iPhone still appears to carry Qualcomm. Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025. Parity takes eight to ten years, which is why the composite is capped at 8/10 with no IP credit. A granted-family count against Samsung and Alphabet would move it: parity in on-device AI, health, hinge and AR optics would restore the withheld point (9/10); fewer than half Samsung's families in foldables and AR optics would cut those sub-scores and add freedom-to-operate cost, holding 8/10 or below. Counter-evidence: Siri needed a Google licence, the car was cancelled, Vision Pro never reached platform volumes. The 10-Q warns DMA rules may stop Apple launching features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions. Diligence: does the Google deal allow on-device fine-tuning, and does the 2027 Pro Max move fully to the C2? [S6, S58, S59, S87, S206, S207, S209, S210]

::: evidence
**Apple's integration advantage is durable in silicon and distribution, but it no longer extends to the model layer.**

The A20 Pro's 2nm node and 32-core Neural Engine keep Apple at the leading edge, and its FDA clearances give it a regulated estate. But basing the next Apple Foundation Models on Gemini concedes that the frontier layer is bought: the reported ~$1bn licence turns a fixed R&D advantage into a variable cost paid to a competitor, and availability varies by jurisdiction, with China on a Qwen/Baidu stack and DMA rules possibly withholding Siri AI in the EU [S6, S58, S64, S86, S120, S171].
:::

The base is large and still growing: revenue reached $416.2bn in FY2025, and the nine months to 2026-06-27 produced $364.4bn, up 16%, with Services at $91.7bn, up 14% [S77, S6].

### Services carry the margin, but the mix engine stalled in FY2026

Services were 26% of FY2025 revenue but 39% of gross profit in the nine months to June 2026, because they earn a 76.3% gross margin against 39.9% for products. The mix engine, however, stopped being the marginal driver: product gross profit grew 26% against 15% for services, so the rise in total gross margin to 49.1% from 46.8% came from hardware mix and tariff refunds, not from services, while memory costs kept rising. Services growth itself came from advertising and cloud services, with the Google search-distribution payment named as a primary driver. That is the engine that funds the buyback and the silicon, and it is also the engine regulators are targeting: the European Commission fined Apple €500m on 2025-04-23 for anti-steering non-compliance, and the General Court dismissed Apple's challenge to its gatekeeper designation on 2026-07-08 [S85, S84, S6]. An investor should value the services annuity on gross profit that compounds in the low-to-mid teens, and apply a discount for the probability that a remedy compresses commission or search income rather than a one-off fine.

### AI is funded as cost and monetised, if at all, through storage

Apple introduced Siri AI with the iOS 27 cycle announced in the third quarter of FY2026, and R&D rose 33% to $34.0bn in the nine months to June 2026, driven by infrastructure including AI investments and headcount. No AI revenue line exists. Availability is a regulatory variable too: China cleared Apple Intelligence only on 2026-07-15, with Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, and the 10-Q warns that DMA rules have in the past, and may in future, cause it not to launch features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions. The reported plan — that high-frequency, compute-intensive Siri use will be gated behind iCloud+ — is plausible because it reuses a price ladder already in place, but Apple has published no tier and no price, so it is unverified [S13, S6, S107, S171]. The mechanism matters more than the price: AI raises the cost of serving every device while its clearest commercial effect is to protect upgrade rates and services attach. If Apple charges, the increment is bounded by storage-subscription willingness to pay, not by the value of the model; if it does not, AI is a permanent tax on gross margin. Either way, 2027 is the test of whether AI spend converts into units or ARPU.

### India lowers tariff risk, not unit cost

iPhone production in India rose 53% in 2025 to ~55 million units, ~25% of global output, and is projected at 28% in 2026; Tata Electronics overtook Foxconn in iPhone export assembly over the FY2022-FY2026 incentive period. The strategy is rational given the tariff record in the filings — Section 232 semiconductor investigation results in January 2026, the Supreme Court striking down certain IEEPA tariffs in February 2026, and new Section 301 tariffs, with manufacturing purchase obligations of $57.0bn at 2026-06-27 [S89, S91, S6]. The limit is that assembly captures little of the value: components, displays and silicon still come from East Asia, so India is an insurance policy on tariffs and single-country concentration, not a margin lever. The signpost to watch is the share of US-bound iPhones assembled in India, which Apple has never disclosed.

### Capital allocation is disciplined and slightly bolder

R&D rose from $29.9bn in FY2023 to $34.6bn in FY2025 and is running at ~$45bn annualised in FY2026. Buybacks remain the primary use of cash: $25.8bn of stock was repurchased in the quarter to 2026-06-27 alone, alongside $4.0bn of dividends at $0.27 per share, which cut the share count to 14.61bn from 14.77bn at FY2025 year-end and helped EPS grow 29% against 27% net-income growth. M&A posture has shifted from tuck-ins: Apple confirmed the acquisition of the AI-audio start-up Q.ai on 2026-01-29, reported by the Financial Times at close to $2bn, and acquired the AI data-engineering company Ascend.io, notified to the European Commission on 2026-06-30; intangible assets rose from $11.1bn to $20.3bn between 2025-09-27 and 2026-06-27 [S77, S88, S6, S13]. Against ~$146bn of cash and marketable securities, that is affordable experimentation rather than a change of strategy — and it is the right test of whether Apple's AI gap can be bought in pieces.

Fourth, India must reach the projected share of output without a quality or logistics incident. Apple's answer is that it does not need to be first — it needs to be best integrated, and it monetises the installed base rather than the model. That is a defensible strategy for a cash-flow investor and a weak one for anyone buying AI optionality [S59, S87, S84, S90, S89].

arguments.markdown:
Apple's markets are contracting in units and expanding in value, and Apple is taking value share inside that contraction: the case for FY2026-FY2028 rests on premiumisation and installed-base monetisation rather than unit volume or a Services mix shift, is strongest in the United States, adequate in Europe, and in China depends on a domestic champion's pricing discipline.

### The pool is shrinking in units and growing in value

IDC's August 2026 forecast has worldwide smartphone shipments at just over 1.0 billion units in 2026, down 16.7%, while total market value rises 6.3% to $613 billion and the average selling price reaches a record $581, up 27.6% in a year. The cause is cost, not demand: DRAM and NAND prices are up more than 300% year on year, memory is more than 65% of bill of materials at the low end, and the sub-$100 tier fell close to 60% in the second quarter of 2026. This supply shock has a dated end — IDC expects memory prices to rise until at least 2028 — so 2026-2027 flatters Apple's unit share while lifting its price; 2028 tests whether either survives. [S66]

Two methods agree closely: 1.0 billion units at the $581 average price gives $581 billion, within 5% of IDC's $613 billion, so the two series are consistent. On that base Apple's serviceable market is the premium tier it addresses — an iOS share of 23.6% of 2026 shipments, a record — while the revenue it can obtain is what it already books: $466.8 billion trailing twelve months to 2026-06-27, or about $483 billion for FY2026 at the nine-month growth rate. [S6]

### China is the swing factor, and India sits in the wrong line

Apple's revenue is moving toward the faster-growing regions, but the swing is China. In the first nine months of FY2026 Greater China produced $64.8 billion, up 30.0% on a base of $49.9 billion, after falling from $72.6 billion in FY2023; the Americas grew 11.4% to $149.4 billion, Europe 16.1% to $95.6 billion, Japan 10.4% and Rest of Asia Pacific 19.4%. That $14.9 billion increase contributes 4.1 points of the group's 16.2% growth, more than any other segment, and part is currency. Europe includes India, the Middle East and Africa, so the fastest-growing large smartphone market is invisible in the segment line. [S13]

### Services carries the profit, but the mix moved back to hardware

The fastest-growing pool Apple monetises is Services, but its share of revenue fell in FY2026: $91.7 billion in the first nine months, 25.2% of $364.4 billion and up 14%, at a 76.3% gross margin, against a 26.2% revenue share in FY2025. Hardware grew faster than Services, so the mix shifted toward premium handsets and China rather than toward the recurring pool — the opposite of what a Services-led thesis needs. The app economy has no published size in the sources retrieved — no platform owner discloses app-store billings or mobile-advertising revenue — so Apple's Services line is the measured pool. The installed base is disclosed at more than 2.5 billion active devices on 2026-01-29, up from 2.35 billion a year earlier, but Apple publishes no replacement rate. [S5, S6, S174, S191]

### Who pays, and how much demand is policy

The budget owner is the consumer, but the transaction is intermediated: 60% of FY2025 net sales, $249,697 million of $416,161 million, went through carriers, resellers and distributors. Apple does not disclose the carrier-only share or subsidy per device, but it discloses the risk transfer: resellers offer financing, instalment plans or subsidies that "may be discontinued or modified any time", and carriers were 27% of trade receivables at 2026-06-27, $8,477 million of $31,398 million. Price protection and other customer incentives are deducted from Products net sales without an amount being given, so the channel's cost to Apple is a revenue deduction, not a disclosed expense; one point of wholesale terms across the indirect channel is $2.5 billion of revenue, 1.3% of FY2025 gross profit. The demand is policy-sensitive: US and UK interest-free financing holds the premium end while emerging markets fall more than 20%, China's government subsidy faded in Q2 2026, and India's $600-800 band grew 32% after the sub-$100 tier fell 59%. Policy also moves margin: after the 2026-02-20 Supreme Court ruling struck down certain IEEPA tariffs, refunds added 2.0 points to the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin. Carrier 10-K equipment-revenue and promotional lines, or paid channel sell-in data, would settle the missing subsidy figure; Apple's fiscal 2026 annual report was not on EDGAR at 2026-10-31. [S5, S6, S105, S40, S13]

### What would break the premiumisation case

Counter-evidence is fourfold. If memory prices normalise from 2028, the entry tier rebuilds and the 2026 share gain is contestable. If China's June-quarter demand was pulled forward ahead of second-half price increases, as IDC's China team reports, the 30% growth line is a launch and currency effect. If courts and the European Commission remove the App Store take rate, the margin layer that offsets hardware cyclicality stops compounding. And the search-distribution payment — $20 billion in 2022, 17% of trailing Services revenue of $120.5 billion and 22% of trailing Services gross profit of $91.6 billion — has not been banned: the 2025-09-02 remedies decision declined to ban distributor payments, and the December 2025 final judgment is under appeal by Google and the Department of Justice, both pending at 2026-10-29. The investor implication is narrow: in a 1-billion-unit market Apple can grow device revenue only if price rises faster than units fall, so average selling price, China durability, the carrier channel and the Services take rate matter most. Sizing confidence is high, because two independent methods agree within 5%; confidence that the mix shift holds to 2028 is medium. Three diligence questions remain open: what share of Services revenue is commission rather than subscription, advertising or licensing? How much of the Greater China increase is currency? And what is the current average replacement cycle, measured rather than asserted? [S66, S40, S82, S118, S42]

::: evidence
**Apple's addressable device market fell 16.7% in units in 2026 while growing 6.3% in value, and revenue grew 16.2% over nine months — the gap is premiumisation and China, not market growth, and 60% of sales run through a channel whose subsidy Apple does not disclose (S66, S13, S6, S5).**

IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0 billion units, $613 billion of value and a $581 ASP (S66, S102). Nine-month FY2026 revenue was $364.4 billion, up 16.2%, with Greater China up 30.0% and Services at 25.2% of revenue against 26.2% in FY2025 (S13, S6). In FY2025, 60% of net sales, $249,697 million, went through carriers, resellers and distributors, and carriers were 27% of trade receivables at 2026-06-27 (S5, S6).
:::

rows.finding: The ten-year average intra-year drawdown is 21.4% over 82 days, with 2018 -36.73%, 2020 -31.43%, 2022 -30.75% and 2025 -30.22%; from $344.63 these map to $218-240, and the average to $271.
rows.follow_up: What multiple would a 2027 correction start from if EPS reaches $11.17?
rows.implication: Position size and the entry band, not a stop-loss, are the defence; the fund should expect a 20-30% mark-to-market drawdown.
rows.mechanism: A 38.9x entry multiple leaves the price exposed to de-rating; drawdowns of 30% have been routine even for a franchise that recovered each time.
rows.weakens: Every episode recovered, and 2020 returned 80.75% for the calendar year; a holder who sold at the trough lost the recovery.

rows.benchmark: Apple's five-year average multiple of 30.2x and five-year range of 22.1-40.6x.
rows.confidence: medium: the EPS paths are the team's calculation; the multiple anchors are observed.
rows.finding: The scenario case is $399 bull (15%, 38x on $10.50), $268 base (50%, 30.2x on $8.87) and $205 bear (35%, 25x on $8.20), an expected value of $266, 23% below the $344.63 close.
rows.follow_up: What evidence on the September guide would move the base toward $296?
rows.implication: No position at $344.63; a 1-2% starter at $240-265 and a 3-4% position at or below $225.
rows.mechanism: The expected return is negative because the base case already de-rates the multiple by 22%; the bull case only pays 16%.
rows.weakens: If the multiple holds above 35x, the expected value rises toward $350 and the discipline never buys.

rows.benchmark: Microsoft/Activision 2022 precedent; Apple's $13.84B average daily traded value over 20 days.
rows.confidence: high.
rows.finding: There is no takeover exit: the largest technology acquisition on record, Microsoft's $68.7B deal for Activision Blizzard, equals 1.4% of Apple's $5,029.6B market value; average daily traded value is $13.84B.
rows.follow_up: Is there any activist or strategic holder large enough to force a transaction?
rows.implication: The exit decision is entirely about price and thesis, not about finding a buyer.
rows.mechanism: Size and antitrust make a strategic bid implausible, so the only exit is the secondary market, where liquidity is not a constraint for a fund position.
rows.weakens: A break-up or a large spin-off is not contemplated; nothing in the record suggests a buyer.

rows.benchmark: The release's own text, which stops at the cash-flow statement and the dividend declaration.
rows.confidence: medium: the call guidance is trade-reported, not verified in the release.
rows.finding: Apple's 2026-07-30 release contains no September-quarter outlook; the 9-11% revenue growth and 47-48% gross margin figures are management's call guidance as reported by third parties.
rows.follow_up: What did management say on the 2026-07-30 call about gross margin ex-refund and December-quarter memory costs?
rows.implication: Size the starter tranche only after the 2026-11-02 release confirms the margin path.
rows.mechanism: The base case depends on a guide the filing does not state, so the evidence is one grade weaker than a filed number.
rows.weakens: If the guide is wrong or withdrawn, the $8.87 base moves; consensus of $9.79 implies a smaller give-back.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's competitive position strengthened in 2026 in every hardware line except smartwatches, but the gain is crisis-specific — bought with memory supply and price discipline rather than product superiority — and it is being offset where profit is made, because the App Store commission that funds the premium position is being dismantled by courts and regulators rather than by a rival's product. Apple leads no hardware category outright except detachable tablets and concedes minority share elsewhere. Head to head, Samsung shipped 62.7 million handsets in Q2 2026 versus Apple's 55.7 million. [S102]

### The lead is in integration, not in units

Apple's 20.2% of global smartphone shipments in Q2 2026 was a record for that quarter and a 3.9 percentage point gain, but Samsung's 22.7% was larger and Xiaomi's 26.4% collapse explains much of the redistribution. In personal computing Apple is second at 18.2% to Lenovo's 20.1%, yet macOS shipments grew 17.4% while Windows fell 6.7% and Android 19.6%, and macOS is the only major operating system IDC expects to grow in 2026. The clearest structural lead is detachable tablets at 55.3%; the weakest spot is smartwatches, where Huawei leads 18.8% to 17.2%, so Apple's 15.5% of all wearables rests on earwear, where it holds 17.2%. [S104]

| Product | Competitor | Competitor share, Q2 2026 | Apple share | Technology basis | Price position | Switching cost | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone, global | Samsung | 22.7%, +3.2pp | 20.2%, +3.9pp | iOS integration and secured memory supply | Industry ASP $581; Apple above it | High: iCloud, iMessage, purchased apps | S102, S66 |
| iPhone, China | Huawei | 22.6%, +4.5pp | 18.1%, +4.2pp | iOS against domestic HarmonyOS | Apple held prices while Android raised them | Medium: leaving iOS loses Apple services | S40 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo | 20.1%, +2.5pp | 18.2%, -0.4% | macOS against Windows | MacBook Neo attacks entry pricing | Medium | S103, S106 |
| Services and App Store | Alphabet, Google Play | $471.1bn TTM revenue | $91.7bn Services, 76.3% margin (9M FY2026) | iOS distribution against Google Play | 15-30% commission, under challenge | High for consumers, falling for developers | S5, S42, S80 |
| Entry tier | Transsion | Outside the top five; "Others" 27.7% | Not present | Android at sub-$200 | Lowest tier, priced out by memory | Low | S102 |
| Foldables | HONOR | Outside the top five; H1 2026 shipments +53% | 20.2% of all phones | Android foldables | Premium foldable | Medium | S102, S215 |

### Samsung is the dangerous one, and the reason is memory

Samsung is the most dangerous competitor. When memory is more than 65% of bill of materials at the low end, the binding constraint is supply access, and Samsung is the only top-five handset vendor that also sells memory: it grew shipments 8.1% and took 3.2 points of share in Q2 2026 while Xiaomi fell 26.4% and vivo 19.6%. Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise Apple now attacks: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, below the $2,550 average price IDC assumes, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027 and 40% of a category growing 12.6% to 22.9 million units this year. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs, leaning on HarmonyOS, which IDC expects to reach 51 million units in 2026; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap in the one market where it mattered most but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses that it is subject to a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain purchases consumers make, that its Digital Markets Act compliance plan has been challenged by the European Commission, and that it faces U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by U.S. courts and European regulators. [S5]

### The next form factor is glasses, and the model layer is becoming free

Smart glasses are the only consumer device growing fast enough to become a platform: IDC counted about 2.25 million display-less units in the first quarter of 2026, up 167%, forecasts 13.6 million units and $5.1 billion for the year and 27.3 million by 2030, and puts Meta at 68.7% of the category in Q2 2026. At $799 for Meta Ray-Ban Display, expanded to five markets on 2026-09-23, glasses cost 38% more than the $581 average smartphone and depend on a phone for connectivity; 13.6 million units are 1.3% of the 1.0 billion phones shipped. Apple's iPhone Duo, on sale 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, is therefore a defence of the phone, not a response to glasses: it sells at 3.4 times the industry ASP into a 22.9 million-unit foldable niche. The threat bites when a display pair with cellular independence sells at or below the iPhone's own average price — closing today's $218 gap — and when glasses pass roughly 10% of phone units; IDC's 2030 forecast reaches 2.7%. OpenAI's first device, reported on 2026-07-14 as a screenless home speaker, targets the same interface layer, and Apple's response so far is a trade-secrets suit. The model layer is commoditising faster: Qwen3-32B runs on one H100 at about $0.82 per million tokens, $0.34 on spot, and Llama 4 Scout at $0.87, so any handset maker can self-host a competent assistant for under $1 per million tokens — under a tenth of a cent for a 1,000-token query. [S212, S214, S216, S213, S217]

### AI is rented, and the phone in the pocket is the strongest competitor

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google, so its assistant depends on a company it also competes with in services, and Samsung's AI-equipped Galaxy S26 Ultra is credited by IDC with returning Samsung to first place in Q1 2026. The strongest competitor is the handset already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening and IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares and legal facts, medium beyond 2028, when memory normalises and the crisis-specific advantage lapses. Three diligence questions remain: what proportion of Services revenue is commission rather than subscription? What margin does the foldable carry at its launch price? What does the Gemini licence cost per query at scale?

Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027 and 40% of a category growing 12.6% to 22.9 million units this year. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs, leaning on HarmonyOS, which IDC expects to reach 51 million units in 2026; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain consumer purchases, a Digital Markets Act compliance plan challenged by the European Commission, and U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by courts and regulators. [S5]

### The next form factor is glasses, and the model layer is becoming free

Smart glasses are the only consumer device growing fast enough to become a platform: IDC counted 2.25 million display-less units in Q1 2026, up 167%, and forecasts 13.6 million units and $5.1 billion for 2026, 27.3 million by 2030, with Meta at 68.7% of Q2 2026 units. At $799 for Meta Ray-Ban Display, expanded to five markets on 2026-09-23, glasses cost 38% more than the $581 average smartphone and depend on a phone; 13.6 million units are 1.3% of the 1.0 billion phones shipped. Apple's iPhone Duo, on sale 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, is therefore a defence of the phone, not a response to glasses: it sells at 3.4 times the industry ASP into a 22.9 million-unit foldable niche. The threat bites when a cellular-independent display pair sells at or below the iPhone's average price — closing today's $218 gap — and when glasses pass 10% of phone units; IDC's 2030 forecast reaches 2.7%. OpenAI's first device, reported on 2026-07-14 as a screenless home speaker, targets the same layer, and Apple's response is a trade-secrets suit. The model layer is commoditising faster: Qwen3-32B runs on one H100 at about $0.82 per million tokens ($0.34 spot) and Llama 4 Scout at $0.87, so a handset maker can self-host a competent assistant for under $1 per million tokens — a tenth of a cent for a 1,000-token query. [S212, S214, S216, S213, S217]

### AI is rented, and the phone in the pocket is the strongest competitor

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google, so its assistant depends on a company it also competes with in services. The strongest competitor is the handset already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening and IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares and legal facts, medium beyond 2028. Three diligence questions remain: what proportion of Services revenue is commission? What margin does the foldable carry at its launch price? What does the Gemini licence cost per query at scale?

arguments.markdown:
Apple's competitive position strengthened in 2026 in every hardware line except smartwatches, but the gain is crisis-specific — bought with memory supply and price discipline, not product superiority — and it is being offset where profit is made, because the App Store commission that funds the premium position is being dismantled by courts and regulators, not by a rival's product. Head to head, Samsung shipped 62.7 million handsets in Q2 2026 versus Apple's 55.7 million. [S102]

### The lead is in integration, not in units

Apple's 20.2% of global smartphone shipments in Q2 2026 was a record for that quarter and a 3.9 percentage point gain, but Samsung's 22.7% was larger and Xiaomi's 26.4% collapse explains much of the redistribution. In personal computing Apple is second at 18.2% to Lenovo's 20.1%, yet macOS shipments grew 17.4% while Windows fell 6.7% and Android 19.6%. The clearest lead is detachable tablets at 55.3%; the weakest is smartwatches, where Huawei leads 18.8% to 17.2%, so Apple's 15.5% of wearables rests on earwear, where it holds 17.2%. [S104]

| Product | Competitor | Competitor share, Q2 2026 | Apple share | Technology basis | Price position | Switching cost | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone, global | Samsung | 22.7%, +3.2pp | 20.2%, +3.9pp | iOS integration and secured memory supply | Industry ASP $581; Apple above it | High: iCloud, iMessage, apps | S102, S66 |
| iPhone, China | Huawei | 22.6%, +4.5pp | 18.1%, +4.2pp | iOS against domestic HarmonyOS | Apple held prices while Android raised them | Medium | S40 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo | 20.1%, +2.5pp | 18.2%, -0.4% | macOS against Windows | MacBook Neo attacks entry pricing | Medium | S103, S106 |
| Services and App Store | Alphabet, Google Play | $471.1bn TTM revenue | $91.7bn Services, 76.3% margin (9M FY2026) | iOS distribution against Google Play | 15-30% commission, under challenge | High for consumers, falling for developers | S5, S42, S80 |
| Entry tier | Transsion | Outside the top five; "Others" 27.7% | Not present | Android at sub-$200 | Lowest tier, priced out by memory | Low | S102 |
| Foldables | HONOR | Outside the top five; H1 2026 shipments +53% | 20.2% of all phones | Android foldables | Premium foldable | Medium | S102, S215 |

### Samsung is the dangerous one, and the reason is memory

Samsung is the most dangerous competitor. When memory is over 65% of low-end bill of materials, supply access binds, and Samsung is the only top-five vendor that also sells memory: it grew shipments 8.1% and took 3.2 points of share in Q2 2026 while Xiaomi fell 26.4% and vivo 19.6%. Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027 in a category growing 12.6% to 22.9 million units this year. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain consumer purchases, a Digital Markets Act compliance plan challenged by the European Commission, and U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by courts and regulators. [S5]

### The next form factor is glasses, and the model layer is becoming free

Smart glasses are the only consumer device growing fast enough to become a platform: IDC counted 2.25 million display-less units in Q1 2026, up 167%, and forecasts 13.6 million units and $5.1 billion for 2026, 27.3 million by 2030, with Meta at 68.7% of Q2 2026 units. At $799 for Meta Ray-Ban Display, expanded to five markets on 2026-09-23, glasses cost 38% more than the $581 average smartphone and depend on a phone; 13.6 million units are 1.3% of the 1.0 billion phones shipped. Apple's iPhone Duo, on sale 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, is therefore a defence of the phone, not a response to glasses: it sells at 3.4 times the industry ASP into a 22.9 million-unit foldable niche. The threat bites when a cellular-independent display pair sells at or below the iPhone's average price — closing today's $218 gap — and when glasses pass 10% of phone units; IDC's 2030 forecast reaches 2.7%. OpenAI's first device, reported on 2026-07-14 as a screenless home speaker, targets the same layer, and Apple's response is a trade-secrets suit. The model layer is commoditising faster: Qwen3-32B runs on one H100 at about $0.82 per million tokens ($0.34 spot) and Llama 4 Scout at $0.87, so a handset maker can self-host a competent assistant for under $1 per million tokens — a tenth of a cent for a 1,000-token query. [S212, S214, S216, S213, S217]

### AI is rented, and the phone in the pocket is the strongest competitor

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google, so its assistant depends on a company it also competes with in services. The strongest competitor is the handset already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening and IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares, medium beyond 2028. Three diligence questions remain: what proportion of Services revenue is commission? What margin does the foldable carry at its launch price? What does the Gemini licence cost per query at scale?

| Product | Leader | Challenger | Niche | Emerging threat | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | Samsung, 22.7% of units | Apple, 20.2% and gaining | Huawei in China, 22.6% | HarmonyOS at 51m units; AI-first Android flagships | S102, S40, S66 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo, 20.1% | Apple, 18.2%, with the only growing OS | Dell in workstations, 40.0% | HarmonyOS NEXT at 1.6%; Windows-on-ARM | S103, S106 |
| Services | Apple, $91.7bn (9M) | Alphabet through Google Play | Netflix, Spotify, Epic | Web payments and alternative marketplaces | S5, S42, S80 |

::: quad
| Quadrant | Points | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Strengths | Record 23.6% iOS share of 2026 shipments; 20.2% of Q2 units, up 3.9 points; 55.3% of detachable tablets; 15.5% of wearables; Services of $91.7bn at a 76.3% margin | S66, S102, S103, S104, S5, S6 |
| Weaknesses | Minority share in every hardware category; second to Samsung, Lenovo and Huawei in phones, PCs and watches; AI licensed from Alphabet; no disclosed replacement rate; no position in smart glasses | S5, S102, S103, S104, S58, S214 |
| Opportunities | More than 17m foldable iPhones and about 40% of a category by 2027; macOS the only major operating system forecast to grow in 2026; India's $600-800 band growing 32% | S66, S103, S105 |
| Threats | Huawei at 22.6% of China with HarmonyOS at 51m units; Meta at 68.7% of glasses; a U.S. court order barring commission on certain external purchases; a DMA plan challenged by the Commission; memory up over 300% from a competing supplier | S40, S5, S66, S102, S214 |
:::

::: evidence
**Apple gained unit share in every hardware line in 2026 except smartwatches, while the commission that funds its premium position was being removed by courts and regulators and the next interface was being won by Meta.**

In Q2 2026 Apple held 20.2% of smartphone units behind Samsung's 22.7%, 18.2% of PC-plus-tablet units behind Lenovo's 20.1% and 15.5% of wearables but only 17.2% of smartwatches against Huawei's 18.8% (S102, S103, S104). Meta held 68.7% of smart glasses, a pool of 13.6m units and $5.1bn in 2026 (S214, S212).
:::

arguments.markdown:
Apple's competitive position strengthened in 2026 in every hardware line except smartwatches, but the gain is crisis-specific — bought with memory supply and price discipline, not product superiority — and it is being offset where profit is made, because the App Store commission that funds the premium position is being dismantled by courts and regulators, not by a rival's product. Samsung shipped 62.7 million handsets in Q2 2026 against Apple's 55.7 million. [S102]

### The lead is in integration, not in units

Apple's 20.2% of global smartphone shipments in Q2 2026 was a record for that quarter and a 3.9 percentage point gain, but Samsung's 22.7% was larger and Xiaomi's 26.4% collapse explains much of the redistribution. In personal computing Apple is second at 18.2% to Lenovo's 20.1%, yet macOS shipments grew 17.4% while Windows fell 6.7% and Android 19.6%. The clearest lead is detachable tablets at 55.3%; the weakest is smartwatches, where Huawei leads 18.8% to 17.2%, so Apple's 15.5% of wearables rests on earwear, where it holds 17.2%. [S104]

| Product | Competitor | Competitor share, Q2 2026 | Apple share | Technology basis | Price position | Switching cost | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone, global | Samsung | 22.7%, +3.2pp | 20.2%, +3.9pp | iOS integration and secured memory supply | Industry ASP $581; Apple above it | High: iCloud, iMessage, apps | S102, S66 |
| iPhone, China | Huawei | 22.6%, +4.5pp | 18.1%, +4.2pp | iOS against domestic HarmonyOS | Apple held prices while Android raised them | Medium | S40 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo | 20.1%, +2.5pp | 18.2%, -0.4% | macOS against Windows | MacBook Neo attacks entry pricing | Medium | S103, S106 |
| Services and App Store | Alphabet, Google Play | $471.1bn TTM revenue | $91.7bn Services, 76.3% margin (9M FY2026) | iOS distribution against Google Play | 15-30% commission, under challenge | High for consumers, falling for developers | S5, S42, S80 |
| Entry tier | Transsion | Outside the top five; "Others" 27.7% | Not present | Android at sub-$200 | Lowest tier, priced out by memory | Low | S102 |
| Foldables | HONOR | Outside the top five; H1 2026 shipments +53% | 20.2% of all phones | Android foldables | Premium foldable | Medium | S102, S215 |

### Samsung is the dangerous one, and the reason is memory

Samsung is the most dangerous competitor. When memory is over 65% of low-end bill of materials, supply access binds, and Samsung is the only top-five vendor that also sells memory: it grew shipments 8.1% and took 3.2 points of share in Q2 2026 while Xiaomi fell 26.4% and vivo 19.6%. Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain consumer purchases, a Digital Markets Act compliance plan challenged by the European Commission, and U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by courts and regulators. [S5]

### The next form factor is glasses, and the model layer is becoming free

Smart glasses are the only consumer device growing fast enough to become a platform: IDC counted 2.25 million display-less units in Q1 2026, up 167%, and forecasts 13.6 million units and $5.1 billion for 2026, 27.3 million by 2030, with Meta at 68.7% of Q2 2026 units. At $799 for Meta Ray-Ban Display, expanded to five markets on 2026-09-23, glasses cost 38% more than the $581 average smartphone and depend on a phone; 13.6 million units are 1.3% of the 1.0 billion phones shipped. Apple's iPhone Duo, on sale 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, is therefore a defence of the phone, not a response to glasses: it sells at 3.4 times the industry ASP into a 22.9 million-unit foldable niche. The threat bites when a cellular-independent display pair sells at or below the iPhone's average price — closing today's $218 gap — and when glasses pass 10% of phone units; IDC's 2030 forecast reaches 2.7%. OpenAI's first device, reported on 2026-07-14 as a screenless home speaker, targets the same layer, and Apple's response is a trade-secrets suit. The model layer is commoditising faster: Qwen3-32B runs on one H100 at about $0.82 per million tokens ($0.34 spot) and Llama 4 Scout at $0.87, so a handset maker can self-host a competent assistant for under $1 per million tokens — a tenth of a cent for a 1,000-token query. [S212, S214, S216, S213, S217]

### AI is rented, and the phone in the pocket is the strongest competitor

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google, so its assistant depends on a company it also competes with in services. The strongest competitor is the phone already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening and IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Two risks offset the gain: memory normalises after 2028, and Meta holds the next interface. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares, medium beyond 2028. Three diligence questions remain: what proportion of Services revenue is commission? What margin does the foldable carry at its launch price? What does the Gemini licence cost per query at scale?

:::

::: evidence
**Apple gained unit share in every hardware line in 2026 except smartwatches, while the commission that funds its premium position was being removed by courts and regulators and the next interface was being won by Meta.**

In Q2 2026 Apple held 20.2% of smartphone units behind Samsung's 22.7%, 18.2% of PC-plus-tablet units behind Lenovo's 20.1% and 15.5% of wearables but only 17.2% of smartwatches against Huawei's 18.8% (S102, S103, S104). Meta held 68.7% of smart glasses, a pool of 13.6m units and $5.1bn in 2026 (S214, S212).
:::

Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain consumer purchases, a Digital Markets Act compliance plan challenged by the European Commission, and U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by courts and regulators. [S5]

### The next form factor is glasses, and the model layer is becoming free

Smart glasses are the only consumer device growing fast enough to become a platform: IDC counted 2.25 million display-less units in Q1 2026, up 167%, and forecasts 13.6 million units and $5.1 billion for 2026, 27.3 million by 2030, with Meta at 68.7% of Q2 2026 units. At $799 for Meta Ray-Ban Display, expanded to five markets on 2026-09-23, glasses cost 38% more than the $581 average smartphone and depend on a phone; 13.6 million units are 1.3% of the 1.0 billion phones shipped. Apple's iPhone Duo, on sale 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, is therefore a defence of the phone, not a response to glasses: it sells at 3.4 times the industry ASP into a 22.9 million-unit foldable niche. The threat bites when a cellular-independent display pair sells at or below the iPhone's average price — closing today's $218 gap — and when glasses pass 10% of phone units; IDC's 2030 forecast reaches 2.7%. OpenAI's first device, reported on 2026-07-14 as a screenless home speaker, targets the same layer, and Apple's response is a trade-secrets suit. The model layer is commoditising faster: Qwen3-32B runs on one H100 at about $0.82 per million tokens ($0.34 spot) and Llama 4 Scout at $0.87, so a handset maker can self-host a competent assistant for under $1 per million tokens — a tenth of a cent for a 1,000-token query. [S212, S214, S216, S213, S217]

### AI is rented, and the phone in the pocket is the strongest competitor

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google, so its assistant depends on a company it also competes with in services. The strongest competitor is the phone already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening and IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Two risks offset the gain: memory normalises after 2028, and Meta holds the next interface. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares, medium beyond 2028. Three diligence questions remain: what proportion of Services revenue is commission? What margin does the foldable carry at its launch price? What does the Gemini licence cost per query at scale?

arguments.markdown:
Apple's competitive position strengthened in 2026 in every hardware line except smartwatches, but the gain is crisis-specific — bought with memory supply and price discipline, not product superiority — and it is being offset where profit is made, because the App Store commission that funds the premium position is being dismantled by courts and regulators, not by a rival's product. Samsung shipped 62.7 million handsets in Q2 2026 versus Apple's 55.7 million. [S102]

### The lead is in integration, not in units

Apple's 20.2% of global smartphone shipments in Q2 2026 was a record for that quarter and a 3.9 percentage point gain, but Samsung's 22.7% was larger and Xiaomi's 26.4% collapse explains much of the redistribution. In personal computing Apple is second at 18.2% compared with Lenovo's 20.1%, yet macOS shipments grew 17.4% while Windows fell 6.7% and Android 19.6%. The clearest lead is detachable tablets at 55.3%; the weakest is smartwatches, where Huawei leads 18.8% to 17.2%, so Apple's 15.5% of wearables rests on earwear, where it holds 17.2%. [S104]

| Product | Competitor | Competitor share, Q2 2026 | Apple share | Technology basis | Price position | Switching cost | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone, global | Samsung | 22.7%, +3.2pp | 20.2%, +3.9pp | iOS integration and secured memory supply | Industry ASP $581; Apple above it | High: iCloud, iMessage, apps | S102, S66 |
| iPhone, China | Huawei | 22.6%, +4.5pp | 18.1%, +4.2pp | iOS against domestic HarmonyOS | Apple held prices while Android raised them | Medium | S40 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo | 20.1%, +2.5pp | 18.2%, -0.4% | macOS against Windows | MacBook Neo attacks entry pricing | Medium | S103, S106 |
| Services and App Store | Alphabet, Google Play | $471.1bn TTM revenue | $91.7bn Services, 76.3% margin (9M FY2026) | iOS distribution against Google Play | 15-30% commission, under challenge | High for consumers, falling for developers | S5, S42, S80 |
| Entry tier | Transsion | Outside the top five; "Others" 27.7% | Not present | Android at sub-$200 | Lowest tier, priced out by memory | Low | S102 |
| Foldables | HONOR | Outside the top five; H1 2026 shipments +53% | 20.2% of all phones | Android foldables | Premium foldable | Medium | S102, S215 |

### Samsung is the dangerous one, and the reason is memory

Samsung is the most dangerous competitor. When memory is over 65% of low-end bill of materials, supply access binds, and Samsung is the only top-five vendor that also sells memory: it grew shipments 8.1% and took 3.2 points of share in Q2 2026 while Xiaomi fell 26.4% and vivo 19.6%. Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain consumer purchases, a Digital Markets Act compliance plan challenged by the European Commission, and U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by courts and regulators. [S5]

### The next form factor is glasses, and the model layer is becoming free

Smart glasses are the only consumer device growing fast enough to become a platform: IDC counted 2.25 million display-less units in Q1 2026, up 167%, and forecasts 13.6 million units and $5.1 billion for 2026, 27.3 million by 2030, with Meta at 68.7% of Q2 2026 units. At $799 for Meta Ray-Ban Display, expanded to five markets on 2026-09-23, glasses cost 38% more than the $581 average smartphone and depend on a phone; 13.6 million units are 1.3% of the 1.0 billion phones shipped. Apple's iPhone Duo, on sale 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, is therefore a defence of the phone, not a response to glasses: it sells at 3.4 times the industry ASP into a 22.9 million-unit foldable niche. The threat bites when a cellular-independent display pair sells at or below the iPhone's average price — closing today's $218 gap — and when glasses pass 10% of phone units; IDC's 2030 forecast reaches 2.7%. OpenAI's first device, reported on 2026-07-14 as a screenless home speaker, targets the same layer, and Apple's response is a trade-secrets suit. The model layer is commoditising faster: Qwen3-32B and Llama 4 Scout run on one H100 at about $0.82-0.87 per million tokens, DeepSeek V3.2 on eight at $13.89, so a handset maker can self-host a competent assistant for under $1 per million tokens — a tenth of a cent for a 1,000-token query. [S212, S214, S216, S213, S217]

### AI is rented, and the phone in the pocket is the strongest competitor

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google, so its assistant depends on a company it also competes with in services. The strongest competitor is the phone already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening and IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Two risks offset the gain: memory normalises after 2028, and Meta holds the next interface. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares, medium beyond 2028. Three diligence questions remain: what proportion of Services revenue is commission? What margin does the foldable carry at its launch price? What does the Gemini licence cost per query at scale?

| Product | Leader | Challenger | Niche | Emerging threat | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | Samsung, 22.7% of units | Apple, 20.2% and gaining | Huawei in China, 22.6% | HarmonyOS at 51m units; AI-first Android | S102, S40, S66 |
| PCs and tablets | Lenovo, 20.1% | Apple, 18.2%, with the only growing OS | Dell in workstations, 40.0% | HarmonyOS NEXT at 1.6%; Windows-on-ARM | S103, S106 |
| Services | Apple, $91.7bn (9M) | Alphabet through Google Play | Netflix, Spotify, Epic | Web payments and alternative marketplaces | S5, S42, S80 |

::: quad
| Quadrant | Points | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Strengths | Record 23.6% iOS share of 2026 shipments; 20.2% of Q2 units, up 3.9 points; 55.3% of detachable tablets; 15.5% of wearables; Services of $91.7bn at a 76.3% margin | S66, S102, S103, S104, S5, S6 |
| Weaknesses | Minority share in every hardware category; second to Samsung, Lenovo and Huawei in phones, PCs and watches; AI licensed from Alphabet; no disclosed replacement rate; no position in smart glasses | S5, S102, S103, S104, S58, S214 |
| Opportunities | More than 17m foldable iPhones and about 40% of a category by 2027; macOS the only growing major OS in 2026; India's $600-800 band growing 32% | S66, S103, S105 |
| Threats | Huawei at 22.6% of China with HarmonyOS at 51m units; Meta at 68.7% of glasses; a U.S. court order barring commission on certain external purchases; a DMA plan challenged by the Commission; memory up 300% from a competing supplier | S40, S5, S66, S102, S214 |
:::

::: evidence
**Apple gained unit share in every hardware line in 2026 except smartwatches, while the commission that funds its premium position was being removed by courts and regulators and the next interface was being won by Meta.**

In Q2 2026 Apple held 20.2% of smartphone units behind Samsung's 22.7%, 18.2% of PC-plus-tablet units behind Lenovo's 20.1% and 15.5% of wearables but only 17.2% of smartwatches against Huawei's 18.8% (S102, S103, S104). Meta held 68.7% of smart glasses, a pool of 13.6m units and $5.1bn in 2026 (S214, S212).
:::

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Exit Strategy Analysis (exit, revision 9 by Valuation Analyst, 8,959 characters)
Apple's exit is the market, not a buyer, and at $344.63 the margin-adjusted 15/50/35 case is worth $266, 23% below the close, which means the discipline is a $240-265 starter, a full position at or below $225 and a trim at $395. At a $5,029.6B market value the largest technology acquisition on record, Microsoft's $68.7B all-cash purchase of Activision Blizzard agreed on 2022-01-18, equals 1.4% of the company, and any bid would face the US and EU antitrust review that Microsoft's own deal attracted; a leveraged buyout of a $4.97T enterprise value is arithmetically impossible. No strategic buyer exists: the only companies that could write a $5T cheque, Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon, are the ones antitrust would block, and none needs Apple's hardware or closed ecosystem. The exit is a sale into the market: a 1% position in a $1B fund is $10M, 0.07% of the $13.84B daily traded value. The exit question is therefore not whether a holder can sell but at what multiple, which makes the sell discipline a set of price bands and thesis breaks rather than an event to wait for. [S9, S169, S154]

| Exit route | Named buyer or venue | Rationale | Timing | Likelihood | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open-market sale | NasdaqGS, $13.84B average daily traded value | The only route that absorbs a position without a discount | Any trading day | The route actually used | S9 |
| Strategic acquisition | No named buyer; largest technology deal $68.7B vs $5,029.6B market value | Size, antitrust, no strategic gap Apple fills | Not foreseeable | Very low | S169 |
| Leveraged buyout | None | $4.97T enterprise value and $84.3B of debt cannot be financed | Not foreseeable | Negligible | S6 |
| Company buyback (partial exit) | Apple Inc. | $100B authorised on 2025-05-01 and a further $100B on 2026-04-30; $61.8B repurchased in the nine months to 2026-06-27, 1.6% of shares a year | Ongoing | High but discretionary | S204, S205, S6 |
| Dividend | Apple Inc. | $0.27 a quarter, 0.31% yield, declared 2026-07-30 | Quarterly | Certain while declared | S13 |
| Index and passive flows | S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 constituent | Structural bid, not an exit route | Ongoing | Structural | S163 |

Apple's own record sets the cost of ownership. Over the last ten completed years the average intra-year peak-to-trough drawdown was 21.4%, lasting 82 days, and four episodes exceeded 30%: 2018 fell 36.73%, 2020 31.43%, 2022 30.75% and 2025 30.22%. Each recovered — 2020 returned 80.75% for the calendar year and 2025 8.56% — but each recovery came with a re-rating as well as earnings growth, and a buyer at 38.9x cannot count on the re-rating half. From $344.63 the average drawdown is $271 and a 30% drawdown is $240. [S163, S168]

| Precedent episode | Peak | Trough | Drawdown | Days | Equivalent price from $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | $58.02 (2018-10-03) | $36.71 (2018-12-24) | -36.73% | 82 | $218 | S163 |
| 2020 | $81.80 (2020-02-12) | $56.09 (2020-03-23) | -31.43% | 40 | $236 | S163 |
| 2022 | $182.01 (2022-01-03) | $126.04 (2022-12-28) | -30.75% | 359 | $239 | S163 |
| 2025 | $247.10 (2025-02-24) | $172.42 (2025-04-08) | -30.22% | 43 | $240 | S163 |
| Ten-year average | - | - | -21.39% | 82 | $271 | S163 |

The economics of the exit turn on the multiple, not the remembered share price: the 2022 trough of $126.04 on 2022-12-28 was 20.6x fiscal 2022 diluted EPS of $6.11, and a repeat of that multiple on the margin-adjusted $8.87 would be $183, below the bear case. The base case is not a bear forecast: it takes the team's margin-adjusted EPS of $8.87 — the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin included 2 points of tariff refunds and its $2.02 EPS included $0.11, and two points of give-back on $490B of fiscal 2027 revenue is $9.8B of pretax profit — and applies 30.2x, the five-year average. That is $268. The bear applies 25x to $8.20, or $205; the bull applies 38x to $10.50, or $399. Weighted 15% bull, 50% base and 35% bear, the value is $266, 23% below the close. [S13, S6, S154]

| Scenario | Probability | EPS | Multiple | Value | Versus $344.63 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 15% | $10.50 | 38.0x | $399 | +16% | S13, S154 |
| Base | 50% | $8.87 | 30.2x | $268 | -22% | S13, S6, S154 |
| Bear | 35% | $8.20 | 25.0x | $205 | -41% | S6, S118 |
| Probability-weighted | 100% | - | - | $266 | -23% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |

A long-only fund should underwrite a three-to-five-year hold, the period over which the Services annuity and the installed base can compound enough to absorb a de-rating. On the margin-adjusted $8.87 growing 8% a year to $11.17 by fiscal 2029 and $3.37 of cumulative dividends, the annual total return depends almost entirely on the exit multiple, which means the entry price decides whether the fund is paid for waiting. At $344.63 a 25x exit loses 6.4% a year and a 35x exit earns 4.6%; at $265 the same exits earn 2.2% and 14.2%; at $225 they earn 7.9% and 20.6%. An 8% return at today's price needs an exit multiple of 38.6x, above the 38x bull case; at $225 it needs 25.1x, essentially the bear multiple. [S154, S157]

| Entry price | Implied P/E on $8.87 | 3-year annual return at exit 25x | At exit 30x | At exit 35x | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $344.63 | 38.9x | -6.4% | -0.6% | +4.6% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |
| $265 | 29.9x | +2.2% | +8.5% | +14.2% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |
| $240 | 27.1x | +5.6% | +12.2% | +18.0% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |
| $225 | 25.4x | +7.9% | +14.6% | +20.6% | Team calc on S13, S6, S154 |

The policy tests are narrow for a US holder: no foreign-buyer limit on a share sale, no lock-up, and no venue constraint at NasdaqGS, the S&P 500 or the Nasdaq-100. The binding policy risk sits in the asset, not the exit. The Google search payment, reported at $20B in 2022 and never disclosed by Apple, is on today's base 17% of trailing Services revenue of $120.5B and 22% of services gross profit of $91.6B, and it survived the D.D.C.'s remedies decision of 2025-09-02, which refused the DOJ's near-total ban on distribution payments and permitted non-exclusive default-placement deals of one year or less. Final judgment followed in December 2025; Google appealed in January 2026 and the DOJ and states in February 2026, with the appeals pending at 2026-10-29. The payment continues on non-exclusive, annually renegotiated terms, which means the event that would force a sale is its loss or material cut at a renewal or on appeal, not a ban in force. $20B of near-pure-margin revenue taxed at 21% is $15.8B of earnings, and at 30x that is $474B, 9.4% of the $5,029.6B market value. Slower policy risks are DMA and DOJ commission rules, and China, where revenue was $64.8B in nine months of fiscal 2026 and can turn on policy rather than execution. At 38.9x margin-adjusted earnings there is no cushion for a services margin shock. [S118, S42, S82, S13]

The strongest case against this discipline is that a 30x-plus multiple never offers a margin of safety again. Its five-year range of 22.1-40.6x shows a 25x entry is not exotic; if Services compounds at 14% on a 76% gross margin and the buyback retires 1.6% of the shares a year, a fund that waits for $225 may never own the best cash generator in the market, and the cost of the discipline is opportunity rather than loss. The strategic answer is a time rule rather than a permanent price target: if Apple trades above $268 for four consecutive quarters while Services growth stays above 10%, reassess the band against the then-current multiple instead of waiting for a level the business has outgrown. Until then, watchlist above $268, a 1-2% starter at $240-265, a full 3-4% position at or below $225 and a trim to half at or above $395. Confidence is high in the drawdown record and the return arithmetic, medium in the exit multiple, which depends on the ten-year yield of 4.93% on 2026-10-30. The diligence questions are the first one-year renewal of the Google payment, the June margin without the 2 points of tariff refund, and whether the 2026-11-02 release confirms the 47-48% September guide. [S154, S157]

| Sell and entry trigger | Threshold | Action | Source |
|---|---|---|---|

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Risk Assessment (risk, revision 5 by Red Team Analyst, 8,966 characters)
Apple is not a franchise at risk, it is a price at risk, and the price risk concentrates in one number. Apple guided gross margin of 47-48% for the September 2026 quarter, including 1 point of tariff refunds, so the underlying margin is 46-47% against 48.1% in the June quarter ex-refund — a two- to three-point decline the chief financial officer attributed to memory costs larger than the entire fall in margin. At 39.5x trailing earnings of $8.72 and 35.2x forward earnings of $9.79, on a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year Treasury, the price assumes 50.1% was a floor. It was a peak: the refund lifted June-quarter EPS by $0.11 of $2.02, the September guide carries 1 point more, and the 49.1% nine-month margin overstates the trading margin by 1 point. At 15% bull, 50% base and 35% bear — $399, $268 and $205 — probability-weighted value is $266, a 23% negative return from the $344.63 close of 2026-10-30. The direction survives; the entry price falls with the arithmetic [S194, S9].

### The margin is a cost transfer to Samsung, not a mix effect

The mechanism is a transfer between two companies in the comparison set. High-bandwidth and server DRAM crowd out consumer DRAM, so three suppliers keep pricing power over handset makers: TrendForce puts the 2026 DRAM sufficiency ratio at −1% to −2%, expects the gap to widen in 2027, sees substantial new output only in 2028 and forecasts another year of declining consumer device shipments in 2027. Apple's quarterly report says component costs are expected to intensify and "may materially negatively impact" gross margin, and IDC sees the shortage through 2027. The mitigations are finite: iPad and Mac prices rose in 2026, a supply-limited September quarter was guided, and carry-in inventory bought at lower prices runs out after September. One point of gross margin on FY2027 revenue near $490bn is $4.9bn of pretax profit, 3.1% of trailing net income, so two points of give-back cancel a year of high-single-digit revenue growth: EPS stays near $8.87 instead of reaching $9.79, and $8.87 at 30.2x is $268 against the $296 that consensus EPS implies. Jefferies' $263.66 target of 2026-08-10 lands within 2% of that arithmetic. Samsung, which sells both handsets and the memory inside them, trades at 12.5x trailing earnings while Apple pays 39.5x; Microsoft at 27.3x, Alphabet at 14.6x and Meta at 21.0x buy no critical input from a competitor [S192, S197, S106, S124, S161].

### Two growth sources are rented, and one has turned volume-negative

Services remains the best asset and stopped being the marginal driver of profit: services gross profit rose 15.3% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 against 26.3% for products, cutting services to 39.1% of gross profit. The reported $20bn payment from Google, a 2022 court figure Apple has never confirmed, is 16.6% of trailing services revenue of $120.5bn and 22% of services gross profit of $91.6bn; after tax at 30x it is $474bn, 9.4% of market value, $32 a share. The risk is dated: the Department of Justice and Google jointly asked the D.C. Circuit to expedite their cross-appeals so argument could be scheduled from 2026-12-09, and the government asks the court to overturn the district court's refusal to bar distribution payments outright. A 30% chance of a 50% cut plus a 10% chance of total loss is $8.0 a share, 2.3% of the price, and the base case carries none of it. China then supplies the second shock: Greater China produced $64.8bn, up 30.0%, in nine months, while IDC's release of 2026-10-13 has China shipments down 15.4% to 57.9m units in the third quarter of 2026, with Apple's units down 4.3% and share up to 17.8% only because rivals fell faster; Huawei shipped 12.2m units at 21.1% and grew 17.3%. A 20% decline in China revenue is $13bn, 3.9% of net income at a 47% group margin, and FY2027 laps a +30% base after the subsidy that supported earlier quarters was withdrawn [S196, S82, S195, S40].

### Capital return cannot cushion a de-rating

Apple repurchased $62.1bn of stock in nine months at 39.5x, a 2.5% earnings yield against 4.93% on the ten-year, for a 1.9% shareholder yield: the buyback adds EPS growth and transfers value to selling holders while the multiple sits above intrinsic value. The exit risk is the multiple. The ten-year average intra-year drawdown is 21.4%, and 21.0x on EPS of $8.87 gives $186: 17% below the $225 full-position entry, 22% below the $240 floor of the starter band and 30% below its $265 top. Maximum loss at the $225 entry is 17%, not the 9% the $205 bear implies [S6, S164, S163, S124].

The strongest case is that this is consensus arriving late: Apple has beaten estimates through the memory squeeze, absorbed iPad and Mac price rises, and holds net cash, so the margin hit may be absorbed rather than capitalised. What weakens that defence is the calendar: the December guide is the first without the inventory cushion and arrives before the first renewal of the search payment. A buyer who waits for the margin to be proven may pay more than one who buys the guidance.

| Revenue 30% lower | Same cost base, 48.7% margin | EPS $4.92 | S6 |
| Channel cost 2x | Apple funds the carrier subsidy | −7.5% of net income | S5 |
