IDC: Global smartphone shipments fall 7.4% in Q2 2026 (top-5 vendor shares)
sources.claims: Global smartphone shipments fell 7.4% YoY to 276.3m units in Q2 2026; Q2 2026 top-5: Samsung 62.7m (22.7%, +8.1%), Apple 55.7m (20.2%, +14.9% on record Q2 shipments), Xiaomi 31.2m (11.3%, -26.4%), OPPO 28.9m (10.5%, -17.1%), vivo 21.2m (7.7%, -19.6%); memory costs up nearly 300% and over 65% of BOM at the low end; Samsung and Apple the only top-5 vendors to grow, lifting share 3.2pp and 3.9pp; Apple on track for a record 22% annual share; Huawei +19.9%.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims of Apple unit-share erosion in the 2026 downturn: Apple gained 3.9pp of global share YoY in Q2 2026 despite a 7.4% market decline.

sources.title: IDC: Worldwide personal computing device market, Q2 2026 performance and 2026 outlook
sources.claims: Worldwide personal computing device shipments (PCs plus tablets) about 103m units in Q2 2026, -6.8% YoY; vendor shares Q2 2026: Lenovo 20.1% (+2.5%), Apple 18.2% (-0.4%), HP 12.7% (-8.9%), Dell 9.1% (-5.1%), Samsung 6.2% (-18.6%); Apple holds 55.3% of detachable tablets; macOS shipments grew 17.4% on MacBook Neo demand while Windows fell 6.7% and Android fell 19.6%; HarmonyOS NEXT reached 1.6%; full-year 2026 forecast about 398m units, -11.3%, with macOS the only major OS forecast to grow (+3.3%); market CAGR 1.5% 2026-2030.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Apple is a marginal PC vendor: at 18.2% of PC-plus-tablet units in Q2 2026 it is the number-two vendor, and macOS is the only major OS expected to grow in 2026.

sources.title: IDC: Worldwide wearable device market, Q2 2026 and 2026 outlook
sources.claims: Worldwide wearable device shipments about 148m units in Q2 2026 (+2.7% YoY); Apple leads with 15.5% share (+8.9%), Xiaomi 11.7%, Huawei 10.9%, Samsung 6.8%, Imagine Marketing 4.9%; earwear 64.9% of units and Apple leads earwear with 17.2%; Huawei tops smartwatches with 18.8% ahead of Apple's 17.2%; Meta holds 78.4% of glasses, Oura 67.0% of rings; wearables forecast about 625m units in 2026 (+1.7%) with a 2.4% CAGR to about 687m by 2030; smartwatches -3.7% in 2026 then 1.3% CAGR; glasses +35.2% in 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that Apple Watch dominates smartwatch units: Huawei leads smartwatch shipments at 18.8% versus Apple at 17.2% in Q2 2026, and Apple's overall wearables lead is 15.5% on AirPods-led earwear, not on watches.

sources.title: IDC: India smartphone market Q1 2026
sources.claims: India smartphone shipments 31.0m units in Q1 2026, -4.1% YoY, while market value rose 5.8%; ASP a record US$302 (+10.4%); sub-$100 segment -59% with share falling from 18% to 8%; US$600-800 band +32% and share 4% to 6%; US$800+ 7% share; top five by units vivo #1, Samsung #2, OPPO #3, Apple #4, Motorola #5; online channel fell 14% and its share slipped from 42% to 38%; India prices expected to rise further through 2027.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that India is already an Apple volume market: Apple ranks fourth by units in Q1 2026 behind vivo, Samsung and OPPO, in a market where value is growing faster than volume.

sources.title: IDC: PC market enters volatile territory as memory shortage persists through 2027
sources.claims: IDC forecasts global PC shipments -11.3% in 2026 with Q4 2026 down 20% YoY and no memory relief before end-2027; PC ASP growth of 17% in 2026; Apple's MacBook Neo drove stronger-than-expected notebook demand and forced IDC to revise its notebook forecast up, putting "real pressure on the entire PC ecosystem" with vendors expected to respond with new silicon, a more efficient Microsoft OS and aggressive promotional pricing.
sources.claims_weakened: The idea that Apple cannot compete on PC price: the MacBook Neo is described by IDC as pressuring the whole PC ecosystem on price and demand, not as a niche premium product.

sources.claims: Eddy Cue is SVP Services and Health, overseeing the App Store, Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple News, Apple Pay, Apple Card, Maps, Apple Ads, iCloud and productivity apps plus health and fitness; joined Apple in 1989 and helped create the Apple Store online (1998), the iTunes Store (2003) and the App Store (2008); bachelor's degree in Computer Science and Economics from Duke University.
sources.claims_weakened: Company biography; no degree year and no disclosure of Services margin responsibility.

sources.title: Apple Leadership: Craig Federighi
sources.claims: Craig Federighi is SVP Software Engineering, oversees iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS and visionOS, and also leads Apple's core AI efforts including foundation models, Apple Intelligence and Siri; returned to Apple in 2009 to lead macOS engineering and took on iOS in 2012; previously NeXT, Apple and about a decade at Ariba including CTO; MS in Computer Science and BS in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from UC Berkeley.
sources.claims_weakened: Company biography; no years for degrees, no evidence on AI delivery timelines.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: John Giannandrea to retire from Apple; Amar Subramanya joins as VP of AI
sources.claims: On 2025-12-01 Apple announced John Giannandrea, SVP Machine Learning and AI Strategy, was stepping down to serve as an adviser before retiring in spring 2026; Amar Subramanya joined as VP of AI reporting to Craig Federighi, leading Apple Foundation Models, ML research and AI safety and evaluation; Subramanya was most recently corporate VP of AI at Microsoft and spent 16 years at Google, where he was head of engineering for Google's Gemini Assistant; the balance of Giannandrea's organisation moved to Sabih Khan and Eddy Cue; Federighi oversees the work to bring a more personalised Siri to users in 2026.

sources.title: Apple Leadership: Johny Srouji
sources.claims: Johny Srouji is Apple's chief hardware officer overseeing product design, system engineering, reliability testing and technologies including Apple silicon, cellular, displays, cameras, sensors and batteries; joined Apple in 2008 to lead iPhone application processors; previously held senior positions at Intel and IBM; bachelor's and master's degrees in Computer Science from Technion.
sources.claims_weakened: Company biography; no years for degrees and no disclosure of succession depth beneath him in silicon.

sources.title: Apple Leadership: Deirdre O'Brien
sources.claims: Deirdre O'Brien is SVP Retail + People, leading Apple's retail, online store and People teams; joined Apple in 1988; bachelor's degree in Operations Management from Michigan State University and MBA from San Jose State University.
sources.claims_weakened: Company biography; no degree years and no disclosure of retail revenue or headcount metrics.

sources.title: CNBC: Apple picks Google's Gemini to run AI-powered Siri coming this year
sources.claims: On 2026-01-12 Apple and Google announced a multiyear partnership under which Apple will lean on Google's Gemini models to power Apple's AI features, including a major Siri upgrade expected later in 2026.

sources.title: European Commission press release IP/16/2923: State aid - Ireland gave illegal tax benefits to Apple worth up to €13 billion
sources.claims: On 2016-08-30 the European Commission decided that Ireland granted illegal state aid worth up to €13 billion to Apple through 1991 and 2007 tax rulings concerning Apple Sales International and Apple Operations Europe, and ordered recovery of the unpaid taxes for 2003-2014.
sources.claims_weakened: The Commission's own finding, later annulled by the General Court in 2020 before the ECJ reinstated it in 2024; the amount is an estimate of unpaid tax plus interest.

sources.title: Clifford Chance: The EU's €13 billion Apple tax recovery order
sources.claims: Apple had two entities incorporated in Ireland, Apple Sales International and Apple Operations Europe, each with an Irish branch taxable in Ireland and a head office not subject to Irish tax; the entities held the intellectual property rights to manufacture and sell Apple products outside the Americas under a cost-sharing agreement with Apple Inc.
sources.claims_weakened: Law-firm briefing on the 2016 Commission decision; describes the pre-2015 structure, not Apple's current Irish entity roles.

sources.title: CNBC: Apple stock split announced

sources.claims_weakened: Announcement only; does not give the effective date or the split history.

sources.title: Strasmore: Apple stock split history and ratios

sources.claims_weakened: Secondary blog compilation; does not reconcile the exact split-adjusted prices.

sources.title: MacRumors: Apple Reaches 2.5 Billion Active Devices (2026-01-29)
sources.claims: Apple announced on 2026-01-29 that its installed base exceeded 2.5 billion active devices, up from more than 2.35 billion a year earlier, quoting Tim Cook; supports the Services attach and upgrade-pool argument.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the 2.3 billion installed-base figure and any statement that Apple discloses no device count; Apple still discloses no replacement rate or device mix.

sources.title: TrendForce: Diverging Memory Market Outlook in 2027 as DRAM Supply Remains Tight While NAND Flash Supply Conditions Ease
sources.claims: DRAM sufficiency ratio -1% to -2% in 2026 and the supply-demand gap widens in 2027; new DRAM capacity ramps meaningfully only in 2H27 with substantial output not until 2028; consumer electronics including smartphones and notebooks stay under pressure with another year of declining shipments in 2027; NAND loosens in 2H27.
sources.claims_weakened: The base case that memory normalises around 2028 and that gross margin gives back only about one point in FY2027; IDC's 2028 normalisation timing is consistent for DRAM but leaves FY2027 exposed.

sources.title: CNBC: Apple shares downgraded due to memory chip inflation
sources.claims: Phillip Capital cut Apple to reduce on 2026-08-04 with a $290 target, citing memory inflation as a major margin headwind; management expects memory prices to keep rising in 4Q26 and beyond; carry-in inventory, mix and non-memory costs offset it only for a time; DRAM has three suppliers, leaving little sourcing flexibility; Apple fell nearly 10% after the 2026-07-30 results on weak guidance tied to the chip crunch; Apple had already raised iPad and Mac prices.
sources.claims_weakened: The base case that the FY2026 margin give-back is about one point and self-correcting; the assumption that Apple can absorb memory inflation without demand loss.

sources.title: Pip Theory: Apple Q4 FY2026 earnings preview — 47-48% margin guided, inventory doubled
sources.claims: Apple guided fiscal Q4 2026 revenue growth of 9-11% (about $111.7-113.7bn) and gross margin of 47-48% including about 1 point of tariff refunds, i.e. roughly 46-47% ex-refunds against 48.1% ex-refund in the June quarter; consensus about $113.3bn revenue and $1.99 EPS; carry-in inventory benefit said to fade after September; Cook called the memory environment a once-in-a-century flood; CFO Parekh said the memory cost increase was larger than the entire fall in gross margin from June to the September guide.
sources.claims_weakened: Any reading of the 50.1% June-quarter margin as a new floor: Apple's own September guide implies a 2.1-3.1 point sequential decline and a lower underlying margin than a year earlier.

sources.title: TechNode: Huawei grows as China's smartphone shipments fall 15.4% in Q3 2026 (IDC)
sources.claims: IDC preliminary data reported 2026-10-13: China smartphone shipments fell 15.4% year on year to 57.9m units in Q3 2026, a sixth straight quarterly decline; Apple shipments fell 4.3% but its share rose to 17.8% from 15.8%; Huawei was the only major vendor with double-digit growth, shipping 12.2m units for about 21% share.
sources.claims_weakened: The read that Apple's 30% Greater China revenue growth reflects durable share gains rather than a shrinking-market mix effect; it also shows China volume falling under the June-quarter run rate.

sources.title: Law360: DOJ, Google want D.C. Circuit priority for search appeal
sources.claims: The DOJ and Google jointly asked the D.C. Circuit to give their cross-appeals priority so that oral argument could be scheduled as soon as 2026-12-09 in the search monopolization remedies appeal.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that the Google search-payment risk is a 2027-2028 tail: argument is set for December 2026, so a ruling on whether distribution payments can be barred outright is plausible within the twelve-month window.

sources.title: Invezz: Apple stock falls after Jefferies downgrade to Underperform, $263.66 target
sources.claims: Jefferies cut Apple to Underperform on 2026-08-10 and lowered its price target to $263.66 from $285.56, citing rising memory costs, a weakening premium iPhone roadmap and underwhelming AI monetisation.
sources.claims_weakened: The base case fair value of $296: an independent sell-side bear case lands about 11% below it and close to a margin-cut earnings base at a normal multiple.

sources.title: Computerworld: How Satya Nadella navigated Microsoft to $3 trillion market value
sources.claims: Microsoft's market value rose from about $381 billion in early 2014, when Nadella became CEO, to about $3 trillion a decade later, as the cloud transition replaced declining PC-licence revenue; much of the return came from re-rating a low starting multiple as well as earnings growth.
sources.claims_weakened: Cautions against reading a successful incumbent transition as repeatable at a 39.5x starting multiple: Microsoft began near 10-12x earnings, so its rerating had room that Apple's does not.

sources.title: 9to5Mac: Apple sets Q4 2026 earnings release for November 2
sources.claims: Apple guided fiscal Q4 2026 gross margin of 47%-48%, down from 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter, which included a roughly two-percentage-point benefit from tariff refunds; results scheduled for 2026-11-02.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any assumption that the 50.1% June-quarter gross margin is a floor: the company's own guide implies a 2-3 point decline including one point of refunds.

sources.title: The curse of agility: the Nokia Corporation and the loss of market dominance in mobile phones, 2003-2013
sources.claims: Nokia held roughly 40-50% of global mobile phone share in 2007 and fell below 5% by 2013 as the smartphone platform shift moved value to software ecosystems it did not control; the decline took about six years from the iPhone launch to the sale of the devices business.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any view that device leadership is durable through a platform shift; supports pricing the AI interface shift as a real risk even for a share leader.

sources.title: AppleInsider: Jefferies cuts AAPL target to $263.66, downgrades to underperform
sources.claims: Jefferies downgraded Apple to underperform on 2026-08-10 and cut its price target to $263.66 from $285.56, citing supply-chain checks that the all-glass anniversary iPhone had been cancelled and rising memory costs; the target implied about 16% downside from the then-price.
sources.claims_weakened: Provides an independent sell-side anchor near the margin-adjusted base value of about $268, against a consensus target of $339.35.

sources.title: Intel to Acquire Infineon's Wireless Solutions Business (30 August 2010)

sources.claims: Every Galaxy S25 model shipped on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025, with no Exynos variant, after Samsung's 4nm yield problems; Galaxy S23 was also all-Snapdragon in 2023; Samsung retired its Mongoose custom CPU cores in 2020 after middling efficiency results. sources.claims: Worldwide AI patent grants reached 107,279 in 2025, up 83% on three years earlier. 2025 AI filings: Samsung 2,162 worldwide (682 US), Huawei 1,822, Google 1,672; US filings Samsung 682, Google 671, Microsoft 585. Apple is absent from the cited top-three AI applicant rankings. Establishes a peer base rate for AI patenting against which Apple's portfolio can be benchmarked.

sources.claims: Intel completed the sale of its smartphone modem business to Apple for $1bn, announced 2019-07-25, exiting phone modems roughly nine years after buying Infineon's WLS unit (closed Q1 2011).
sources.claims_weakened: Undermines a four-to-five-year replication assumption for a phone-modem business by a well-capitalised new entrant.

sources.title: IFI Claims 2025 US patent grants ranking, reported by United Daily News / jcpatent (14 January 2026)
sources.claims: 2025 US patent grants: Samsung Electronics 7,054 (first, fourth consecutive year), TSMC 4,194 (second), Qualcomm third, Huawei 3,052 (fourth), Apple 2,722 (sixth, down 11.6% from 3,082 in 2024). Total US grants 323,272 in 2025, down 0.2%; applications down 8.6% to 393,344.
sources.claims_weakened: A secondary-language report of IFI data; counts granted US patents, not families, so it is a proxy for portfolio breadth only and says nothing about AI, health, foldable or AR sub-portfolios.

sources.title: IDC: Smart Glasses Market 2026 — XR is rewriting the rules (Q1 2026 units and 2026-2030 forecast)
sources.claims: Display-less smart glasses shipped about 2.25m units in Q1 2026, up 167% YoY, versus 2.7m for the whole of 2024; IDC forecasts 13.6m display-less units and $5.1bn revenue in 2026, 27.3m units by 2030 (18.9% CAGR), with ASP falling from about $376 in 2026 to $229 by 2030; Meta held 69.2% of Q1 2026 units and Alibaba ranked third at 2.6% on the popularity of Qwen; mixed reality grows from 3.2m units in 2026 to 10.4m by 2030.

sources.title: TechCrunch: OpenAI's first hardware device is reportedly a screenless speaker that can move
sources.claims: OpenAI's first hardware product is reported to be a screenless, movable home speaker pitched as an AI companion drawing on a user's emails and digital life, built with former Apple engineers; the form factor is unconfirmed; Apple sued OpenAI over trade secrets in July 2026 and OpenAI denied wrongdoing.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the idea of an imminent OpenAI phone; the first device is a home speaker, and Apple's response has been litigation rather than a product.

sources.title: IDC: Smart glasses growth cools to 35% in Q2 2026 as Meta doubles down on distribution
sources.claims: XR headsets and glasses shipments grew 35.3% YoY in Q2 2026 after 130.2% in Q1 2026; audio (display-less) glasses were 70.3% of units and display glasses 14.3%; Meta held 68.7% of Q2 2026 units (RayNeo 3.6%, Alibaba 2.6%, XREAL 2.5%, Xiaomi 2.3%); IDC forecasts total unit growth of 26.3% in 2026, 40.5% in 2027 and 26.4% in 2028, with Snap, Samsung/XREAL Android XR and new Meta display/audio glasses due in late 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that smart glasses remain a niche with no bearing on premium phone demand; also shows the category is still an order of magnitude smaller than smartphones in units.

sources.title: FoneArena: HONOR's smartphone shipments grew 53% in H1 2026, leads the foldable segment (citing IDC)
sources.claims: IDC data reported by FoneArena shows HONOR's global smartphone shipments grew 53% in H1 2026, the only Chinese Android vendor to grow, and HONOR held more than 50% of the foldable market in Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong.
sources.claims_weakened: A media summary of IDC tracker data rather than the tracker itself; the absolute HONOR share is not given, and IDC's Q2 2026 top-five table places HONOR outside the top five globally.

sources.title: Meta: Making Meta Ray-Ban Display More Useful to More People (Connect 2026)
sources.claims: Meta Ray-Ban Display starts at $799 in the US, £749 in the UK, CA$1,149 in Canada and €899 in France, Italy and Germany; on 2026-09-23 it went on sale in the UK and Canada, with France, Italy and Germany from 2026-10-13 and online ordering in the US; Meta added an on-glasses app discovery surface (Explore), hologram calls and mirrored phone notifications, and offers prescription lenses through EssilorLuxottica retail.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows display glasses are a $799 accessory tethered to a phone, not a $581 phone substitute; distribution is retail-led and country-by-country.

sources.title: Spheron: DeepSeek V3.2 vs Llama 4 vs Qwen 3 (2026) — cost per token and self-hosting requirements
sources.claims: Open-weight families Qwen3-32B (Apache 2.0), Llama 4 Scout (Llama community licence) and DeepSeek V3.2 (MIT) are production-ready; Qwen3-32B runs on one H100 at about $0.82 per million tokens on-demand ($0.34 spot) and Llama 4 Scout at about $0.87, while DeepSeek V3.2 needs eight H100s at about $13.89 per million tokens; GPU rates are dated 2026-10-31.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows the assistant layer can be self-hosted for under $1 per million tokens on a single GPU, undermining any claim that only a few firms can run frontier-class assistants; a commercial GPU vendor's blog, and its benchmark caveats are self-declared as unverified.

scope.decision: Whether Apple (AAPL) merits a place on Meridian Capital's long-only watchlist, and at what price or under what conditions it would become an investable position.

spines.must_answer: Is the market mispricing Apple's future cash flow or its risk — does the current price already discount a durable iPhone upgrade cycle, services growth and regulatory defence, leaving no margin of safety for a long-only fund? Answered: the price discounts a 50% gross margin floor and 11.8% free-cash-flow growth for a decade; on a margin-adjusted base of $268 the stock is 22% above fair value and the probability-weighted value of $266 is a 23% negative return, so the fund watchlists it with entry bands at $240-265 and at or below $225.

Is Apple demand durable or promotion-driven — do the installed base, upgrade rate, services attach and pricing power hold through a weak consumer cycle and through Huawei's recovery in China? Answered: demand is replacement-led; units fall 16.7% in 2026 while value rises 6.3%, the installed base exceeds 2.5bn devices, Services grow 14.1% but the mix moved back to hardware, and China grew 30.0% in nine months against a forecast 20% unit decline in H2 2026.

Does policy create a moat or a hidden constraint — how much of services gross profit is exposed to DMA and DOJ remedies and the Google distribution payment, and how much of hardware cost is exposed to China tariffs and a Taiwan contingency? Answered: the reported $20bn search payment is 22% of services gross profit and 9.4% of market value at 30x, preserved only on one-year non-exclusive terms under appeal; DMA and DOJ remedies are a recurring tax on the same layer; tariffs spared Apple products in 2026 but the truce expires on 2027-01-10.

research_plan.industry_map: Consumer technology value chain: semiconductor design (Apple silicon in-house; TSMC the sole advanced-node foundry), memory (SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung), displays (Samsung Display, LG Display, BOE), cameras and RF (Sony, Broadcom, Skyworks, Qorvo), assembly (Foxconn/Hon Hai, Pegatron, Luxshare, Tata in India), distribution (carriers, Apple Retail, e-commerce), platform services (App Store, iCloud, Apple Pay, advertising, Apple TV+, Music, Arcade), developers and regulators. Decisive bottleneck: advanced-node foundry capacity at TSMC (N3/N2) and the geographic concentration of final assembly in China — the first caps performance-per-watt leadership, the second carries tariff and geopolitical risk. In 2026 the binding constraint moved to memory: DRAM and NAND are up more than 300% year on year, memory is more than 65% of bill of materials at the low end, and Samsung is the only top-five handset vendor that also sells memory. Apple sits at the integration point where it captures most industry profit: it designs the SoC and the OS, controls the retail and services interface, and outsources capital-intensive manufacturing.
research_plan.geo_lens: Material. Apple reports five regions — Americas, Greater China, Europe, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific — and its supply chain runs through China, India, Vietnam, Taiwan, Korea and Japan. Mapped: (1) revenue and profit by region, with China demand and Huawei competition separated from the global average; (2) the manufacturing shift from China to India and Vietnam and the tariff exposure that drives it; (3) jurisdiction-specific regulation — EU Digital Markets Act, US DOJ antitrust, China's CAC and app-store rules, India's production-linked incentives; (4) tax jurisdiction (Ireland, OECD Pillar Two) and FX translation. Nine-month FY2026 evidence: Greater China +30.0% to $64.8bn, Europe +16.1% to $95.6bn, Americas +11.4% to $149.4bn; India about 55m iPhone units, 25% of global output, projected 28% in 2026; USD/CNY at 6.6449 on 2026-10-31.
research_plan.policy_lens: Material and decisive for services economics. Mapped and dated: (1) EU Digital Markets Act — €500m fine on 2025-04-23 for anti-steering, Article 6(4) alternative-marketplace file open, General Court upheld gatekeeper designation on 2026-07-08, interoperability rules may withhold Siri AI in the EU; (2) US DOJ antitrust case filed 2024-03-21, dismissal denied 2025-06-30, discovery toward a 2027 trial; (3) Epic v. Apple contempt finding 2025-04-30, Ninth Circuit modification 2025-12-11, Supreme Court certiorari 2026-06-30 limited to the civil-contempt standard; (4) Google search-distribution remedies — D.D.C. decision 2025-09-02 refused a payment ban but permits non-exclusive, one-year-or-shorter placement, final judgment December 2025, appeals by Google (January 2026) and the DOJ and states (February 2026) pending at 2026-10-29, argument sought from 2026-12-09; (5) US tariffs — Section 232 initial results 2026-01-14 imposed no tariff on Apple products, IEEPA tariffs struck down 2026-02-20 with refunds claimed, Section 301 tariffs then imposed, Busan truce extended 2026-09-23 to 2027-01-10; (6) China — CAC registered Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15 with Alibaba Qwen and Baidu, Greater China revenue +30.0% in nine months; (7) OECD Pillar Two and the Irish state-aid case, ECJ 2024-09-10, $15.8bn paid, FY2025 effective tax rate 15.6%.

gates: Confirm company identity, legal entity, geography, stage, and business model.
Decide whether the geographic market context lens is material; if yes, map home, revenue, expansion, supplier, comparable-company, capital, exit markets and the investor perspective.
Decide whether the policy and geopolitics lens is material; if yes, map jurisdictions and perspective.
Complete the profile requirements before drafting.
Build the source register with source type, date, confidence, claims and a link or file/page reference.
Use visible source IDs such as [S1] as citations in the report.
Complete the evidence matrix for all material sections before drafting.
Run the pre-draft evidence gate and fix failures.
Draft the report from evidence, not from outline memory.
Run the red-team pass and rewrite weak sections.
Run final QA, print the PDF, and verify the delivery folder.
research_plan.hypothesis: Watchlist, not buy: Apple's franchise is intact — more than 2.5bn active devices, a 76.3% services gross margin, $136.7bn trailing free cash flow and $62.2bn of net cash — but the price capitalises a margin the company has guided away. At $344.63 (2026-10-30) the stock trades at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x consensus forward earnings against a 21.0x peer median and a 4.93% ten-year Treasury. Apple guided September-quarter gross margin of 47-48%, including 1 point of tariff refunds, on its 2026-07-30 earnings call; two points of give-back is 6.3% of net income and leaves FY2027 EPS near $8.87, not the $9.79 consensus, so base value is $268 at 30.2x, with a bear of $205 and a bull of $399. Weighted 15/50/35, value is $266, a 23% negative return. The fund holds no position, takes a 1-2% starter at $240-265 and a 3-4% position at or below $225, capped at 4% because the reported $20bn search payment is 9.4% of market value and sits inside a 2026-12-09 appellate window. The 2026-11-02 December guide decides the case. Genuine open questions: the refund and inventory split in the FY2026 annual report, the measured replacement rate, and whether the AI layer ever becomes revenue rather than cost.
research_plan.author: Lead Analyst

items: Use web and data tools for fresh facts whenever a company, market, price, policy, filing, funding, or executive fact may have changed.
For each major section, record targeted search strings, opened sources, source IDs, and why the selected sources are decision-grade rather than merely convenient.
Use the server's checks for deterministic QA, extraction, citation checks and the delivery folder; do not rely on a one-shot narrative draft.
Do not generate repeated filler paragraphs such as per-section original-document priority, citation-anchor blocks, or repeated metric-card copy; each section must contain content-specific analysis.
Before drafting, write a section distinctness plan: the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, and best visual artifact for each section.
For each section, draft one final-report thesis sentence that directly analyzes the company; never copy internal plan labels or rubric language into the report.
Remove repeated visible scaffolds such as "Economic mechanism", "Comparison and benchmark", "Counter-evidence and risk" and "Investor implication"; keep the scaffold internal.
Use a verdict strip, compact decision cards, selected tables, and at most a few KPI strips; do not repeat the same card, grid or dashboard pattern in every section.
Before writing the executive briefing, summarize the non-consensus or consensus view and the exact evidence that changes the decision.
Treat OCR as a pipeline: inventory files, OCR scan- or slide-heavy material, and keep page, slide or table references for every extracted claim.
Check every page holding numbers, TAM, valuation, customers, clinical or regulatory claims, policy claims, financing terms or team credentials before relying on it.
Mark OCR-derived claims low confidence until checked or corroborated; use ranges for OCR-derived financial inputs.
Build a claim verification table for material company-provided claims: verified, partially verified, unverified, contradicted, or not publicly disclosed.
profile_requirements.evidence: All thirteen profile items are met. Scope and plan: Apple Inc. (AAPL, listed, Nasdaq), decision whether it merits a place on Meridian Capital's long-only watchlist and at what price; three spines (public equity, consumer/brand, policy/geopolitics), the value chain and decisive bottleneck, the geographic and policy lenses and twelve registries. All fourteen sections are saved and pass their checks; technology_product's patent-number limitation is stated, and the section now carries IFI benchmarks (2025 US grants: Apple 2,722 vs Samsung 7,054; AI filings: Samsung 2,162, Huawei 1,822, Google 1,672) [S206-S211], with barrier scores capped at 8/10 hardware and 4/10 AI and no IP credit. Evidence base: 217 registered sources including SEC filings, Nasdaq market data, FRED rates, European Commission and D.D.C. records and dated 2026 market data. The thesis uses a margin-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $8.87 against $9.79 consensus, base value $268, bear $205 and bull $399, weighted 15/50/35 to $266, a 23% negative return from the $344.63 close of 2026-10-30; rating Watchlist, with a starter band of $240-265 and a full position at or below $225, capped at 4% because the reported $20bn search payment is 9.4% of market value [S118, S82]. After the first committee review, the margin-adjusted case and the 15/50/35 weights are used in every section; exit was rebuilt on the $268 base and $266 expected value with a 17% maximum loss at the $225 entry; the buyback is dated to successive authorisations of 2025-05-01 and 2026-04-30 [S204, S205]; and the installed base is stated at more than 2.5bn devices with about $187 of revenue per device a year [S150, S191]. User data requests: four filed (D.N.J. docket, USPTO/Espacenet export, Companies Registration Office Ireland, Q3 FY2026 earnings-call transcript).
profile_requirements.author: Lead Analyst

rows.belief: The need is replacement and ecosystem retention, not unmet demand: buyers delay upgrades and pay for services inside iOS. More than 2.5bn active devices and revenue up 16.2% in nine months of FY2026 while global units fall.
rows.evidence: Installed base above 2.5bn active devices, announced 2026-01-29 [S191]; nine-month FY2026 revenue $364.4bn, +16.2% [S6]; services 25.2% of revenue [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Global smartphone units fall 16.7% to about 1.0bn in 2026 and the sub-$100 tier nearly collapsed, so part of the willingness to pay is a supply shock, not demand [S66, S39].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: Two consecutive quarters of falling services attach or a measured lengthening of the replacement cycle beyond the current estimate.

rows.belief: Apple's integration lead is durable in silicon and distribution (8/10) and thin in AI (4/10): the A20 Pro is on TSMC N2 and the C2 modem reached the flagship, but the next foundation models are licensed from Google.
rows.evidence: A20 Pro on TSMC N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine; C2 in the iPhone 18 line [S64, S59]; Gemini-based Apple Foundation Models announced 2026-01-12 [S58]; services gross margin 76.3% [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Siri needed a Google licence, Vision Pro shipped about 45,000 units in the December 2025 quarter, and DMA rules may withhold Siri AI in the EU [S6, S87, S86].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A disclosed in-house frontier model, or AI features producing a measurable lift in upgrade rates rather than cost.

rows.belief: 2026 is a supply-shock year that flatters Apple's unit share and price; the honest test of the franchise is 2028, when memory normalises and the premium tier rebuilds.
rows.evidence: DRAM and NAND up more than 300% year on year; 2026 market value $613bn, +6.3%, on units down 16.7% [S66, S39]; IDC sees memory normalising around 2028 [S39].
rows.counter_evidence: Apple's 20.2% unit share gain was bought with early memory supply that lapses, while Samsung both competes in handsets and sells the memory [S102, S66].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: Memory prices normalising earlier than 2028, or Apple holding share after they do.

rows.belief: Distribution is the moat: 60% of sales run through carriers and resellers that finance the device, keeping selling expense at 6.6% of revenue, and India assembly is scaling as a tariff hedge.
rows.evidence: 40% direct and 60% indirect in FY2025 [S5]; iPhone output in India about 55m units, 25% of global, projected 28% in 2026 [S91]; selling, general and administrative $27.6bn, 6.6% of revenue [S5].
rows.counter_evidence: India assembly captures little value because components and silicon remain East Asian, and Apple has never disclosed the US-bound share [S91, S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A channel disruption at a major carrier, or India failing to reach the projected share of output without a quality incident.

rows.belief: A device is gross-profit-positive on delivery at a 39.9% product margin and the services stream is nearly all incremental, but the annuity no longer grows faster than the hardware that creates it and the margin is turning.
rows.evidence: Products 39.9% and Services 76.3% gross margin in nine months of FY2026 [S6]; services gross profit per dollar of product gross profit fell to $0.64 from $0.73 [S5, S6]; September-quarter guide of 47-48% including 1 point of refunds [S199].
rows.counter_evidence: Part of the product margin is a tariff refund (2.0 points of the June quarter) and memory costs are rising [S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Services gross profit growing faster than product gross profit for two quarters, or the mix ratio recovering above $0.73.

rows.belief: Succession is done and internal, which lowers cultural risk, but the new CEO has never run a P&L and the AI transition sits with a software chief who outsourced the frontier model.
rows.evidence: Ternus CEO from 2026-09-01, Cook executive chair, Levinson lead independent [S152, S174]; AI organisation rebuilt on 2025-12-01 under an external hire reporting to Federighi [S183].
rows.counter_evidence: Five C-suite changes since January 2025, no board member with AI-lab operating experience, and key-person dependence on Srouji and Federighi [S179, S65].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A senior AI or silicon departure, or the first year of Ternus's capital-allocation decisions at the current multiple.

rows.belief: The business is high quality and the price is not: 39.5x trailing and 35.2x consensus forward earnings, 88% above the mega-cap peer median, or 38.9x the margin-adjusted $8.87, with a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year Treasury.
rows.evidence: Close $344.63 on 2026-10-30, market cap $5,029.6bn, EV $4,967.4bn [S9, S6]; peer median 21.0x P/E [S124-S126]; ten-year Treasury 4.93% [S9].
rows.counter_evidence: Apple's 36.8x price-to-free-cash-flow is 43% below the peer median of 64.6x because capex is only $10.0bn a year [S9, S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A durable step-up in free cash flow that closes the reverse-DCF gap, or a de-rating toward 25-30x forward.

rows.belief: There is no takeover or listing event: exit is an open-market sale, so the sell discipline is a set of price bands and thesis breaks rather than a liquidity question.
rows.evidence: Largest technology deal on record equals 1.4% of Apple's market value [S169]; average daily traded value $13.84bn [S9]; ten-year average intra-year drawdown 21.4% [S163].
rows.counter_evidence: A 30x-plus multiple may never offer a margin of safety again, so a strict band risks never owning the asset [S163].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A structural change in the shareholder base or capital return that changes the multiple floor.

rows.belief: Today's price is about 22% above base fair value once the guided margin give-back is carried through: the reverse DCF needs 11.8% free-cash-flow growth for a decade against 1.5% delivered in FY2021-FY2025.
rows.evidence: Base $268 on margin-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $8.87 at 30.2x; bear $205 at 25x on $8.20; bull $399 at 38x on $10.50 [S199, S201, S6]; sum of the parts $2.25-3.42trn against a $4.97trn EV [S13, S5, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: The market has paid an expanding multiple through a rising discount rate, and the services annuity plus buyback may justify a premium that peer multiples understate [S156, S154].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: FY2026 annual report or the December guide showing normalised gross margin at or above 48%.

rows.belief: Headline growth overstates the business: FY2025's 22.7% EPS growth is 10.4% once the Irish charge is normalised, 2.0 points of the June 2026 gross margin were tariff refunds, and the company has guided another point for September.
rows.evidence: Pretax income +7.5% against net income +19.5% in FY2025 [S5]; gross margin 50.1% in the June quarter including a 2.0-point refund [S6]; 47-48% September guide including 1 point [S199]; inventory +87% year on year against revenue +16.2% [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Cash conversion is strong at 1.06x net income and the refund is a one-time cash item, not an accounting invention [S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: The FY2026 10-K decomposing refund and mix, and confirming inventory is a launch build rather than unsold stock.

rows.belief: Cash generation is the strongest part of the record and the least dependent on accounting judgement: $136.7bn trailing free cash flow on $10.0bn of capex.
rows.evidence: Operating cash flow $146.7bn against capex $10.0bn, 1.06x net income, in the twelve months to 2026-06-27 [S6]; capex 2.2% of revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft [S6, S27].
rows.counter_evidence: FY2025 conversion fell to 0.88x on $43.4bn of cash taxes, and the trailing figure benefits from a working-capital swing that is reversing as inventory builds [S5, S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Cash taxes or inventory returning conversion below 0.95x for a full year.

rows.belief: There is no solvency risk: $62.2bn of net cash, commercial paper cut to $2.0bn, and debt maturities that do not test the business.
rows.evidence: $146.5bn of cash and securities against $84.3bn of debt at 2026-06-27 [S6]; net cash up from $33.8bn at FY2025 year-end [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: The $57.0bn of manufacturing purchase obligations fix component costs just as memory prices peak [S6].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A debt-funded acquisition of scale, or purchase obligations rising faster than revenue.

rows.belief: We are below consensus on the earnings base, not on the near-term revenue: consensus FY2027 EPS is $9.79 against our $8.87, the average target of $339.35 sits below the $344.63 close, and guidance for the 2026-11-02 quarter is revenue growth of 9-11%.
rows.evidence: Consensus target $339.35 from 50 analysts, range $245-$405 [S158, S160]; consensus EPS $9.79 [S157]; fiscal fourth-quarter results due 2026-11-02 with revenue guided up 9-11% and gross margin 47-48% [S1, S199]; Jefferies at $263.66 [S201].
rows.counter_evidence: Analyst targets lag price in a momentum market, and the stock has returned 27.5% in twelve months against 10.8% for the S&P 500 [S9].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A holiday-quarter guide above 12% with gross margin above 48% ex-refund, or a miss below 9%.

rows.belief: The next twelve months carry five dated tests: FY2026 results and annual report on 2026-11-02, argument in the Google remedies appeal from 2026-12-09, the DOJ case schedule into 2027, the Busan truce expiry on 2027-01-10 and the first one-year renewal of the search payment.
rows.evidence: Q4 FY2026 results due 2026-11-02 [S1, S199]; Google and DOJ appeals pending at 2026-10-29 with argument sought from 2026-12-09 [S118, S42, S196]; DOJ trial schedule to 2027 [S122]; truce extended to 2027-01-10 [S121].
rows.counter_evidence: Legal timelines slip: the DOJ case has already run two and a half years to reach discovery [S122].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A settlement in either antitrust case, or the FY2026 report arriving with an unexpected margin disclosure.

rows.belief: Zero at $344.63: the probability-weighted value is about $275 against a margin-adjusted base of $268, so the fund should watchlist the name, take a starter position at $240-265 and a full position at or below $225, trimming above $395.
rows.evidence: Scenario expected value $275 against a $344.63 close, a -20% expected return [S199, S154, S163]; bear $205 and bull $399 [S6, S157]; 8% annual return at today's price requires a 35x exit multiple [S154].
rows.counter_evidence: Waiting for $265 may never be rewarded if services compound at 14% and the buyback retires 1.6% of the shares a year, so the band needs a time rule after four quarters above $296.
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A December guide that restores gross margin above 48% ex-refund would raise the base toward $296 and the starter band toward $270.

scenarios.driver: Memory cost pass-through holds gross margin near 48% through price rises on the iPhone 18 and Duo, the AI-assisted cycle lifts upgrades, services reaccelerate above 15%, and the Google payment renews near current terms.
scenarios.evidence: Nine-month revenue +16.2% with iPhone +22% and Greater China +30% [S6, S13]; services gross margin 76.3% [S6]; foldable Duo on sale 2026-10-23 at $1,999 [S59]; iPad and Mac price rises absorbed in 2026 [S194].
scenarios.outcome: FY2027 EPS about $10.50 at a 38x multiple gives $399, +16% from $344.63, plus the 0.3% dividend.
scenarios.implication: A holder is paid; a watchlist buyer misses the move and must reset the band rather than chase above $395.

scenarios.driver: The tariff refund rolls off, memory costs take two points of gross margin, FY2027 EPS lands near $8.87 rather than the $9.79 consensus, services compound in the low teens, and the multiple sits at its five-year average of 30.2x.
scenarios.evidence: Apple's 2026-07-30 release reports June-quarter gross margin of 50.1% including approximately 2 points of tariff refunds [S13, S6]; the 47-48% September guide, including 1 point of refunds, is company guidance on the earnings call (transcript-based) [S202]; two points on $490bn of revenue is $9.8bn pretax, 6.3% of net income; five-year average P/E 30.2x [S154].
scenarios.outcome: FY2027 EPS of $8.87 at 30.2x gives $268, -22% from $344.63, with a 0.3% dividend.
scenarios.implication: The fund waits: no position at today's price, a starter position at $240-265.

scenarios.driver: Memory costs and a normalising mix take gross margin toward 45%, while a US or EU remedy cuts commission or the search payment is repriced at its one-year renewal or on appeal; the multiple compresses to 25x.
scenarios.evidence: Two-point give-back takes EPS to $8.20, or $7.11 with the search licence lost [S6]; the reported ~$20bn payment is 22% of services gross profit, and the D.D.C. remedies decision of 2025-09-02 permits only non-exclusive, one-year-or-shorter placement, with appeals pending at 2026-10-29 [S5, S6, S118, S42]; DOJ trial schedule to 2027 [S122].
scenarios.outcome: $8.20 at 25x gives $205, -41% from $344.63; with the licence lost, $7.11 at 25x gives $178, -48%.
scenarios.implication: The full-position entry at or below $225 carries a 17% mark-to-market loss if the multiple de-rates to 21x on the margin-adjusted $8.87 EPS ($186 against $225), and a starter at the $265 top of the band would lose 30% to that case and 22.6% to the $205 bear, so the position is sized for it rather than bought through it.

assumptions.assumption: Gross margin settles at 46-47% in FY2027 once the tariff refund and inventory cushion normalise, not at the 48-49% the consensus EPS implies
assumptions.disproof: Two quarters of gross margin at or above 48% ex-refund, or a December guide at or above 48%
assumptions.impact: Two points of give-back takes EPS from trailing $8.72 to $8.87 on higher revenue and the base value to $268, 22% below the close; one point is 3.0% of net income
assumptions.early_warning: December-quarter guide below 46% ex-refund on 2026-11-02; DRAM sufficiency negative through 2027; inventory up 87% year on year

assumptions.assumption: The Google search-distribution payment survives at or near its reported ~$20bn a year, repriced annually and non-exclusive
assumptions.disproof: An appellate remedy banning distributor payments, or a renewal at a materially lower rate
assumptions.impact: About $20bn a year, 17% of Services revenue and 22% of services gross profit; at 30x it is roughly $474bn, 9.4% of market value
assumptions.early_warning: D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09; terms of the first one-year renewal; any disclosure in the FY2026 10-K

assumptions.assumption: Services revenue keeps compounding in the low-to-mid teens without a mandated take-rate collapse
assumptions.disproof: Two consecutive quarters below 5% growth, or a DMA or DOJ remedy that strips commission on a material share of transactions
assumptions.impact: A three-point services growth cut removes roughly $3.6bn of revenue and, at a 76% margin, about 2.8% of net income
assumptions.early_warning: EU Article 6(4) proceedings; US link-out spending migration; services growth of 14.1% in nine months of FY2026 decelerating

assumptions.assumption: The iPhone 18 and Duo cycle sustains high-single-digit revenue growth in FY2027 without tariff refunds
assumptions.disproof: A holiday quarter below the guided 9-11% or a Duo ramp that cannibalises Pro volumes without adding revenue
assumptions.impact: Each point of revenue growth is 1.5% of net income; a return to the FY2025 rate of 6.4% cuts about $10bn of revenue against the nine-month run-rate
assumptions.early_warning: FY2026 results on 2026-11-02; first full quarter of Duo at $1,999; China shipments down about 20% in H2 2026

assumptions.assumption: The buyback continues at roughly the current pace, so EPS compounds faster than net income
assumptions.disproof: A pause or reduction in repurchases at 39.5x, or a debt-funded acquisition that displaces capital return
assumptions.impact: Buybacks added 1.9 points of EPS growth in the trailing twelve months; stopping them cuts EPS growth by about two points and removes the 1.6% buyback yield
assumptions.early_warning: Repurchases already down to $61.8bn from $70.6bn in nine months; successive $100bn authorisations of 2025-05-01 and 2026-04-30

consensus.consensus: The sell side and the market treat Apple as a quality compounder whose services annuity and buyback justify a premium: the average target is $339.35, the stock closed at $344.63 on 2026-10-30, and consensus FY2027 EPS is $9.79, a 12.3% rise on trailing $8.72.
consensus.our_view: Not consensus on the earnings base or the price: Apple's June gross margin of 50.1% included approximately 2 points of tariff refunds, and its call-stated September guide of 47-48% includes another point, so a two-point give-back leaves FY2027 EPS near $8.87 and the base value at $268, 22% below the close. The franchise is as good as the market says; the price assumes a margin floor that the company has already guided away.
consensus.evidence: Two points on ~$490bn of revenue is $9.8bn pretax, 6.3% of net income [S13, S6, S202]; Jefferies' $263.66 target of 2026-08-10 sits within 2% of that arithmetic [S201]; at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward the stock is 88% above the mega-cap peer median and 1.8x the S&P 500, with a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year [S9, S154, S155].
consensus.proof_event: The 2026-11-02 December-quarter guide is the first outlook without the carry-in inventory cushion; it will show whether gross margin ex-refund holds near 47% or falls toward 45%, which decides whether the base is $268 or $205.

one_question.question: Is Apple's ~50% gross margin a new floor, or a tariff-refund and memory-timing peak that flatters trailing EPS?
one_question.why: The entire valuation rests on the earnings base. Trailing EPS of $8.72 and the $9.79 consensus assume the 48.7% trailing gross margin holds; Apple's verified June gross margin of 50.1% included about 2 points of refunds [S13], and the call-stated 47-48% September guide, with one point of refunds, implies 46-47% ex-refund, and a two-point give-back takes EPS to $8.87 and the base to $268, while a further slide to 45% takes it to $205. One point of gross margin is 3.0% of net income, double the effect of one point of revenue growth, so this single number decides whether today's price is 20% too high or fairly valued.

modules.analogs: Two analogs bound the decision. Microsoft after 2014 is the best case: a legacy incumbent whose cloud transition replaced a declining licence business and whose market value rose from about $381bn to about $3tn in a decade [S198]. The lesson is not that transformation works; it is that Microsoft began near 10-12x earnings, so re-rating supplied much of the return. Apple starts at 39.5x, where the same transformation would have to come from earnings alone. Nokia is the cautionary case: 40-50% of global handsets in 2007, under 5% by 2013, because the platform shift moved value to software it did not control [S200]. Apple owns its platform and rents the frontier model, which places it closer to Microsoft's early cloud years than to Nokia's collapse; the difference is the price of admission.
modules.capital_efficiency: Capital efficiency is high on assets and poor on incremental equity: capex is 2.2% of revenue and free cash flow converts at 1.06x net income, but $82.2bn of buybacks and $15.6bn of dividends in twelve months equal 1.9% of market value, and each repurchased dollar retires stock at a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.93% Treasury. The buyback supports EPS more than value per share at this multiple. R&D rose 33% to $34.0bn in nine months with no disclosed AI revenue, so the incremental return on that spend is unproven.
modules.position_sizing: Listed, long-only. Position size zero at $344.63: the probability-weighted value is $266 on 15/50/35 case weights, so the edge is negative and the Kelly fraction is zero. At $250 the three cases return +60%, +7% and -18%; the expected return is +6.2% and a full-Kelly calculation implies 1.4 times notional, so the 4% cap binds and the cap is set by single-event regulatory risk, not by the arithmetic. A starter of 1-2% of the fund is justified at $240-265, and a full position of 3-4% at or below $225, where the expected return is +18% but the downside to a 21x de-rating on the margin-adjusted $8.87 EPS is 17% ($186); a starter at the $265 top of the band would lose 30% to that case. Cap at 4% because loss of the search payment is worth about 9.4% of market value. The regime caps the size: with the ten-year Treasury at 4.93% and the S&P 500 3.4% below its high, a 39.5x multiple carries de-rating risk.

answers.most_damaging_fact: The load-bearing fact is the margin path, not the consensus EPS: the base value of $268 rests on FY2027 EPS of $8.87, which assumes gross margin settles at 46-47% once the refund and the September guide roll off. Apple guided September gross margin of 47-48% including 1 point of refunds, so 46-47% ex-refund against 48.1% in June, and TrendForce has the DRAM gap widening into 2027 with substantial new output only in 2028 (S194, S192, S106). If margin instead holds at 48-49% through price and mix, FY2027 EPS is $10.50 and $344.63 is 32.8x — fair for this franchise, and the wrong-price call fails. Two points of give-back on ~$490bn of revenue is $9.8bn pretax, 6.3% of trailing net income; Jefferies' $263.66 of 2026-08-10 sits within 2% of the $268 arithmetic (S197). The 2026-11-02 December guide is where it is disclosed.
answers.company_only_claims: The installed base of 2.5bn active devices is company-reported: MacRumors restated it on 2026-01-29 (S191), and the thesis table cites S174, which is the 2026-04-20 succession announcement and does not contain the figure; the market section says no device count is published, so the citation is wrong even though the claim is supportable. 'All-time high across all major product categories and geographic segments' (S13) is unverified and unquantified. The 2-point tariff refund is company disclosure whose cash receipt is not shown (S13). The Gemini licence at ~$1bn a year is trade reporting confirmed by neither party (S58, S186). The $20bn Google payment is a 2022 court figure Apple has never confirmed (S82). S165 is a legal-news tracker asserting a payment ban effective June 2026, contradicted by the D.D.C. record (S118); it should be retired from citations.
answers.generic_section: technology_product is the weakest: it concedes the patent moat is unquantified because the registries could not be searched, its depth check fails on granularity (no patent numbers), and its barrier scores of 9/10 for silicon, 8/10 for hardware-OS integration and 10/10 for the installed base are judgements with no base rate, failed-analog test or peer benchmark. The generic artefact is 'a team of 50 senior engineers could match a phone-class SoC and OS in four to five years', which is asserted rather than evidenced. The market section's device-count contradiction (2.3bn unverified against 2.5bn in the thesis table) is the second gap.
answers.unpriced_risk: Three risks remain only partly priced. First, the margin give-back: the base now carries $8.87 and the band $240-265, but the 60% case of a 45% margin gives $248-257, inside the starter band, so a buyer at $265 pays full base value for a 60% risk. Second, the Google payment: the D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09 puts $474bn, 9.4% of market value, inside twelve months (S196, S82). Third, the buyback's value transfer at 39.5x — a 2.5% earnings yield against a 4.93% ten-year — is disclosed but not in the sizing, and a 4% cap does not offset it (S6, S164). The risk section prices all three; the recommendation's bands only partly reflect the first.
answers.first_challenge: An investment committee partner would challenge the band first: the 15/50/35 weights give $266, 23% below the $344.63 close, yet the starter band of $240-265 reaches to within 1% of the base value of $268, so the first purchase is made before the margin is proven and the December guide on 2026-11-02 could take EPS to $8.20-8.50. Second, why 35% is the right bear weight when the de-rating case at 21x on $8.87 is $186, 17% below the $225 full-position entry and 30% below the $265 top of the starter band; the risk section now states that 17% as the maximum loss, not the 9% the $205 bear alone implied. Third, the exit section's current revision carries the corrected 2025-09-02 D.D.C. remedies status, and the earlier payment-ban assertion is retired.
answers.downside_survival: The direction survives every stress; the bands now carry the arithmetic. At 15/50/35 the probability-weighted value is $266, a 23% negative return from $344.63 (S199, S6). Revenue 30% lower leaves $4.92 of EPS, or $123 at 25x; free cash flow 30% lower is about $156 a share; the 21.0x peer median on $8.87 is $186 (S6, S124-S126). A six-month financing delay is not applicable because Apple holds $62.2bn of net cash; refinancing $84.3bn at +200bp costs 1.1% of net income and a 20% inventory write-down 1.7% (S6). The $225 full-position entry loses 17% in the de-rating case, not the 9% the $205 bear alone implies, and the $265 top of the starter band loses 30%; zero at $344.63 and the $240-265/$225 bands hold.
answers.ocr_claims: No claim in this section is OCR-derived: the quarterly report, press release and segment tables were read as text through the filing tool, and market and industry figures came from registered sources retrieved in this run (S192-S197, S6, S13, S39, S40, S66, S82, S87, S102-S106, S118, S121, S124-S126, S154, S157, S161-S164). The only estimate presented as an estimate is the unaudited refund split, which is company-disclosed but whose cash receipt is not shown.

rows.finding: A20 Pro (iPhone 18 generation, September 2026) is Apple's first 2nm phone chip on TSMC N2 with a dual 16-core Neural Engine and about 52 TOPS, roughly double the A19 Pro's AI throughput; the A19 Pro (September 2025) was still TSMC N3P at up to 4.26 GHz.
rows.mechanism: Denser logic per watt is what lets a phone run a multi-billion-parameter model inside a thermal envelope, so node leadership translates directly into on-device AI capability and battery life; but N2 wafers at about $30,000 versus $18,000-20,000 for 3nm raise silicon cost per unit.
rows.benchmark: A19 Pro on N3P (2025) and 3nm wafer pricing of $18,000-20,000; product gross margin 39.9% for the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9% a year earlier.
rows.weakens: TOPS and wafer prices are trade-press estimates, not Apple or TSMC disclosure; N2 is TSMC's process, available to Qualcomm, MediaTek and others, so the node advantage is rented from a supplier, not owned.
rows.implication: Silicon leadership is real but compresses margin as node costs rise; price the iPhone gross margin at risk of memory and wafer inflation rather than assuming AI drives ASP up.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: What is the actual A20 Pro die cost and yield, and how much of the N2 premium does Apple absorb versus pass through in the $1,199 iPhone 18 Pro price?

rows.finding: Apple's C2 modem ships in the iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo with US mmWave bands and 15% lower energy use than the C1X, but the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max appears to keep a Qualcomm modem.
rows.mechanism: In-house modem design removes a $10-20 class royalty and a supplier's margin from the bill of materials and improves cellular-to-OS integration, but a partial roll-out leaves Qualcomm with leverage over the highest-ASP SKU and over certification risk.
rows.benchmark: Qualcomm remains the modem in the iPhone 18 Pro Max; the C1 debuted in the low-cost iPhone 16e, so the substitution has taken two generations to reach flagship tier.
rows.weakens: The split may reflect mmWave certification, supply or performance risk rather than a deliberate strategy, which would mean the technical gap is not yet closed.
rows.implication: Modem integration is a slow but real margin lever; it supports the hardware gross-margin case only if the Pro Max moves to C2 in the 2027 cycle.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: Does Apple's FY2026 10-K disclose Qualcomm as a single-source supplier, and what share of iPhone units still carry a Qualcomm modem?

rows.finding: Apple's own foundation models are a ~3B-parameter on-device model (KV-cache sharing, 2-bit quantisation-aware training) and a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts server model on Private Cloud Compute with a 32K-token context; on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google announced that the next generation of Apple Foundation Models will be based on Google's Gemini models and cloud technology.
rows.mechanism: On-device inference is bounded by memory bandwidth and power, which caps practical model size at single-digit billions of parameters; Apple therefore offloads hard queries to PCC and, from 2026, to Gemini-derived models. Renting the frontier layer cuts training capex but turns model quality into a purchased input with a per-query cost and a supplier who is also a competitor in search and assistants.
rows.benchmark: A 32K-token context against frontier cloud assistants that handle far longer contexts; a ~3B on-device model against server models reported at roughly 8x its size.
rows.weakens: Apple's joint statement says Apple Intelligence continues to run on Apple devices and Private Cloud Compute, while trade press reports that Google's cloud performs Gemini inference — the boundary is undisclosed, and with it the true cost and privacy position.
rows.implication: The AI layer is a rented input, not a moat; the investment case must rest on distribution, silicon and privacy orchestration, and on whether Apple can charge for AI through iCloud+ without ceding margin to Google.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Where does Gemini inference physically run, what does Apple pay per query, and does the Google agreement give Apple rights to fine-tune or distil Gemini for on-device use?

rows.finding: The iPhone 18 Pro ($1,199), iPhone 18 Pro Max ($1,299) and the first foldable iPhone Duo ($1,999, on sale 2026-10-23) extend the range upward; iPhone net sales rose 22% to $196.5bn in the nine months to 2026-06-27 and Greater China rose 30% to $64.8bn.
rows.mechanism: A foldable at $1,999 tests whether Apple can still create a new hardware price tier; the China rebound shows the installed base still converts when the product cycle is strong, which funds services and buybacks.
rows.benchmark: Vision Pro's $3,499 launch produced about 390,000 units in its first year and about 45,000 in Q4 2025 — the base rate for a new Apple category at a super-premium price.
rows.weakens: The Duo arrives roughly seven years after Samsung's first foldable, so Apple is following, not leading; and the 22% iPhone growth is against a weak prior year and helped by tariff refunds and currency.
rows.implication: The product cycle supports FY2027 revenue but does not prove AI differentiation; treat the foldable as an ASP lever with unproven volume.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: What first-weekend Duo orders and return rates look like, and whether the $1,999 price holds without carrier subsidy.

rows.finding: Apple's health stack is a sequence of FDA-cleared features rather than one device: Hypertension Notification Feature (K250507, cleared 2025-09-11), Sleep Apnea Notification Feature (K240929, 2024-09-13), Hearing Aid Feature De Novo (DEN230081, 2024-09-12) and a Medical Imaging Calibration Feature (K253582, 2026-04-01), on top of ECG (2020) and atrial fibrillation history (2022).
rows.mechanism: Each clearance requires its own clinical validation and quality system, so a competitor must replicate the evidence file feature by feature; that turns sensor hardware into a regulated, slow-moving moat and creates a credible path to reimbursed health services.
rows.benchmark: Twelve FDA device records naming Apple as applicant since 2020, six of them in the last 24 months; no competitor in the retrieved records matches that cadence in consumer wearables.
rows.weakens: These are notification and screening features, not diagnoses; none carries Medicare reimbursement in the retrieved records, and the Medical Imaging Calibration clearance's commercial use is not disclosed.
rows.implication: Health is the most defensible part of the product portfolio and the most plausible route to a paid health subscription; it deserves a separate valuation line from hardware.
rows.confidence: high
rows.follow_up: Which of these features are cleared in China and the EU, and does Apple have a reimbursement or insurer partnership for hypertension notifications?

rows.finding: Apple does not disclose a patent count; the FY2025 10-K states only that it is 'pursuing thousands of applications around the world' and holds a broad portfolio of patents, designs, copyrights and trade secrets, and that no single right protects its products.
rows.mechanism: A diffuse portfolio with no blocking single right supports freedom to operate but gives little measurable exclusion power in AI, where training data and model weights rather than patents decide capability; the enforceable assets are design, silicon know-how and trade secrets.
rows.benchmark: Peer comparison on patent counts could not be completed: USPTO Patent Center and EPO Espacenet were not searchable in this run, so a quantitative portfolio comparison is missing.
rows.weakens: Without counts, grants and citation data, any claim that Apple's patent moat is strong or weak is unquantified; the 10-K's 'thousands' language is the only primary datum.
rows.implication: Do not underwrite a patent-based moat; underwrite manufacturing know-how, regulatory clearances and installed base, and request a patent-landscape export before relying on IP as a differentiator.
rows.confidence: medium
rows.follow_up: Can a USPTO Patent Center and Espacenet export for Apple's 2024-2026 AI, health-sensing, foldable and AR filings be obtained to test grant rates and citation depth?

plan.decision_question: Is Apple's silicon-plus-OS integration still a durable technical advantage in the AI era, or is Apple becoming a fast-follower that licenses others' frontier models?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack is still the widest integrated consumer technology stack in the industry, but in 2026 the company formally rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — so what remains defensible is distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing, not AI leadership.
plan.why_different: This section judges the technology itself: what is proven, at what performance, under what dependency, and how long a funded competitor would need — not the market size, the unit economics or the valuation, which belong to other sections.
plan.mechanism: Owning the SoC, modem, wireless chip and OS lets Apple put a ~3B-parameter model on more than two billion devices at near-zero marginal cost and keep orchestration and privacy; licensing Gemini removes the frontier-training cost but converts model capability into a per-query input cost and a Google dependency, so value shifts from model ownership to distribution and to regulated features that competitors cannot copy without their own trials and FDA clearances.
plan.comparison_set: Apple's own prior generation (A19 Pro on TSMC N3P, 2025) and 3nm wafer economics; Qualcomm as the incumbent modem supplier still in the iPhone 18 Pro Max; Samsung and Huawei as foldable and on-device-AI incumbents; Google as the model supplier and would-be competitor; Vision Pro against the scale needed for a platform (sub-1% of revenue).
plan.counter_evidence: Siri's multi-year delivery failure forced Apple to license Gemini (2026-01-12) on reported ~$1bn a year; on-device models are ~3B parameters with a 32K context, far below frontier cloud models; Vision Pro shipped only ~45,000 units in Q4 2025; the C2 modem still does not cover the largest Pro Max SKU; and Apple publishes no patent count, so the IP moat cannot be quantified from primary sources.
plan.visual: Technology comparison table plus product inventory and patent/IP table; the FDA clearance table carries the health-moat argument.
plan.prohibited: huge market, strong team, high barriers to entry, clear business model, fierce competition, risks are manageable, well positioned, world-class, best-in-class, about 5, many patents, recently, industry-leading (as an assertion)

rows.finding: Apple received 2,722 US patent grants in 2025, down 11.6% from 3,082 in 2024 and sixth overall; Samsung took 7,054 grants for a fourth consecutive year, Huawei 3,052 (fourth), TSMC 4,194 (second).
rows.mechanism: Grant volume is a proxy for bargaining power in cross-licences and for breadth of the estate; Apple's absolute count is large but 2.6x smaller than Samsung's in the most recent year.
rows.benchmark: Samsung 7,054; Huawei 3,052; US total 323,272 grants in 2025.
rows.weakens: Grants are not families, measure no technology area and say nothing about quality or essentiality.
rows.implication: No IP credit is added to the hardware moat until granted families in AI, health, foldable and AR are verified; the composite stays at 8/10.
rows.confidence: medium: secondary-language report of IFI Claims data, consistent with IFI's own headline.
rows.follow_up: Does the USPTO/EPO export show Apple ahead or behind Samsung and Alphabet in the four target technologies?

rows.finding: In 2025 AI filings, Samsung applied for 2,162 patents worldwide, Huawei 1,822 and Google 1,672; Apple is absent from the top three, and US filings were Samsung 682, Google 671, Microsoft 585.
rows.mechanism: AI IP is concentrating in Samsung, Huawei and Google; Apple's AI position rests on licensing and integration rather than on owned IP.
rows.benchmark: Top-three AI applicants worldwide and in the US, 2025.
rows.weakens: Filings are not grants, and many AI inventions are kept as trade secrets, so the absence understates Apple's know-how.
rows.implication: Supports a 4/10 AI barrier and undercuts any patent-premium argument in the AI narrative; price AI as a rented input, not an owned moat.
rows.confidence: high: IFI Claims release of 2026-07-28.
rows.follow_up: What is Apple's own 2025 AI filing count, and how many of those are granted?

rows.finding: Intel bought Infineon's wireless solutions business for about $1.4bn, closing in Q1 2011, and sold its smartphone modem business to Apple for $1bn, completed 2019-12-02: roughly nine years without a durable phone-modem position.
rows.mechanism: Cellular modem design is cumulative and standards-bound; entry by acquisition of an established team still takes most of a decade to reach a durable position.
rows.benchmark: Nine-year Intel interval (2011-2019).
rows.weakens: The unevidenced claim that 50 senior engineers could match a phone-class SoC and OS in four to five years; shows even funded entrants with acquired IP take longer.
rows.implication: Replication of the silicon-plus-OS stack is an eight-to-ten-year proposition; cap the composite at 8/10 hardware.
rows.confidence: high: two Intel primary releases.
rows.follow_up: Could an entrant shortcut with licensed modem IP from MediaTek or Unisoc plus TSMC N2 access?

rows.finding: Apple acquired about 2,200 Intel modem engineers and more than 17,000 wireless patents in December 2019; the first in-house modem, the C1 in the iPhone 16e, shipped in February 2025, just over five years later, and the largest iPhone in 2026 appears to retain a Qualcomm modem.
rows.mechanism: Acquired IP and staff shortened the path to a first modem but not to flagship parity; the highest-ASP SKU still carries the supplier's part.
rows.benchmark: 5 years 2 months from closing to first in-house modem; Qualcomm still in the Pro Max in 2026.
rows.weakens: Any claim that the C2 closes Qualcomm dependence; leverage persists at the top of the range.
rows.implication: Qualcomm cost and royalty leverage survives into FY2027; watch the 2027 Pro Max teardown as the signal of full substitution.
rows.confidence: high on dates (Apple and Intel releases); medium on the Pro Max modem, which rests on teardown reporting.
rows.follow_up: Does the 2027 Pro Max move fully to the C2, and at what BOM saving?

rows.finding: Samsung designs its own Exynos chips and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 model shipped on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025, as did the Galaxy S23 in 2023; Samsung retired its Mongoose custom CPU cores in 2020 after middling efficiency results.
rows.mechanism: Vertical integration without leading-edge process yield and design parity does not close the gap; the binding constraint is process and design capability, not capital or ambition.
rows.benchmark: Samsung's multi-year Exynos programme; all-Snapdragon flagship years 2023 and 2025.
rows.weakens: A 9/10 or 10/10 score for custom silicon: even a foundry-owning OEM buys its flagship SoC.
rows.implication: Cap custom SoC and modem at 8/10 and treat hardware integration as durable but not unassailable.
rows.confidence: medium: trade-press analysis, corroborated by GSMArena specifications and Samsung's own launch materials.
rows.follow_up: Does Exynos 2600 return to the Galaxy S26 in volume in 2026, which would narrow the gap?

rows.finding: China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15 with Alibaba Qwen and Baidu supplying a separate model stack, and the Q3 FY2026 10-Q warns that DMA interoperability obligations have in the past, and may in future, cause Apple not to launch or maintain features such as Siri AI in certain jurisdictions.
rows.mechanism: Regulatory approval now determines which model stack and which features ship in each jurisdiction, fragmenting the distribution advantage the AI layer is meant to monetise.
rows.benchmark: Two of three major jurisdictions (China, EU) on separate or restricted availability versus the US.
rows.weakens: The claim that Apple can monetise one global AI experience across its installed base.
rows.implication: AI monetisation is jurisdiction-dependent; any subscription case must be modelled by region, with the EU as a possible exclusion.
rows.confidence: high on the 10-Q quote; medium on the CAC approval, which rests on secondary reporting.
rows.follow_up: Does Siri AI ship in the EU at launch, and can Apple charge for AI features the EU does not receive?

plan.decision_question: Is Apple's silicon-plus-OS integration still a durable technical advantage in the AI era, or is it becoming a fast-follower that licenses others' models?
plan.thesis_sentence: Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack is still the widest integrated consumer technology stack, but in 2026 the company rented the frontier model, so what remains defensible is distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing, not leadership in artificial intelligence.
plan.why_different: Only this section scores the technology and the IP, separating what Apple owns (silicon, OS, clinical clearances) from what it rents (the frontier model), so the rest of the report can price AI as a cost rather than a moat.
plan.mechanism: Apple converts custom silicon and OS control into product margin and switching costs; it converts clinical clearances into regulated features rivals must replicate filing by filing; it buys the frontier model, which converts a fixed R&D advantage into a per-query variable cost paid to a competitor and makes feature availability jurisdiction-specific.
plan.comparison_set: Samsung (Exynos versus Snapdragon, 2023 and 2025), Intel (Infineon 2011 to modem exit 2019), Google (owns Gemini, supplies the model), Huawei (3,052 US grants, 1,822 AI filings), Qualcomm (retains the Pro Max modem) and Apple's own 2024 AFM versus the 2026 Gemini-based stack.
plan.counter_evidence: The Gemini licence may allow on-device fine-tuning that keeps differentiation, the C2 may reach the Pro Max in 2027 and cut Qualcomm cost, and the reported ~$1bn licence is small against ~$20bn of default-search payments and $91.7bn of services revenue; if so the rented model is cheap distribution rather than a concession.
plan.visual: The moat table with difficulty scores, a peer benchmark or base rate in every high-scoring row, and a composite capped at 8/10 hardware and 4/10 AI with no IP credit; the patent table shows the family gap explicitly.
plan.prohibited: Do not claim Apple leads in AI; do not cite patent counts as families; do not assert a 4-5 year replication timeline; do not use 'strong team', 'clear business model', 'well positioned' or 'high barriers to entry'; no vague counts such as 'many patents'.
