Apple: the valuation sections (price bands, buyback authorisations, base case) are final and pass. The second review of the whole report is under way; delivery follows only if that review approves the current version.

**Apple (AAPL) — report delivered.** Rating **Watchlist**, composite **5.7/10**, data as of 2026-10-31, price basis $344.63 (NasdaqGS close, 2026-10-30).

**Final review: passed, grade A−**, no Critical or Important item open, and Watchlist sits inside the evidence gate. Both items that were Critical at the previous round closed on new evidence rather than rewording: the exit section is rebuilt on bull $399 / base $268 / bear $205 at 15/50/35, which recomputes to $265.60 probability-weighted (−23% from the close), with every band, return cell, Kelly entry and the $186 de-rating case following; and the margin chain now runs from Apple's own 2026-07-30 release, with the 47–48% September guide labelled call-stated and unverified in the release. Seven minor editorial items remain and none move the call: the forward multiple needs a label (35.2x on consensus $9.79 versus 38.9x on our $8.87), $61.8bn and $62.1bn both appear in the valuation section, the chair's "since 2000" wording and an "independent Chair" line conflict with Tim Cook as executive chair, and the competition section could name Alexa and Copilot. One report-level style flag about wording that describes how the report is made survives the final check; all fifteen section bodies read clean and the reviewer could not reproduce it, so I treat it as a rendering artefact.

**Thesis.** Apple is a top-decile franchise — more than 2.5bn active devices, Services at a 76.3% gross margin, $62.2bn of net cash and free cash flow at 1.06x net income — trading at a bottom-decile price against its own history: $5,029.6bn of market value is 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 21.0x peer median, with a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against a 4.93% ten-year Treasury. If the ~50% gross margin is near a floor the base case is $268 on margin-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $8.87 at 30.2x; unless the margin give-back Apple has already guided to stops around 46–47% and the search payment survives its one-year renewal, the stock is worth 20–25% less than it trades.

**Main risks.** (1) Margin: 2.0 points of the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin were tariff refunds, and two points of give-back is 6.3% of net income. (2) The Google search payment, reported at $20bn for 2022 (Apple does not disclose the current figure), is 22% of Services gross profit, survives only on non-exclusive one-year terms with appeals pending, and is worth about $474bn, 9.4% of market value, at 30x. (3) China: nine-month revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn on 18.1% unit share, still behind Huawei's 22.6%, while IDC expects China shipments down about 20% in the second half of 2026. (4) The multiple sits at the 100th percentile of its five-year range with the VIX at 19.42 and technology 7.4 points behind the S&P 500 over one month. (5) AI is a cost line, not a revenue line — Gemini-based models reported at about $1bn a year, R&D up 33%, and EU features may not launch at all under the DMA. (6) Buybacks at 39.5x: $62.1bn repurchased in nine months at a 2.5% earnings yield.

**The one question:** is Apple's ~50% gross margin a new floor, or a tariff-refund and memory-timing peak that flatters trailing EPS? A two-point give-back takes EPS to $8.87 and fair value to $268; 45% takes it to $205; a hold at 48% supports $296. One point of gross margin is 3.0% of net income, double the effect of one point of revenue growth.

**Three takeaways.** (1) Watchlist with zero position at $344.63: base value $268, probability-weighted $266, a 23% negative return even though the franchise is strong. (2) Buy bands are $240–265 for a 1–2% starter and at or below $225 for a 3–4% position, capped at 4% because one regulatory event is worth 9.4% of market value. (3) The 2026-11-02 December-quarter guide decides the case: at or above 48% gross margin ex-refund the base moves toward $296, near 45% it converges on the $205 bear.

**Data we would like you to fetch (four requests, filed in the report).** (1) The PACER docket for the DOJ antitrust case in the District of New Jersey — trial date, discovery cut-offs and the scope of equitable relief sought; it dates the remedy risk to 2027 or 2029 cash flows. (2) A USPTO Patent Center or EPO Espacenet export of Apple-assigned families for 2024–2026 in on-device AI, wearable health sensing, foldable hinge and AR optics; without it the IP moat is unquantified and scores no credit. (3) The latest annual accounts of the three Irish entities from the Companies Registration Office; entity-level profit and IP ownership set the durability of the 15.6% effective tax rate. (4) The 2026-07-30 earnings-call transcript with the exact September guidance — revenue growth, gross-margin range and the tariff-refund component — because the $8.87/$268 base rests on a guide the press release does not contain.

**Further diligence.** The December guide for margin ex-refund; the terms of the first renewal of the search payment and the D.C. Circuit argument from 2026-12-09; the annual report's refund and inventory split (inventory is up 87% against 16.2% revenue growth); China revenue against its nine-month base; Services growth after the US link-out injunction and the EU Article 6(4) file; carrier-subsidy depth, which the 10-K does not quantify (one point of wholesale terms is $2.5bn of revenue); and the device replacement rate.

Delivered as HTML and PDF with the full source appendix; the report is for research only and is not investment advice.

1.name: Completeness sweep
1.notes: Version 1 completeness: all 15 sections present, all required components (verdict/briefing/efficiency/one-question/takeaways; evidence; quad; info; risk-matrix; scenarios/analogs; sensitivity) present, all required tables present. Character counts 6,368 (executive_summary) and 7,351-8,990 for sections 1-14 (floor 2,500, cap 9,000), so no section is short and none throttled. Lens checklist mostly met: entity table maps 19 subsidiaries and states that EX-21 gives no ownership percentages or functions (disclosed, not papered over); timeline dated to YYYY-MM-DD; one share class with free float 99.94%, insider ownership 0.06%, Levinson's dual role and 9.0% opposition vote; TAM bottom-up and top-down reconciled within 5%; market bifurcated by region incl. India inside Europe; unit economics per revenue dollar with CAC/LTV explicitly 'not computable' and why; valuation by reverse DCF, sum of the parts, multiples, historical percentile and entry-price return table. Gaps: no per-device monetisation metric for the 2.5bn base; no earnings-surprise table; patent estate unquantified (owner recorded, check flags granularity, licence export outstanding); barrier scores 9/8/10 and the replication claim carry no benchmark or analog; the exit section's band and base value contradict four other sections, which is the report's most serious defect. Check reading: rule findings empty; the one depth finding is technology_product granularity, which does not by itself change the rating because the composite credits installed base, share, services margin and ROA rather than patents - but it must be closed by the stated limitation or by the export.

2.name: Claim verification
2.notes: Source audit of the decisive claims. Primary and adequate: balance sheet, income statement, segment revenue, product gross margin, purchase obligations, tax note (S5, S6); Q3 FY2026 8-K and revenue outlook (S13); proxy ownership, say-on-pay, board (S65, S153); FDA clearances with numbers and dates (S29-S34); IDC unit and value data (S66, S102-S106); market close and market data (S9-S12, S123-S126, S163); CRS legal sidebar on the Google remedies (S118); EC and General Court records (S7, S84, S85). Trade press labelled or self-evidently trade: N2 wafer price and A20 Pro specs (S64), Vision Pro units (S87), India assembly (S89, S91), Jefferies target (S197, S201). Low confidence and load-bearing: S86 (Gemini licence, Siri replacement), S107 (iCloud+ gating), S194 (the 47-48% guide), S199 (cited for margin arithmetic it does not contain). S165, the legal-news tracker asserting a payment ban in force, is cited nowhere in version 1 - retired, correct. S163 drawdown history and S155/S156/S157 multiples are independent and dated 2026-10-30/31. N3 labelling: the ~$1bn licence, the $20bn payment, the 2.5bn installed base and the 2-point refund are all labelled company-reported, trade-reported or unverified; the claim that Apple put the installed base at 2.5bn is supported by S191 on 2026-01-29 and is correctly labelled company-reported through an independent restatement.

3.name: Missing competitors
3.notes: Competitors considered and disposition. Covered well: Samsung (with the memory-supply mechanism, the strongest passage in the report), Huawei and HarmonyOS in China, Lenovo, Xiaomi/OPPO/vivo, Google Play as the services competitor, Netflix/Spotify/Epic as app-store challengers, Qualcomm as modem dependency, TSMC as single-source silicon. Considered and reasonably excluded: Sony (image sensors), BOE (displays), Foxconn/Tata (assembly, no product share), Nothing and Motorola (no premium share), Microsoft Surface (no share). Not covered and material: Meta (smart glasses as the next form factor), OpenAI (hardware and assistant), open-weight model providers as commoditisers of the layer Apple rents, Transsion and Honor (top-five shippers absent from the regional tables), Amazon/Alexa and Microsoft Copilot as assistant substitutes. Samsung Electronics' 12.5x multiple is correctly kept out of the peer median rather than cherry-picked in, which errs against the target.

4.name: Product/market fit
4.notes: Product/market-fit questions put to the report. (1) Hardest thing about selling it: not the product but the replacement decision - 60% of sales flow through carriers who fund the subsidy, and the report does not measure promotion depth. (2) Budget owner: the consumer, financed by the carrier in the US, cash or instalment in India and China; the government subsidy that supported China demand was withdrawn in Q2 2026, which the market section handles well. (3) Sales cycle: effectively none at retail, but the carrier contract cycle and the annual search-payment renewal are the real cycles; the latter is dated (first one-year renewal, appeal argument from 2026-12-09). (4) Why adoption is not faster: price and memory-driven entry-tier collapse; the report's answer - premiumisation inside a shrinking unit pool - is coherent, and the 16.7% unit decline against 16.2% revenue growth is the evidence. (5) Lost deals: handled for China (Huawei and HarmonyOS, first-time buyers in lower-tier cities never entering iOS) but not for the US, where the lost sale is a buyer keeping a four-year-old iPhone or moving to a discounted Android flagship; the lengthening replacement cycle is asserted by IDC and not quantified for Apple. Unanswered and material: services attach per device (see pass 1), the AI price, and the Duo's willingness to pay.

5.name: Number stress-test
5.notes: Stress arithmetic, each key number 30% worse against the $344.63 close of 2026-10-30. FY2027 EPS $8.87 less 30% is $6.21, or $188 at 30.2x (-45%) and $130 at 21x (-62%); base value $268 less 30% is $188; expected value $275 less 30% is $193. Multiple stress alone: the bottom of the five-year range, 22.1x, on $8.87 is $196. Combined: 21x on $8.20 is $172, against a $225 full-position entry (-24%). Search payment cut 30%: $6bn of revenue, $4.7bn after tax, $0.32 a share, $9.7 at 30x, 2.8% of the price - the report's $8.0 probability-weighted figure is consistent. Revenue 30% lower: $4.92 of EPS, $123 at 25x, matching the risk section. Gross margin: the base $268 needs 46-47% ex-refund to hold; the guide implies 46-47% including 1 point of refund, so a one-point miss on the ex-refund margin moves the base by roughly $25 and a two-point miss by roughly $50, which is the difference between the $240-265 starter band paying and not. Direction survives every stress because the price sits above every fair value computed; the entry bands and the stated 9% maximum loss do not. Cross-checks that reconcile: market cap $5,029.6bn = 14,594.18M x $344.63; P/E 39.5x = 344.63 / 8.72; forward 35.2x = 344.63 / 9.79; two points on $490bn = $9.8bn, and $9.8bn x 0.83 / $128.93bn = 6.3% of net income; $20bn x 0.79 x 30 = $474bn = 9.4% of market value; the reverse DCF at 11.8% growth reproduces the $345 price; exit returns from $344.63 on $12.33 of FY2029 EPS and $3.37 of dividends give -3.3%, +2.7% and +8.1% at 25x/30x/35x exits. The 2026-11-02 release falls three days after the data cut and remains the correct decisive test; the FY2026 10-K will settle the refund and inventory split.

items.issue: The load-bearing number of the whole report - Apple's 47-48% September gross-margin guide, 46-47% ex-refund - is tagged in thesis and executive summary to S199 (a 9to5Mac article that only announces the 2026-11-02 earnings date) and S201 (an AppleInsider article on Jefferies' $263.66 target); in risk it rests on S194, a medium-confidence trade preview. The $8.87 EPS and $268 base value are the team's own arithmetic on that guide but appear with a target-article tag. No section cites Apple's own 2026-07-30 8-K/press release (S13) for the range, although S13 is in the register and is used for the same quarter's revenue.
items.action: Cite Apple's Q3 FY2026 8-K/press release (S13, 2026-07-30) for the 47-48% range and the 1 point of refunds; write $8.87 and $268 as 'calculation on S6 and S13' rather than tagging an analyst target; if the 2026-07-30 release does not carry the range, label the guide 'trade-reported, unverified' as company claims must be, and state the confidence effect on the Watchlist rating.
items.evidence_request: What gross-margin range, tariff-refund point and revenue outlook does Apple's 2026-07-30 earnings release state for the September quarter? Cite the release, not a preview of it.

items.issue: Two different dates for the same $100bn repurchase authorisation: company_overview says it was 'announced on 2025-05-01', funding_valuation and exit say 'authorised April 2026' (S164, dated 2026-04-30). A reader cannot tell which capital-return fact is true, and the buyback pace is a scored input.
items.action: Settle on the April 2026 authorisation (S164, dated 2026-04-30) with the increase to the programme and the dividend; correct the 2025-05-01 reference in the entity section and reconcile the quarter in which the $25.8bn was repurchased against the total.
items.evidence_request: Which authorisation is current: the amount, the board date and the filing that records it? Check the 2026-04-30 8-K or press release rather than a secondary report.

items.issue: The Gemini licence cost of ~$1bn a year and the iCloud+ AI gating are carried by S86 (low confidence, a technical blog) and S107 (low confidence) and described as 'trade reporting' without the confidence qualifier; both are material to the cost-side argument and to the only proposed AI revenue line.
items.action: Flag S86 and S107 as low-confidence trade reporting in the tag or the sentence, so the reader sees that the ~51bn licence and the iCloud+ gating are single-source and unconfirmed by either party. The joint statement (S58) supports the licensing itself and should be the citation for that.

items.issue: The briefing card says the search payment is 'reported at $20bn a year'; the underlying figure is a 2022 court statement by Eddy Cue, not an annual run-rate, and the tag reads as current.
items.action: Write 'reported at $20bn for 2022 (S82); Apple does not disclose the current figure', as financials and exit already do.

items.issue: The report's own Nokia analog turns on a platform shift moving value to a layer the incumbent does not control, yet no section examines the next form factor or the model layer as a competitor. Missing: Meta's smart glasses, the strongest candidate to displace the phone as the assistant interface; OpenAI, now both supplier-adjacent and a would-be device maker; open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek) that would let a phone maker rent or self-host an assistant cheaply, which would weaken Apple's rented-model position further; and in unit share, Transsion and Honor, which the regional tables omit while listing Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo.
items.action: Add a short subsection with dated evidence on each: Meta's Ray-Ban display glasses (units, 2026 launches, price), OpenAI's hardware programme following the device announcement, open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek) that would let a rival self-host the assistant layer instead of licensing it, and Transsion and Honor in the unit tables. State explicitly whether the foldable Duo is a response to smart glasses or a defence of the phone, and at what price gap the threat starts to bite.
items.evidence_request: IDC or Counterpoint smart-glasses shipments and vendor share for 2025 and 2026, Meta's and OpenAI's disclosed device plans, and Transsion's and Honor's 2026 handset shares by region.

items.issue: The competitive set covers handsets, PCs, wearables and app stores but no non-device assistant: Alexa and Copilot sit in the same rooms as Siri and are the substitute for someone who does not buy the next iPhone.
items.action: Name Amazon/Alexa and Microsoft Copilot as substitutes in the home and enterprise assistant use case, with a sentence on why they have not taken the phone interface.

items.issue: The report says 60% of net sales go through carriers, resellers and distributors and that 'the carrier bears the acquisition cost', which makes the carrier's willingness to subsidise the single biggest determinant of Apple's US demand - and nothing in the report measures it. The buyer is described as a consumer with a discretionary, increasingly financed purchase, but no section says how much of the $1,199 iPhone 18 Pro the carrier absorbs, how deep 2026 promotions ran, or what a subsidy withdrawal would do to units. That is the hardest part of selling this product in its largest market, and the analysis stops at naming the channel.
items.action: Model the channel: state the share of US iPhone sales that carry a carrier promotion, the typical trade-in or instalment discount on the iPhone 18 Pro in 2026, and what a one-third cut in carrier promotion depth would do to US revenue. If the carrier subsidy is not disclosed, say so and use a documented proxy for promotion depth.
items.evidence_request: US carrier promotion depth for the iPhone 18 Pro at launch (trade-in values and instalment terms at the three national carriers, autumn 2026) and the share of US iPhone sales financed through carrier instalment plans.

items.issue: The AI subscription has no price, no tier, no launch date and no identified budget owner; the section calls it plausible and unverified, which is right, but leaves the one quantified question - who pays and how much - open.
items.action: Bound the AI revenue line: name the paying population (iCloud+ subscribers), the price band Apple already charges, and the maximum plausible revenue at 5-10% attach, so the reader can see it is not a valuation lever.

items.issue: The Duo launched at a reported $1,999 on 2026-10-23, six days before the valuation date, against IDC's $2,550 foldable average; the report never tests whether the lower price buys share or simply carries lower margin, which matters for the FY2027 mix the base case assumes.
items.action: Add one sentence on why $1,999 against a $2,550 category average is the right price and what margin the Duo needs to avoid diluting product gross margin.

items.issue: Section 12 keeps a starter band of $275-296 and a full position at or below $250, on a base of $296 built from consensus FY2027 EPS of $9.79 at 30.2x, with an 'add to full position' sell trigger at $250 and the return table also run on $9.79. Thesis, scoring, risk and the executive summary use a margin-adjusted base of $268 on $8.87, a starter of $240-265, a full position at or below $225 and a trim above $395. The risk section says in terms that 'the $275-296 entry band does not survive'. The report therefore tells the reader to buy 15-25% above the fair value it computes itself, and the band that a fund would act on depends on which section the reader opens.
items.action: Rebuild section 12 on the margin-adjusted case the rest of the report uses: base EPS $8.87 at 30.2x = $268, starter $240-265, full position at or below $225, trim above $395, and the 'add' trigger at the full-position band rather than $250. Recompute the three-year return table on $8.87 (the 25x/30x/35x exits at $344.63, $250 and $225), restate the policy-event arithmetic, and reconcile the closing 'reassess if above $296 for four quarters' time rule with the new base. If the Valuation Analyst still believes $9.79 and $296, the thesis, scoring, risk and executive summary must move to that view - one number, one band, across all five sections.
items.evidence_request: No new source needed: recompute from the September guide and trailing revenue already cited, and state the multiple and EPS behind every band.

items.issue: The section states Apple 'discloses no unit volumes, average selling price or installed-base figure' and that LTV is 'not computable', while market, thesis and scoring all use the company-reported 2.5bn active devices (S191). With the installed base named as the annuity's engine, the report has no per-device monetisation metric anywhere: services revenue per active device is computable from S6 and S191 and is not shown.
items.action: Replace the 'not computable' line with a disclosed proxy: trailing-twelve-month services revenue per active device of $48.2 ($120,500M / 2,500M) against $46.5 a year earlier ($109,158M / 2,350M), i.e. 3.7% growth per device, and state that this, not unit volume, is the monetisation engine the thesis pays for.
items.evidence_request: Does the 2026-11-02 release or the FY2026 annual report restate the active-device count, and does it disclose any services revenue per device or paid-subscription count?

items.issue: The section check still flags granularity: no patent numbers. The patent row reads 'Count not disclosed', which is honest, but the moat conclusion rests on barrier scores of 9/10 for silicon, 8/10 for hardware-OS integration and 10/10 for the installed base that carry no peer benchmark, base rate or failed-analog test, and on the assertion that 'a team of 50 senior silicon and operating-system engineers could match a phone-class SoC and OS in four to five years', which is asserted rather than evidenced.
items.action: Add to the patent row: patent families and grants unverified; the moat judgement therefore rests on silicon, integration and the FDA-cleared feature estate, and the composite barrier score is capped at 8/10 hardware, 4/10 AI with no IP credit. Either evidence the replication claim from one dated precedent (Intel's exit from phone modems after buying Infineon in 2011; Samsung's Exynos gap against Apple silicon 2020-2026) or delete the sentence.
items.evidence_request: The patent export in the outstanding request for 2024-2026 Apple-assigned families in on-device AI, wearable health sensing, foldable hinge and AR optics remains open; the section should say what a count of granted families against Samsung and Alphabet would change in the 8/10 composite.

items.issue: 'The largest installed base in the industry' is stated without a source and without qualification; Apple's 2.5bn active devices is smaller than the Android ecosystem base, so the superlative needs to be defined as single-vendor or dropped.
items.action: Qualify it as the largest single-vendor installed base in the industry, or cite a dated comparison; if no comparison exists, say the cross-vendor ranking is not established.

items.issue: The education table puts 'About 1997 (inferred from 2001 join)' in a year column; an inference with a hedge word is the kind of vague count the writing standard excludes.
items.action: Write '1997 (inferred)' with the basis, or 'not disclosed'.

items.issue: The financial section asserts Apple 'has beaten estimates through every quarter of the memory squeeze' and the thesis repeats it, but the report has no earnings-surprise history; consensus EPS, guidance and surprise history are the lens's public-equity check and only guidance (9-11% revenue, 47-48% margin) is present.
items.action: Add a four-quarter table of consensus EPS against reported EPS with report dates, sourced to the earnings releases already in the register, or soften the claim to what is documented.

items.issue: Scoring states that at the full-position entry of $225 the maximum loss to the $205 bear case is 'about 9%' and that the cap therefore contains the single regulatory event. The risk matrix in the same report assigns 50% probability to a multiple de-rating to the 21.0x peer median with -46% impact; on base EPS that is $186 and on bear EPS $172, which is 17-24% below the $225 entry. The stated maximum loss is only true if 25x is a floor, which the report itself denies.
items.action: Restate the downside as a range: at 21x, the base EPS of $8.87 is $186 and the bear EPS of $8.20 is $172, so the drawdown from a $225 entry is 17-24%, not 9%. Re-derive the position cap from that loss (a 4% position then risks 0.7-1.0% of the fund, not 0.4%), or state explicitly why 25x is a floor when the risk matrix gives a 21x de-rating 50% probability.

items.issue: Two probability sets produce two expected values for the same three cases on the same $268 base: risk uses bear 35 / base 50 / bull 15 for $266, while thesis, executive summary and scoring use 20/50/30 for $275. The risk matrix separately puts 60% probability on gross margin settling at 45%, which contradicts a 30% bear weight and would move the expected value far below both.
items.action: Adopt one weight set and one expected value across all four sections, and make the risk matrix's 60% probability on the 45% margin outcome consistent with the bear-case weight; a 60% bad outcome and a 30% bear cannot both stand.

items.issue: The multiple is described as at the '100th percentile' of a five-year range given in the same paragraph as 22.1-40.6x, while today's 39.5x is below that maximum: the percentile and the range contradict each other, and the claim is repeated in the executive summary, thesis and scoring as a core valuation argument.
items.action: State the percentile with its method (e.g. '97th percentile of daily closes since 2021') or quote the source's percentile directly beside the range, and drop '100th' where the range's own maximum exceeds today's multiple. The same sentence appears in four sections and should change in all of them.

items.issue: The financial section says one point of gross margin is $4,668M of pretax profit, or 3.0% of net income, and one point of revenue growth at the current margin is $1,878M, or 1.5%. A point of revenue on $466.8bn is $4,668M, which at a 48.7% margin is $2,273M of gross profit, not $1,878M; the margin figure is stated post-tax and the revenue figure pre-tax, so the comparison that drives the thesis is not on one basis.
items.action: Restate both sensitivities on one basis (post-tax, at a stated incremental margin) so the ratio is checkable, and note that margin matters twice as much as revenue growth only if the incremental margin on added revenue is below 50%.

items.issue: The Kelly illustration is run at $250 with a stated +10% upside to a $268 base, but $250 to $268 is 7.2%; the illustration also sits above the $225 full-position band it is meant to justify.
items.action: Run the sizing illustration at the stated full-position band ($225) or mark it explicitly as a what-if above the band.

1.name: Completeness sweep
1.notes: All fourteen checked sections are between 8,085 and 8,986 characters, inside the 2,500-9,000 window, with the required components: verdict/briefing/efficiency/one-question/takeaways (executive_summary), kpi+timeline (company_overview), evidence (team, technology_product, market, competition, business_model, strategy), quad (competition), info (financials; risk carries info plus risk-matrix), scenarios+analogs (thesis), sensitivity+takeaways (scoring), three risk-matrix blocks (esg). Every section check passes; the version check records no rule findings (N1-N4, N6 clean) and one report-level language note. Each section carries a judgement thesis sentence, peer or base-rate comparison, counter-evidence and stated confidence: exit opens on "the market, not a buyer"; competition on the crisis-specific share gain; technology_product on the rented frontier model. Depth floor met in every section on inspection (figures, distinct source IDs and tables well above 8/4). The two R1 Critical items are structurally resolved, not reworded: section 12 is rebuilt end to end on the margin-adjusted case, and the margin chain now runs from Apple's own 2026-07-30 release. Round-2 restraint: no new Important item was added; the open items below are language and labelling polish that do not hide a decision-relevant gap.

2.name: Claim verification
2.notes: R1 Critical 2 closed on new evidence: thesis, executive_summary, risk and exit cite S13 (2026-07-30 release) for the 50.1% June margin, the 2.0 points of refunds and the $0.11 of $2.02; the 47-48% September guide is labelled company guidance stated on the call, unverified in the release, with S202 behind it; $8.87 and $268 are written as 'the team's calculation on S6 and S13' and the confidence effect is stated (high in arithmetic, medium in the margin path, rating does not rest on the precise range). N3 labels checked across sections: 2.5bn installed base 'company-reported, not audited' (business_model, market); $20bn search payment '2022 court figure Apple has never confirmed' and 'Apple does not disclose the current figure' (risk, business_model, market, exit, executive_summary); ~$1bn Gemini licence 'reported, neither Apple-confirmed' (technology_product, strategy); iCloud+ gating 'reported only, no tier and no price' (strategy); ESG supply-chain claims 'company-prepared and unverified here' and the carbon-neutral gap stated. No stale source: S165's payment-ban assertion, flagged in the red-team review, appears in no section; the D.D.C. status is the 2025-09-02 remedies decision with appeals pending, dated to 2026-10-29 consistently in exit, risk, thesis and esg. Attacked-source independence: the load-bearing margin claim now rests on a primary filing plus a labelled secondary transcript; the load-bearing valuation inputs ($9.79 consensus, 30.2x five-year average, 21.0x peer median) rest on S158, S154 and S124-S126. No unattributed material figure found in any paragraph, list item or table row in the sections read.

3.name: Missing competitors
3.notes: R1 Important closed with new evidence in competition rev 10: IDC 2.25m display-less units in Q1 2026 (+167%), 13.6m units and $5.1bn for 2026, 27.3m by 2030, Meta at 68.7% of Q2 2026 units, Ray-Ban Display at $799 in five markets from 2026-09-23 (S212, S214, S216); OpenAI's screenless speaker reported 2026-07-14 (S213); open-weight cost per million tokens from S217; Transsion and Honor in the competitor table with S102 and S215. Geographic blind spots checked: China (Huawei 22.6%, Apple 18.1%, S40), India inside the Europe segment (S105), Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific in market's regional table. Adjacent giants: Samsung as memory supplier and handset rival, Huawei as domestic OS plus silicon, Lenovo in PCs, Alphabet twice (Google Play and the model licence). Substitutes: web payments and alternative marketplaces in the Services row; missing only Alexa and Copilot. Academic spin-outs and open source are covered through the open-weight model discussion. The Duo is explicitly assessed as a phone defence rather than a glasses response, with the trigger stated (a cellular-independent display pair at or below the iPhone ASP, closing the $218 gap; glasses at 10% of phone units).

4.name: Product/market fit
4.notes: Product/market-fit questions put to the section owners, and how the report answers them as written. Hardest thing about selling: no longer discovery but price - a 1.0bn-unit market down 16.7% in units while ASP rises 27.6% to a record $581, so Apple must sell a $1,199-$1,999 portfolio into a contracting unit pool and defend a 30% commission that courts are dismantling; answered in market, competition and business_model. Budget owner: the consumer, intermediated by carriers, resellers and distributors (60% of FY2025 net sales, $249,697M of $416,161M), with the carrier able to withdraw subsidies at any time and 27% of trade receivables ($8,477M of $31,398M) sitting with them; answered. Sales cycle: consumer replacement cycle, with the finance decision delegated to the carrier; the carrier subsidy per device, the wholesale discount and the reseller-support spend are stated as undisclosed, and one point of wholesale terms is valued at $2.5bn, 1.3% of FY2025 gross profit; answered as a stated limitation, which closes the R1 Important. Why adoption is not faster: memory at more than 65% of low-end BOM, sub-$100 tier down about 60%, the sub-$200 entry tier priced out, Chinese buyers postponing rather than abandoning, and the AI feature arriving as a retention feature with no price; answered. Where the case would break in the market: if the June China growth was pull-forward ahead of second-half price rises, and if the entry tier rebuilds after 2028 when memory normalises; both stated. The residual gap is lost deals and churn, which is what the Minor item asks for.

5.name: Number stress-test
5.notes: Stress-test arithmetic, recomputed from the report's own inputs. Case weights are now 15/50/35 in thesis, exit, risk, scoring and the executive summary: 0.15 x $399 + 0.50 x $268 + 0.35 x $205 = $59.85 + $134.00 + $71.75 = $265.60, reported as $266, -23.0% from $344.63, and $268 is -22.2%. Multiples: 399/10.50 = 38.0x, 268/8.87 = 30.2x, 205/8.20 = 25.0x. Return table, recomputed at 8% EPS growth to $11.17 by FY2029 plus $3.37 of dividends: at $344.63, 25x gives -6.4% a year, 30x -0.6%, 35x +4.6%; at $265, +2.2%, +8.5%, +14.2%; at $240, +5.6%, +12.2%, +18.0%; at $225, +7.9%, +14.6%, +20.6%. The 8% hurdle needs 38.6x at today's price and 25.1x at $225; both check out. Bands: $240-265 is 27.1-29.9x, $225 is 25.4x and 10% above the $205 bear, $395 is 44.5x base and 37.6x bull. Downside at the full-position entry: 21x on $8.87 = $186, which is -17.3% from $225, -22.5% from the $240 floor and -29.8% from the $265 top; scoring's 17% and 30% and risk's 17%/22%/30% agree, closing R1's 9% item. Kelly arithmetic: at $250 the cases are +59.6%, +7.2% and -18.0%, expected +6.2%; at $225 expected +18.0%, matching scoring. Margin chain: 2 points on $490bn = $9.8bn pretax, 6.3% of trailing net income of $128,930M, EPS $8.87; one point of gross margin on TTM revenue = $4,668M, 3.0% of net income after tax, against 1.5% for one point of revenue growth - the 3:2 ratio used in the executive briefing and financials is right. Other figures spot-checked and correct: revenue per device $466,823M/2.5bn = $187; services 39.1% of nine-month gross profit ($69,963M of $178,782M); nine-month segment sum $364.4bn; Greater China $14.9bn of increase = 4.1 points of 16.2% growth; search payment 16.6-17% of $120.5bn services revenue and 22% of $91.6bn gross profit, $32 a share and 9.4% of market value; 30%/50% cut plus 10% total loss = $8.0 a share; repayment arithmetic on the peer table and the reverse DCF ladder ($221/$255/$298/$345) is internally consistent. Thesis survives 30% worse on every axis tested in the report: revenue -30% gives $4.92 of EPS ($123 at 25x), FCF -30% gives $156 a share, a 21x peer-median de-rate gives $186 - all below the $225 full-position entry, which is why the rating is Watchlist and the entry bands are conditional on 2026-11-02. What the numbers do not settle, and what the report says it cannot settle: the patent-family count behind the 8/10 hardware barrier, the current search payment, the refund-versus-mix split and the measured replacement cycle. The buy band tops out $3 below the base value ($265 against $268), so a starter is bought at full base value and the band rests on the December guide; risk and scoring state the consequence (30% markdown to the 21x case) without changing the band, which I accept at Minor rather than Important because the loss is disclosed at the point of purchase.

items.issue: The report-level check still records 'writes about how the report is made ("section check")'. I read all fifteen section bodies in version 2 and cannot reproduce any sentence describing the report's own checks or production; no rule finding is attached to it, and it hides no decision-relevant gap, so it is not treated as blocking.
items.action: Run one final search of the assembled text for 'check', 'section check' and 'this report' and delete any sentence that describes how the report is made; if the search returns nothing in the section bodies, record it at handover as a checker artefact rather than editing text to defeat a false positive.

items.issue: The September guide is now properly labelled (call-stated, unverified in the 2026-07-30 release, S202) and $8.87/$268 are labelled the team's calculation on S6 and S13, which closes the R1 Critical. One citation detail remains loose: S202 is a transcript dated 2026-08-07 while the text consistently places the statement on the 2026-07-30 call, and Apple's 2026-07-30 release (S13) is cited only for the June facts.
items.action: Correct the citation date to the date the call was held, or state why the transcript is dated a week after the call; if S202 is a transcript of a different event, requote the guide from the 2026-07-30 call. No change to the numbers.

items.issue: R1's Minor item on non-device assistants is still open: the new form-factor subsection covers Meta's Ray-Ban Display at $799, OpenAI's screenless speaker, open-weight models at $0.82-0.87 per million tokens and Transsion and Honor, but Alexa and Copilot as substitutes for a buyer who does not buy the next iPhone are still unnamed. Separately the subsection attributes '68.7% of Q2 2026 units' to Meta while the preceding clause counts Q1 2026 display-less units, so the period of the share figure is ambiguous.
items.action: Add one sentence naming Amazon/Alexa and Microsoft Copilot as the non-device substitutes in the home and enterprise assistant use case, with why neither has taken the phone interface, or state explicitly that the report scopes them out. Also date the 68.7% Meta share to Q2 2026 in the subsection body as the quad does, since the text attaches it to a Q1 2026 units sentence.

items.issue: The section set answers the budget-owner and channel questions well (consumer as budget owner, 60% intermediated, carrier financing transferable at will, 27% of receivables) and explains why adoption is not faster (units -16.7%, lengthening replacement cycles, China postponement, memory-constrained supply). It does not address lost deals or churn: no switching data between iOS and Android, no enterprise or education displacement evidence, and no developer-attrition read after the US link-out injunction, although Services is the rated profit pool.

# Apple Inc.: Investment research report
Rating: Watchlist
Composite score: 5.7
Data as of: 2026-10-31

## Executive Briefing

Apple closed at $344.63 on 2026-10-30, a $5,029.6bn market capitalisation, 1.2% below its all-time closing high of $348.91 on 2026-10-29 and 27.5% higher over twelve months against 10.8% for the S&P 500, with an 11.6% gain since the 2026-07-30 results against 1.2% for the index. The regime offers no cushion: the S&P 500 sits 3.4% below its 52-week high, the VIX is 19.42 at the 77th percentile, the ten-year Treasury yields 4.93%, and technology lagged SPY by 7.4 points over the past month while energy and health care led. [S9, S10, S11, S12]

The recommendation is Watchlist with no position and a composite score of 5.7 out of 10. Apple is a high-quality franchise at a price that capitalises its best margin year: on a margin-adjusted FY2027 EPS of $8.87 at the five-year average multiple of 30.2x, fair value is $268, 22% below the close, and the probability-weighted value of the three cases is $266, a 23% negative return. The fund should own it only below $265, where the base case pays and the bear case is survivable. [S13, S154]

The positives are not in dispute: the largest single-vendor installed base in the industry, a services margin near 76%, free cash flow at 1.06x net income, $62.2bn of net cash and a succession that is already complete. The risks are equally concrete: a gross margin that included 2.0 points of tariff refunds in June and a September guide of 47-48% stated on the earnings call rather than in the release, a search payment worth 22% of services gross profit that survives only on one-year non-exclusive terms, a China business that grew 30% in nine months against a forecast 20% unit decline in the second half, and a multiple at the 100th percentile of its five-year range. [S6, S118, S191, S202]

The sell side is not wrong about the franchise; it is higher than us on the earnings base and the multiple. Its average target sits below the price it covers, and its forward EPS assumes the margin recovers while the company's own call-stated September guide assumes it falls. Our difference is narrow in direction and large in consequence: we are below consensus on FY2027 EPS and on the multiple, and the gap is the whole margin of safety.

The next twelve months carry three dated tests: the fiscal fourth-quarter results and December-quarter guide on 2026-11-02, argument in the Google search-remedy appeal from 2026-12-09, and the Busan trade truce expiry on 2027-01-10. The first of these decides the case, because it is the first outlook without the carry-in inventory cushion and the first clean read on the margin ex-refund.

The entry plan follows the evidence rather than the excitement: a starter position only in the lower band, a full position only at the bear-case level, a cap because one regulatory event is worth a tenth of market value, and a trim at the top of the range. The follow-up diligence is the December guide for margin ex-refund, the terms of the first renewal of the search payment, the annual report's refund and inventory split, China revenue against its nine-month base, and Services growth after the US link-out injunction. Confidence is high in the valuation arithmetic, medium in the margin path, and low in any AI revenue forecast, which does not yet exist; the rating does not rest on the precise September range.

3. The 2026-11-02 December guide decides the case: at or above 48% gross margin ex-refund the base moves toward $296, near 45% it converges on the $205 bear [S13, S6].

## Company Overview

Apple's structure is clean in law — one share class, a majority-independent board and net cash — but not in economics: 61.8% of pretax profit is booked outside the U.S. at a 15.6% effective tax rate, insiders own 0.06%, and the same director has chaired the board since 2000, so the "alignment" in the equity story rests on pay design and on a tax structure the EU has already litigated once. The listed parent is Apple Inc., a California corporation whose common stock ($0.00001 par value) trades on Nasdaq under AAPL: 14,594,180,000 shares outstanding at 2026-07-17, down from 14,697,926,000 at 2026-01-02, and a market capitalisation of $5.03 trillion at 2026-10-30. Votes track economics one-for-one, and the free float is 99.94% because all directors and officers together hold 9,079,765 shares [S5, S6, S65, S172].

### Three Irish companies sit between the product and the profit

EX-21 lists 19 subsidiaries domiciled in 15 jurisdictions and omits the rest as not significant; it gives neither ownership percentages nor functions, so what follows is a map of domicile, not of economic activity. The two entities the European Commission found held Apple's intellectual property for sales outside the Americas — Apple Sales International and Apple Operations Europe — no longer appear on the list; in their place are three Irish companies. Apple does not describe the 2015 restructuring or name the entity that now owns the non-U.S. IP, but the tax note shows the consequence: foreign pretax earnings of $82.0bn of $132.7bn in FY2025 and a 15.6% effective rate against 21%. The 5.4-point gap is worth $7.2bn a year in cash tax, and it is exactly what the Commission attacked: the 2016 decision ordered recovery of up to €13bn, the General Court annulled it on 2020-07-15, the Court of Justice reinstated it on 2024-09-10, and Apple took a $10.2bn net charge in Q4 FY2024, paying $15.8bn to Ireland through escrow against a $4.8bn U.S. foreign tax credit [S5, S187]. Ireland closed the opinions in January 2015, so the scheme itself is gone, but the precedent is not. Entity accounts filed with Ireland's Companies Registration Office, which the 10-K does not reproduce, would show where profit now sits.

### Capital return, not leverage, is the capital-structure question

Apple carries $62.2bn of net cash — $146.5bn of cash and securities against $84.3bn of debt at 2026-06-27 — and in the nine months to that date repurchased 215m shares for $61.8bn, against $70.6bn a year earlier, under successive $100bn authorisations approved on 2025-05-01 and 2026-04-30, the latest announced with Q2 FY2026 results [S6, S204, S205]. At a $5tn capitalisation each $10bn of repurchase retires 0.2% of the company, so the return depends on the price paid. A 12% year-on-year slowdown in dollars while the shares rose 25.7% is consistent with price discipline, or with lower free cash flow; the filings do not distinguish. Solvency is not the risk; executing the market's largest buyback at a multiple that assumes the AI transition works is.

### Ownership is institutional, and the board is long-tenured

Vanguard holds 9.63% and BlackRock 7.10%, but the BlackRock figure is taken from a 2023-12-31 filing quoted in the 2026 proxy and is stale [S65, S153]. Directors and officers hold 0.06%; Tim Cook's 3,280,295 shares are worth $1.13bn at the current price yet are 0.02% of the company. The board has nine members after Ternus joined on 2026-09-01, seven of them independent; Arthur Levinson, a director since 2000 and chair for 15 years, became lead independent director that day. At the 2026-02-24 annual meeting Levinson drew 9.0% opposition, say-on-pay 8.6% and a "China Entanglement Audit" proposal 1.4% support. That passes Nasdaq's majority-independent rule and is not a governance crisis, but it is a professional board, not a founder-aligned one.

### The business model is an annuity on hardware

Apple sells devices to consumers, enterprises and carriers, but the buyer that matters is the installed base: more than 2.5bn devices whose owners upgrade and pay for services. FY2025 net sales were $416.2bn (+6%), with Services gross margin of 75.4% against 46.9% for the group; in the nine months to 2026-06-27 net sales rose 16% to $364.4bn, Services 14% to $91.7bn and Greater China 30% to $64.8bn after a 4% decline in FY2025 [S5, S6]. That is the growth engine — a replacement cycle plus attach, with China swinging from drag to driver in two years. It makes the model resilient to unit stagnation but not to a remedy that breaks the Services attach: Services produced 39.1% of nine-month gross profit on 25.2% of revenue.

### The legal front is about Services margins, not fines

Three proceedings test the container. The DOJ's civil antitrust suit, filed on 2024-03-21 in the District of New Jersey, seeks equitable relief rather than damages; the Epic litigation produced a 2025-04-30 finding that Apple violated the 2021 injunction, a ban on fees for out-of-app purchases and a referral to the U.S. Attorney for possible criminal contempt; and the EU fined Apple €500m under the Digital Markets Act on 2025-04-23, which Apple appealed [S5, S7]. The fines are small against $416bn of revenue; the remedies are not, because they target the 75%-gross-margin Services line and the App Store's toll gate on 2.5bn devices. Counter-evidence is real — the DOJ must prove market definition, Apple says it has substantial defences, and no court has ordered a structural remedy — but the direction in both jurisdictions is toward alternative distribution and payment, the one outcome that would change the franchise's economics rather than its legal bill.

## Founding Team & Key Personnel

The succession is done and internal — Ternus, Srouji, Federighi and Parekh are all Apple lifers — which lowers cultural and execution risk but concentrates the AI transition in a software chief who has outsourced the frontier model to Google and a first-time CEO who has never run a P&L, so the team offers continuity rather than evidence of renewal. The board appointed John Ternus CEO effective 2026-09-01, with Tim Cook as executive chair and Arthur Levinson, chair for the previous 15 years, as lead independent director. Ternus, 50, joined Apple's product design team in 2001, became VP Hardware Engineering in 2013 and SVP in 2021; his record includes iPad, AirPods, the iPhone 17 line and the MacBook Neo, but no disclosed CEO, P&L or capital-allocation role before 2026 [S152, S177].

**The board has already executed the succession by promoting an internal hardware engineer, and the appointment was unanimous.**

The 8-K of 2026-04-20 records the board's appointment of Ternus as CEO effective 2026-09-01, Cook's move to executive chair and Levinson's to lead independent director. Ternus joined Apple in 2001 and has led hardware engineering since 2021. The doubt sits one level down: the AI organisation was rebuilt on 2025-12-01 around an external hire reporting to Federighi, and the rebuilt Siri will run on Google's Gemini models [S152, S177, S183, S186].

The division of labour is unusually clear for a company of this size. Ternus integrates and decides; Johny Srouji became chief hardware officer on 2026-04-20, adding hardware engineering to silicon and becoming the single owner of Apple's deepest technical moat; Craig Federighi owns software and, since December 2025, AI; Eddy Cue runs services and now health; Kevan Parekh funds the company; Sabih Khan runs operations; Deirdre O'Brien runs retail and people [S179, S184]. That design fits a business whose advantage is integration across silicon, software and services, but it places the two capabilities that matter most in the next cycle — silicon and AI/software — in two individuals with no disclosed deputies.

### AI leadership failed once and has been rebuilt around an outside hire and an outside model

John Giannandrea stepped down as AI chief on 2025-12-01 after the Siri delay; Amar Subramanya, formerly corporate VP of AI at Microsoft and head of engineering for Google's Gemini Assistant, joined as VP of AI reporting to Federighi, while the rest of the AI organisation was split between Khan and Cue. On 2026-01-12 Apple and Google announced a multiyear deal to power Apple's AI features, including the Siri upgrade due in 2026, with Gemini [S183, S186]. The mechanism is speed for dependency: Apple gets a competitive assistant without building a frontier model, but it hands a competitor the most valuable interface in consumer technology and caps the differentiation it can charge for. Underwrite AI as a feature that protects the hardware replacement cycle, not as a new profit pool, until Apple discloses model economics.

### Pay and turnover: equity retains, but the C-suite is new

Cook's 2025 total target compensation was $59m: a $3m base unchanged since 2016, a cash incentive at 200% of base and a $50m equity target, positioned in the 80th-90th percentile of the primary peer group; the other named executives target $1m base, 200% cash and $20m equity, and Parekh's target was $16.75m. The CEO ownership guideline is 10 times salary. The design retains executives through the transition rather than rewarding new AI outcomes: 8.6% of votes cast opposed say-on-pay at the 2026-02-24 annual meeting, a protest worth noting but not a rejection. Retention is being tested at the same time. The CFO moved from Luca Maestri to Parekh on 2025-01-01, the COO from Jeff Williams to Khan in July 2025, the general counsel from Kate Adams to Jennifer Newstead on 2026-03-01, the AI chief from Giannandrea to Subramanya on 2025-12-01 and the CEO from Cook to Ternus on 2026-09-01. Against Apple's near-static 2011-2023 executive team that is a large amount of institutional change at once; none was a resignation under pressure, and the risk is coordination while antitrust remedies and a China reset land [S65, S153, S170, S166].

### The missing capability is frontier AI at the top, not finance or operations

No board member has operating AI-lab experience — Wanda Austin ran Aerospace, Alex Gorsky ran Johnson & Johnson — and the AI leader sits at VP level, outside the executive team [S179, S173]. That is the reference check a diligence team should run: who inside Apple can credibly challenge Google's model roadmap, and what retention packages hold Srouji and Federighi, the two people whose departure would impair the franchise. Counter-evidence is genuine: internal succession worked in 2011 when Cook replaced Steve Jobs, Ternus's product record is strong, and the Gemini deal buys time. The judgement is not that the team is weak; it is that the team is unproven at exactly the task the next three years demand.

## Technology & Product

Apple's silicon-plus-OS stack is the widest integrated consumer stack, but in 2026 Apple rented the one layer it could not build — the frontier model — leaving distribution, custom silicon and regulated health sensing as the defensible assets, not leadership in artificial intelligence. In two years the A20 Pro moved to TSMC N2, the C2 reached the flagship, the first foldable shipped at $1,999, and on 2026-01-12 Apple and Google said the next Apple Foundation Models would be Gemini-based [S58, S59, S63, S64].

### The silicon lead is real, costly, and rented from TSMC

The A19 Pro used TSMC N3P; a year later the A20 Pro moved to N2 with a 32-core Neural Engine and ~52 TOPS. N2 wafers are reported at ~$30,000 against $18,000-20,000 for 3nm. Product gross margin was 39.9% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 versus 36.9%, but only with tariff refunds and mix offsetting "higher costs, including memory", and the 10-Q expects memory and node constraints to worsen [S6, S64].

### Apple Intelligence is an architecture with a rented brain

On device Apple runs a ~3B-parameter model with KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantisation-aware training; server queries go to a Parallel-Track Mixture-of-Experts model inside Private Cloud Compute, with stateless processing, no privileged access and attested images. Memory bandwidth caps on-device inference at a few billion parameters; harder queries are offloaded. Where Gemini-derived inference runs is unresolved: Apple says Apple Intelligence continues on its devices and PCC, while trade reporting puts the Gemini computation in Google's cloud at a reported ~$1bn a year; neither is Apple-confirmed. China's CAC approved Apple Intelligence on 2026-07-15, with Qwen and Baidu on a separate stack. Differentiation is orchestration, distribution and privacy, not model quality; so a fixed-R&D moat becomes a cost that scales with usage: rented intelligence pays only if it lifts upgrades or carries a subscription [S8, S58, S60, S61, S86, S120, S171].

### Products: a strong cycle, a late foldable, a spatial computer that never became a platform

The replication test is a base rate. Intel bought Infineon's wireless unit for ~$1.4bn in 2011 and sold its modem business to Apple for $1bn in 2019 — nine years without a durable phone-modem position. Apple started from that purchase, 2,200 engineers and over 17,000 wireless patents, and shipped the C1 in the iPhone 16e in February 2025, just over five years later; in 2026 the largest iPhone still appears to carry Qualcomm. Samsung designs Exynos and owns a foundry, yet every Galaxy S25 shipped on Snapdragon 8 Elite in 2025. Parity takes eight to ten years, which is why the composite is capped at 8/10 with no IP credit. A granted-family count against Samsung and Alphabet would move it: parity in on-device AI, health, hinge and AR optics would restore the withheld point (9/10); fewer than half Samsung's families in foldables and AR optics would cut those sub-scores and add freedom-to-operate cost, holding 8/10 or below. Counter-evidence: Siri needed a Google licence, the car was cancelled, Vision Pro never reached platform volumes. The 10-Q warns DMA rules may stop Apple launching features "such as Siri AI" in some jurisdictions. Diligence: does the Google deal allow on-device fine-tuning, and does the 2027 Pro Max move fully to the C2? [S6, S58, S59, S87, S206, S207, S209, S210]

**Apple's integration advantage is durable in silicon and distribution, but it no longer extends to the model layer.**

The A20 Pro's 2nm node and 32-core Neural Engine keep Apple at the leading edge, and its FDA clearances give it a regulated estate. But basing the next Apple Foundation Models on Gemini concedes that the frontier layer is bought: the reported ~$1bn licence turns a fixed R&D advantage into a variable cost paid to a competitor, and availability varies by jurisdiction, with China on a Qwen/Baidu stack and DMA rules possibly withholding Siri AI in the EU [S6, S58, S64, S86, S120, S171].

## Market & Industry Analysis

Apple's markets are contracting in units and expanding in value, and Apple is taking value share inside that contraction: the case for FY2026-FY2028 rests on premiumisation and installed-base monetisation rather than unit volume or a Services mix shift, is strongest in the United States, adequate in Europe, and in China depends on a domestic champion's pricing discipline.

### The pool is shrinking in units and growing in value

IDC's August 2026 forecast has worldwide smartphone shipments at just over 1.0 billion units in 2026, down 16.7%, while total market value rises 6.3% to $613 billion and the average selling price reaches a record $581, up 27.6% in a year. The cause is cost, not demand: DRAM and NAND prices are up more than 300% year on year, memory is more than 65% of bill of materials at the low end, and the sub-$100 tier fell close to 60% in the second quarter of 2026. This supply shock has a dated end — IDC expects memory prices to rise until at least 2028 — so 2026-2027 flatters Apple's unit share while lifting its price; 2028 tests whether either survives. [S66]

Two methods agree closely: 1.0 billion units at the $581 average price gives $581 billion, within 5% of IDC's $613 billion, so the two series are consistent. On that base Apple's serviceable market is the premium tier it addresses — an iOS share of 23.6% of 2026 shipments, a record — while the revenue it can obtain is what it already books: $466.8 billion trailing twelve months to 2026-06-27, or about $483 billion for FY2026 at the nine-month growth rate. ### Services carries the profit, but the mix moved back to hardware

The fastest-growing pool Apple monetises is Services, but its share of revenue fell in FY2026: $91.7 billion in the first nine months, 25.2% of $364.4 billion and up 14%, at a 76.3% gross margin, against a 26.2% revenue share in FY2025. Hardware grew faster than Services, so the mix shifted toward premium handsets and China rather than toward the recurring pool — the opposite of what a Services-led thesis needs. The app economy has no published size in the sources retrieved — no platform owner discloses app-store billings or mobile-advertising revenue — so Apple's Services line is the measured pool. The installed base is disclosed at more than 2.5 billion active devices on 2026-01-29, up from 2.35 billion a year earlier, but Apple publishes no replacement rate. [S5, S6, S174, S191]

### Who pays, and how much demand is policy

The budget owner is the consumer, but the transaction is intermediated: 60% of FY2025 net sales, $249,697 million of $416,161 million, went through carriers, resellers and distributors. Apple does not disclose the carrier-only share or subsidy per device, but it discloses the risk transfer: resellers offer financing, instalment plans or subsidies that "may be discontinued or modified any time", and carriers were 27% of trade receivables at 2026-06-27, $8,477 million of $31,398 million. Price protection and other customer incentives are deducted from Products net sales without an amount being given, so the channel's cost to Apple is a revenue deduction, not a disclosed expense; one point of wholesale terms across the indirect channel is $2.5 billion of revenue, 1.3% of FY2025 gross profit. The demand is policy-sensitive: US and UK interest-free financing holds the premium end while emerging markets fall more than 20%, China's government subsidy faded in Q2 2026, and India's $600-800 band grew 32% after the sub-$100 tier fell 59%. Policy also moves margin: after the 2026-02-20 Supreme Court ruling struck down certain IEEPA tariffs, refunds added 2.0 points to the June quarter's 50.1% gross margin. Carrier 10-K equipment-revenue and promotional lines, or paid channel sell-in data, would settle the missing subsidy figure; Apple's fiscal 2026 annual report was not on EDGAR at 2026-10-31. [S5, S6, S105, S40, S13]

### What would break the premiumisation case

Counter-evidence is fourfold. If memory prices normalise from 2028, the entry tier rebuilds and the 2026 share gain is contestable. If China's June-quarter demand was pulled forward ahead of second-half price increases, as IDC's China team reports, the 30% growth line is a launch and currency effect. If courts and the European Commission remove the App Store take rate, the margin layer that offsets hardware cyclicality stops compounding. And the search-distribution payment — $20 billion in 2022, 17% of trailing Services revenue of $120.5 billion and 22% of trailing Services gross profit of $91.6 billion — has not been banned: the 2025-09-02 remedies decision declined to ban distributor payments, and the December 2025 final judgment is under appeal by Google and the Department of Justice, both pending at 2026-10-29. The investor implication is narrow: in a 1-billion-unit market Apple can grow device revenue only if price rises faster than units fall, so average selling price, China durability, the carrier channel and the Services take rate matter most. Sizing confidence is high, because two independent methods agree within 5%; confidence that the mix shift holds to 2028 is medium. Three diligence questions remain open: what share of Services revenue is commission rather than subscription, advertising or licensing? How much of the Greater China increase is currency? And what is the current average replacement cycle, measured rather than asserted? [S66, S40, S82, S118, S42]

**Apple's addressable device market fell 16.7% in units in 2026 while growing 6.3% in value, and revenue grew 16.2% over nine months — the gap is premiumisation and China, not market growth, and 60% of sales run through a channel whose subsidy Apple does not disclose (S66, S13, S6, S5).**

IDC forecasts 2026 shipments at just over 1.0 billion units, $613 billion of value and a $581 ASP (S66, S102). Nine-month FY2026 revenue was $364.4 billion, up 16.2%, with Greater China up 30.0% and Services at 25.2% of revenue against 26.2% in FY2025 (S13, S6). In FY2025, 60% of net sales, $249,697 million, went through carriers, resellers and distributors, and carriers were 27% of trade receivables at 2026-06-27 (S5, S6).

## Competitive Landscape

Apple's competitive position strengthened in 2026 in every hardware line except smartwatches, but the gain is crisis-specific — bought with memory supply and price discipline, not product superiority — and it is being offset where profit is made, because the App Store commission that funds the premium position is being dismantled by courts and regulators, not by a rival's product. Samsung shipped 62.7 million handsets in Q2 2026 versus Apple's 55.7 million. [S102]

### The lead is in integration, not in units

Apple's 20.2% of global smartphone shipments in Q2 2026 was a record for that quarter and a 3.9 percentage point gain, but Samsung's 22.7% was larger and Xiaomi's 26.4% collapse explains much of the redistribution. In personal computing Apple is second at 18.2% compared with Lenovo's 20.1%, yet macOS shipments grew 17.4% while Windows fell 6.7% and Android 19.6%. The clearest lead is detachable tablets at 55.3%; the weakest is smartwatches, where Huawei leads 18.8% to 17.2%, so Apple's 15.5% of wearables rests on earwear, where it holds 17.2%. [S104]

### Samsung is the dangerous one, and the reason is memory

Samsung is the most dangerous competitor. When memory is over 65% of low-end bill of materials, supply access binds, and Samsung is the only top-five vendor that also sells memory: it grew shipments 8.1% and took 3.2 points of share in Q2 2026 while Xiaomi fell 26.4% and vivo 19.6%. Apple's answer was to secure memory early, which is why its units fell only 1.3% in 2026 against Android's 24.3% and why IDC puts iOS at a record 23.6% of shipments — a sourcing feat rather than a structural advantage, and it lapses when memory normalises while Samsung keeps its costs. Samsung also holds the foldable franchise: the iPhone Duo went on sale on 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, against a forecast of more than 17 million foldable iPhones by 2027. [S66, S59]

### In China the competitor and the rules are different

Huawei held 22.6% of a Chinese market that fell 4.3% in Q2 2026 and grew 19.9% by holding prices while Android rivals raised theirs; Apple grew 24.4% and gained 4.2 points to 18.1%. The mechanism is a domestic operating system plus price discipline, and neither is a feature Apple can copy. Apple Intelligence was registered with China's internet regulator on 2026-07-15 alongside Alibaba's Qwen and Baidu, which narrows the AI gap but does not settle it. [S40, S120]

### The profit pool is being taken by courts, not by rivals

Apple's FY2025 annual report discloses a U.S. court order preventing it from imposing any commission on certain consumer purchases, a Digital Markets Act compliance plan challenged by the European Commission, and U.S. monopolization suits over smartphones; separately, the September 2, 2025 remedies order against Google, if upheld, could remove the search-distribution payments inside Services. No competitor needs to win a device sale for the 76.3% services margin to compress: a developer that routes a subscriber to the web converts a 15-30% commission into a payment-processing fee, and Services growth of 14.1% then arrives at a lower margin. The hardware position improved while the pricing power behind it was cut by courts and regulators. [S5]

### The next form factor is glasses, and the model layer is becoming free

Smart glasses are the only consumer device growing fast enough to become a platform: IDC counted 2.25 million display-less units in Q1 2026, up 167%, and forecasts 13.6 million units and $5.1 billion for 2026, 27.3 million by 2030, with Meta at 68.7% of Q2 2026 units. At $799 for Meta Ray-Ban Display, expanded to five markets on 2026-09-23, glasses cost 38% more than the $581 average smartphone and depend on a phone; 13.6 million units are 1.3% of the 1.0 billion phones shipped. Apple's iPhone Duo, on sale 2026-10-23 at a reported $1,999, is therefore a defence of the phone, not a response to glasses: it sells at 3.4 times the industry ASP into a 22.9 million-unit foldable niche. The threat bites when a cellular-independent display pair sells at or below the iPhone's average price — closing today's $218 gap — and when glasses pass 10% of phone units; IDC's 2030 forecast reaches 2.7%. OpenAI's first device, reported on 2026-07-14 as a screenless home speaker, targets the same layer, and Apple's response is a trade-secrets suit. The model layer is commoditising faster: Qwen3-32B and Llama 4 Scout run on one H100 at about $0.82-0.87 per million tokens, DeepSeek V3.2 on eight at $13.89, so a handset maker can self-host a competent assistant for under $1 per million tokens — a tenth of a cent for a 1,000-token query. [S212, S214, S216, S213, S217]

### AI is rented, and the phone in the pocket is the strongest competitor

Where Apple is not ahead is AI: Siri AI arrived at WWDC26 in June 2026 on foundation models licensed from Google, so its assistant depends on a company it also competes with in services. The strongest competitor is the phone already in the buyer's pocket: replacement cycles are lengthening and IDC describes Chinese buyers as postponing rather than abandoning upgrades, which supports Services attach while suppressing units. Two risks offset the gain: memory normalises after 2028, and Meta holds the next interface. Unit position and profit per unit are moving in opposite directions, so the question worth paying for is not who sells more phones but what share of the transaction Apple controls in 2027. Confidence is high in the shares, medium beyond 2028. Three diligence questions remain: what proportion of Services revenue is commission? What margin does the foldable carry at its launch price? ## Business Model

Apple runs a hardware annuity with a services margin on top — 73 cents of services gross profit per dollar of product gross profit — but the mix shift the multiple pays for stalled in fiscal 2026, when hardware margins, helped by tariff refunds, grew gross profit faster than Services. In fiscal 2025, 40% of net sales went through Apple's own stores and direct sales force and 60%, or $249,697M of $416,161M, through carriers, resellers and distributors. The carrier finances or subsidises the handset, so it bears the acquisition cost and Apple's selling expense stays at $27,601M, or 6.6% of revenue; the dependency is contractual, not permanent, because Apple's risk factor says resellers offer financing, installment plans or subsidies that "may be discontinued or modified any time." The balance-sheet footprint is smaller: carriers were 27% of trade receivables at 2026-06-27, $8,477M of $31,398M, down from 34% of $39,777M at 2025-09-27 [S5, S6].

### The installed base, and what $187 a device does not say

Apple reported more than 2.5 billion active devices on 2026-01-29, against more than 2.35 billion a year earlier, and repeated the figure in its 2026-04-20 succession release; the count is company-reported, not audited. Divided into $466,823M of trailing-twelve-month revenue to 2026-06-27 it gives at most $187 of revenue per active device a year, a ceiling because the denominator is a floor. On fiscal 2025 revenue and Services the same arithmetic gives $166 and $44, so Services are about a quarter of revenue per device, and the base grew roughly 6% while nine-month revenue grew 16.2%. The metric does not capture users rather than devices, the gap between a Pro iPhone and AirPods, first-time buyers, regional pricing or services attach, and it divides a trailing year by a count four months older [S150, S191, S5, S6].

### The mix shift, and its reversal

In fiscal 2025 Services produced $109,158M of revenue at a 75.4% gross margin against $307,003M of Products at 36.8%: 26.2% of revenue but 42.2% of gross profit ($82,314M of $195,201M), up from 35.7% two years earlier, with services gross profit per dollar of product gross profit rising from $0.55 in fiscal 2023 to $0.73. Then the mechanism ran backwards. In the nine months to 2026-06-27 product gross profit rose 26.3% to $108,819M and services gross profit 15.3% to $69,963M, so Services fell to 39.1% of gross profit; product gross margin reached 39.9% against 36.9%, taking total gross margin to 49.1% and to 50.1% in the June quarter against 46.5%. Apple attributes the gain to "a different mix of products and tariff refunds, partially offset by higher costs, including memory": fiscal 2026's margin is hardware-led and partly a refund, not a trading gain. A device is gross-profit-positive on delivery at 36.8% and the services that follow are nearly all incremental, services cost of sales being $26,844M on $109,158M of revenue; the $0.73 per dollar is therefore the closest disclosed proxy for lifetime value against acquisition cost, and its fall to $0.64 the number to watch [S5, S6].

Apple publishes list prices on its own store but not in its filings, and no verified 2026 price list was retrieved; third-party unit data would settle it [S6].

### The highest-margin layer is also the most litigated

App Store economics are recognised net — Apple books "only the commission it retains" on third-party app sales — so a take-rate cut passes straight to revenue and gross profit with no offsetting cost. Apple is subject to a US court order barring a commission on certain consumer purchases, though the Ninth Circuit has told the district court to amend the injunction to permit one, and in the EU the Digital Markets Act forces alternative distribution, payment processing and fee structures. A second concentration sits in the same line: licensing revenue from Google for search distribution inside Services advertising, which Apple names as a primary driver of Services growth in fiscal 2025 and the first nine months of fiscal 2026. The payment was $20bn in 2022 per unsealed court documents, 18.3% of fiscal 2025 Services revenue, and Apple does not disclose the current figure; the District of Columbia order of 2025-09-02 preserved payments while banning exclusive agreements, but Apple says a reversal could impose remedies "prohibiting Google from offering the Company commercial terms for search distribution" [S6, S82].

### Cost structure, and what would break the durability

The cost base is bought, not built: product cost of sales of $194,116M goes to TSMC for wafers, memory suppliers for DRAM and NAND, and Foxconn and its peers for assembly. Research and development reached $34,035M in the nine months to 2026-06-27, up 33% and 9.3% of revenue against 8.3% in fiscal 2025, on "infrastructure-related costs, including investments in artificial intelligence"; capital expenditure is 2.2% of trailing-twelve-month revenue against 34.9% at Microsoft in fiscal 2026. Apple rents its manufacturing and buys much of its AI through the income statement, so that bill reaches the operating margin immediately. What remains is a disclosure gap: Apple reports the 60% indirect share, the carrier receivable and that price protection and other incentives reduce Products net sales, but not the carrier-only share of sales, the wholesale discount, the subsidy per device or the reseller-support spend inside SG&A; carrier 10-K equipment-revenue and promotional lines, or paid channel sell-in data, would settle them, and one point of wholesale terms across the indirect channel is $2.5bn of revenue, 1.3% of fiscal 2025 gross profit. For investors the durable asset is the installed base and the $44 of services revenue per device; the margin expansion of the last four quarters is not the mix shift it is described as, but product mix, a tariff refund and memory cost timing, on a services base whose most profitable parts face an appeal, a court order and a European regulatory process. Giving back three points of gross margin and losing the search licence together would take more than a fifth of trailing-twelve-month net income. Three facts would settle durability and none is disclosed — the current search payment, the App Store share of Services and the refund-versus-mix split; the fiscal 2026 annual report, not on EDGAR as of 2026-10-31, may settle them [S6, S27].

**The service mix still drives Apple's margin, but in fiscal 2026 it stopped being the marginal driver — hardware did, and part of that gain is a refund.**

In the nine months to June 2026 product gross profit grew faster than services gross profit for the first time in three years, and Apple attributes the higher product margin to product mix and tariff refunds rather than to trading gains. The installed base grew more slowly than revenue, so the next leg depends on revenue per device rather than on more devices.

## Financial Analysis

The three-year record is slowing revenue and rising margin: revenue fell 2.8% in fiscal 2023, grew 2.0% in fiscal 2024 and 6.4% to $416,161M in fiscal 2025, while gross margin rose from 44.1% to 46.9% and operating margin from 29.8% to 32.0%.
